title: The last good meal before the front
content: A warm bowl of borscht in a cold country, after a long day of work. Maybe that's what happiness is all about. I'm sitting in Trypichchia, a traditional restaurant in Kharkiv, a city about 30 km from Russian positions. And this borscht, I swear to god, might be the best I've ever had in my entire life. As a devoted enthusiast, I've eaten it in every possible setting: in fancy restaurants, at petrol stations, in village canteens, in shelters, and in trenches. I know my borscht. Mykyta, 29, one of the founders, tells us that the place started out as a local canteen at the beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion. Its sole purpose was to feed soldiers and volunteers who had stayed in the city when Russian forces were on the verge of capturing it. Since then, it has grown into a 300-sq-metre restaurant dedicated to one thing: “Serving the best food at the lowest price while rediscovering Ukrainian cuisine in a Kharkiv that has been Russified for far too long.” And you can feel it. Every recipe, Mykyta explains, is quite complex. The borscht is made with beet “kvass” (fermented beetroot juice), which gives it a lovely acidic kick and an even deeper reddish colour. title: “Young people can question those in power and demand something better”
content:
Children and young people around the world continue to speak up despite challenges because they believe their actions can make a difference. Many of them are tackling the impact of climate change head on, some are struggling to get an education, while others face dangers when they protest.

The Spark Club is a group of 11 to 18-year-old activists from around the world working with Amnesty International to make sure their voices are included, heard and listened to. They have been instrumental in shaping Amnesty’s new briefing Sparking Change - Children’s Right to Protest: A Perspective from Children and Young Activists, working alongside our researchers.

Here three young activists share more about the challenges they face in their countries and how they’re holding their governments to account.  

I first understood how powerful social protest can be as I held my mother’s hand during a demonstration when I was very little. I learned not to stay quiet facing an injustice. 

Now I study Political Science in Buenos Aires University (UBA) and I focus my activism on fighting for human rights.

title: Here, have some cancer with your smoky bacon crisps
content: The taste of smoke triggers memories of cosy firesides and tasty barbecues. Think smoked ham, smoked salmon, smoked cheese, and the less traditional smoky bacon crisps. Smoke flavourings are usually made by burning wood, capturing the smoke, and turning it into a liquid that can be added to food. But these smoky flavours may damage DNA and risk causing cancer, EU food experts said in 2023, leading to an EU ban on eight substances that came into effect in July for flavours added to sauces, soups, and snacks. And more are now set to be snuffed out: a wider ban on smoke flavourings in ham, fish, and cheese will land in 2029. The traditional method of exposing food to smoke and heat in a smokehouse oven, though it too can introduce some toxic compounds, is still allowed. The flavourings industry has tried, and failed, to fight back. Food flavourings companies Kerry Inc and Kerry Ingredients last week lost their legal fight to overturn the ban for three flavours they make. title: Global: Protesting children and young people face human rights abuses, including violence and discrimination
content:
Children and young people around the world face barriers, challenges and human rights abuses while exercising their right to protest, a new briefing from Amnesty International reveals, ahead of World Children’s Day on 20 November.

Sparking Change – Children’s Right to Protest: A Perspective from Children and Young Activists, is a briefing from Amnesty International developed in partnership with the Spark Club, a group of 11- to 17-year-olds from 12 countries across five regions. Drawing on research with more than 500 children and young people worldwide, the briefing examines why children protest, the risks they encounter, and what states and other actors must do to ensure that children can safely exercise their rights.

From the Gen-Z protests in Kenya to the Fridays for Future climate movement and recent youth-led demonstrations across Europe, young people have taken to the streets to make their voices heard. Yet many face violence, discrimination and other barriers when speaking out and putting forward their demands.

title: Whose Knowledge Gets Counted? Fourteen Years of Wikidata and African Women’s Contributions
content:
For fourteen years, Wikidata has helped organise the world’s knowledge into a structured, interconnected and freely accessible resource. From people and institutions to languages, cultural heritage and historical events, its data connects information across languages and digital platforms.

Yet, as Wikidata celebrates its 14th birthday and enters its fifteenth year, an important question remains: whose knowledge is being documented, whose contributions are visible, and who gets to participate in shaping the knowledge systems increasingly influencing how we discover and understand the world?

For African Wiki Women, this question goes beyond the absence of biographies or incomplete records. It concerns their participation in the processes through which knowledge is sourced, organised, connected and made accessible.

title: Digital Commons Policy Summit 2026: “The EU NOW has everything it needs to make open source the main Show “
content:
16th November, Brussels:  The Digital Commons Policy Summit 2026 brought together more than 100 participants in person, almost 600 who streamed online: policymakers from the European Union, representatives from the private sector, civil society and the NGI community – or the new ‘Open Internet Stack’ community. The common message that emerged was that open source and digital commons are no longer a niche topic. They are now an integral part of Europe’s technological sovereignty. The question that remains is how to ensure their long-term sustainability.

“We want to innovate and scale up, by focusing on both demand and supply. Digital commons and open source are crucial for Europe’s sovereignty and competitiveness, because they help us reduce our dependencies.”

Benjamin Bögel, Member of the Cabinet of the European Commission Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy

title: Climate Justice and Community Resilience: Mutual Aid, Organising and Disaster Recovery
content:
The resources on this page have been collated by the Commons librarians to support community leaders, organisers and others building resilience and readiness for climate impacts, emergencies and natural disasters.

As the climate crisis escalates more and more extreme weather events are occurring, with big impacts on people and the environment. How communities prepare for these events can make a crucial difference.

On this page we have gathered links to resources in the following areas:

  • Organising: An approach to social change which involves recruiting community members, developing leaders, identifying issues, taking collective action and building and using power for positive outcomes.
  • Mutual Aid: Sharing resources and care at the grassroots level, not waiting for interventions from the state or corporations.
  • Resilience: Building the capacity of individuals, organisations and communities to respond to, and recover from, crisis.
  • Just Recovery: An approach to disaster recovery which centres social justice, addressing power relationships and systemic harms.
  • Collaboration: Ways organisations, communities and government agencies can work together to prepare, respond and recover.

title: Five Years of CC’s Open Culture Program: Landmarks, Lessons, and Legacy
content:
Five years ago, we set out to build a coordinated global effort to help cultural heritage institutions (libraries, museums, archives…) open up access to the knowledge and culture they steward in their collections for everyone, everywhere, to enjoy. Thanks to a $5 million grant from the Arcadia Fund, in 2021 we launched the Open Culture program to promote more equitable access to culture and heritage in the digital environment. From new practical resources for practitioners and policymakers, to opportunities for local action through community engagement, all the way to the co-creation of an ambitious manifesto—the Open Heritage Statement—we’ve built a solid foundation for open culture on a global scale. What started as a niche field in the open family evolved into one of CC’s largest programs in the organization’s 25-year history.  

In this blog post, we first offer a retrospective of the key milestones we reached over half a decade of activity, share lessons learned, and end with reflections as one chapter closes and a new one opens.

  • Over 15 new resources developed especially for open culture
  • 30+ funded community activities in the global majority world

title: Poland’s new security reality: When terrorism hits close to home
content:
Until recently, terrorism was far less common in Poland than in countries such as France, Belgium or Spain. Attacks involving firearms were virtually unheard of. The main security concerns identified by the police included sabotage, disinformation, cyberattacks and espionage. These threats were largely linked to Poland’s geographical proximity to Russia, which continues its war against Ukraine while conducting hybrid operations against NATO and EU member states.

The events of 7 November 2026 have shifted these priorities. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the incident as an act of terrorism. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said the evidence collected so far suggested that the perpetrator was fascinated by far-right ideology. However, the authorities have not confirmed any links to radical organisations, nor has any foreign involvement been established.

Above all, the incident highlighted how difficult it can be to prevent an attack in the heart of a major city.

Dr Paulina Piasecka, director of the Terrorism Research Centre at Collegium Civitas, believes the response of Kraków’s emergency services demonstrated the readiness of Poland’s state institutions.

title: The trouble with pet turtles and pink flowers
content: If you went on a walk this summer, you might not have noticed anything out of place. Pink flowers blooming near the riverbank. A turtle with a red stripe behind its eye sunbathing on a log. A raccoon enjoying its breakfast next to your rubbish bin. But the Himalayan balsam, pond slider, and raccoon that you might have seen are all on an EU list of species it considers a major threat to native ones. The list of “invasive alien species of Union concern” currently includes 114 plant and animal species that were introduced accidentally or deliberately into a natural environment where they are not normally found. EU countries are required to try to prevent accidental introductions, catch and eradicate new arrivals quickly, and manage the species that have already become widespread. A TEC analysis of the geographical spread of 75 invasive alien species of Union concern show that 83% are present in more than one country, and 60% are reported in at least five. The success of invasive alien species can be attributed to a couple of important shared characteristics, according to Piero Genovesi, biologist and chair of the IUCN SSC Invasive Species Specialist Group. title: Four Maryland high school students sue after AI mistakes Doritos bag for gun
content:
Football players say they are ‘traumatized’ after being handcuffed and detained by police while waiting for rides home

Four current and former students at a Maryland high school have filed a lawsuit a year after armed police detained them, prompted by an AI alert that mistook a bag of Doritos for a gun, in an incident that left them “fearing for their lives”.

The plaintiffs sued Omnilert, the company behind the AI gun-detection system, Baltimore county police, the board of education, individual officers and the school principal, alleging unlawful detention and search because of technological and human errors.

title: Chicago’s City Council Orders Independent Review of Finances as Scrutiny Intensifies
content:
The debate over Chicago’s financial struggles — out in the open as never before — took a new turn on Wednesday as the City Council added to the scrutiny.

The City Council voted 45-5 in a special meeting to give a leading alderperson the authority to hire an outside firm to independently review Chicago’s finances.

It’s unclear if an audit would be complete in time for the City Council to consider its findings before the Dec. 29 deadline mandated by state law to pass a 2027 budget, in what likely will be contentious negotiations with Mayor Brandon Johnson. Later in the day came another sign of distress: S&P Global put the city on credit watch with a warning that the budget wrangling is likely to result in a credit downgrade within 90 days.

The intense council debate over the city’s financial future comes in the wake of a package of stories published Monday by WTTW News and ProPublica that examined how a $55 billion debt burden, decades in the making, was hampering efforts to service Chicagoans and how the Johnson administration was turning to more borrowing to plug holes, such as large police settlements.
snippet: The debate over Chicago’s financial struggles — out in the open as never before — took a new turn on Wednesday as the City Council added to the scrutiny.

title: Tavion Somalia-päätökselle sinetti – järjestöt kantelevat oikeuskanslerille
content:
Suomen laki on ministerin toimivallan yläpuolella, Fingo muistuttaa. Järjestöt aikovat tehdä ministerin toiminnasta kantelun. Tiedotteen lopussa on sitaatteja järjestöiltä, joita Tavion päätös koskee.

Jaa

Ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavio (ps.) eväsi tuet neljältä Somaliaan suunnitellulta kehitysyhteistyöhankkeelta, joille virkahenkilöt olivat esittäneet rahoitusta. Varsinainen päätös ilmoitettiin järjestöille tänään keskiviikkona, ja ulkoministeriö myös tiedotti asiasta.

Virkahenkilöt ovat Fingon tietojen mukaan jättäneet neljää Somalia-hanketta koskien eriävän mielipiteen.

Järjestöt ovat kritisoineet Tavion linjausta, koska Somaliaa ei oltu suljettu ulos hanketuen hakuvaiheessa. Fingo on vaatinut Tavion päätöksen korjaamista.

Hallituspuolueiden puheenjohtajat ovat vedonneet siihen, että päätös kuuluu ministerin toimivaltaan. Kun virkahenkilöt arvioivat julkisesti ministerin toimineen lainvastaisesti, hallituskumppanit eivät voi kuitenkaan Fingon mielestä mennä sen taakse, että tapaus kuuluu ministerin toimivaltaan.

title: Subventionen für Gaskraftwerke: Zwölf Milliarden Euro für fossile Konzerne
content:
Die Bundesregierung will die Energieversorgung sicherstellen und vergibt deshalb riesige Summen – allerdings nur für Gaskraftwerke. Fast das gesamte Geld landet bei zwei fossilen Energiekonzernen. Unsere Karte zeigt, um welche Projekte es geht.

Bundeswirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche (CDU) verfolgt eine klare Strategie, wenn es um die Sicherung der Stromversorgung geht. Anstatt klimafreundlichere Batteriespeicher zu fördern, setzt sie sich vor allem für einen massiven Ausbau der Gasinfrastruktur ein – ganz im Sinne der fossilen Lobby.

Gemeinsam mit Umweltorganisationen haben wir das Ausmaß dieser Strategie erstmals auf der GemeinsamGegenGas-Karte sichtbar gemacht. Neben geplanten Flüssiggasterminals, Pipelines und Gasbohrungen zeigt die Karte auch die zahlreichen geplanten Gaskraftwerke. Im August haben wir die Karte veröffentlicht. Nun wurde bekannt, welche Gaskraftwerke von der Bundesregierung subventioniert werden. Wir haben diese Daten auf der Karte ergänzt.

title: Trump administration targets yet another journalist’s sources
content:
Tomorrow, a federal court in Virginia will hold a hearing in a case that offers a troubling look at just how far the Trump administration will go to attack journalists and their confidential sources.

Journalist Matthew Cole is facing a Department of Justice that seems determined to force him to reveal his confidential sources. Cole was one of several journalists behind a September 2025 New York Times article about a disastrous American military operation in North Korea during the first Trump administration, one that resulted in civilian deaths.

Just five months after the article was published, the DOJ issued a grand jury subpoena to Cole, seeking to compel him to identify his sources and testify about his reporting. Cole moved to quash the subpoena, but in July, a magistrate judge recommended that his motion be denied.

If the district judge hearing the case tomorrow adopts that recommendation, it’s very possible that Cole will have to decide between burning sources and, potentially, facing crippling fines or even jail time.

title: An AI chatbot can explain your rights. But can it get you justice?
content:
Getting information does not equate to accessing justice

Originally published on Global Voices

Image courtesy the Hague Institute for Innovation in Law

By Zainab Malik

This post is part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “Justice as infrastructure.” In this Spotlight, Global Voices is partnering with The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law (HiiL) to highlight the ways justice functions as critical infrastructure for any society. You can support this coverage by donating here.

Imagine a woman facing eviction who turns to an AI chatbot for help. It explains her rights and drafts a letter to her landlord. But she cannot afford a lawyer, does not know where to submit the letter and has no institution that can enforce her rights fairly. The chatbot has made the law easier to understand, but has it brought her any closer to justice?

title: Kulttuuri kuuluu kaikille lapsille, ei vain varakkaista perheistä tuleville
content:
Elämme yhteiskunnassa, jossa perhetausta määrittää yhä vahvemmin lapsen tulevaisuutta, hyvinvointia ja harrastusmahdollisuuksia. Kun julkisesta taloudesta leikataan, kohdistuvat iskut usein kaikkein herkimpiin, kuten lapsiin, nuoriin ja kulttuuriin. Tämä kehityssuunta on paitsi epäoikeudenmukainen, myös yhteiskunnallisesti lyhytnäköinen. Kulttuuri ja taide eivät ole luksustuotteita, joita ostetaan silloin kun rahaa jää yli. Ne ovat inhimillisen kasvun perusta, itsetunnon rakennuspalikoita ja jokaisen lapsen oikeus.

”Tasa-arvoinen kulttuuripolitiikka on tehokkainta mahdollista ennaltaehkäisevää mielenterveystyötä ja segregaation torjuntaa.”

– Pia Lohikoski (vas.)

Tasa-arvoinen taidekasvatus vaatii rakenteita, jotka murtavat varallisuuden asettamia esteitä. Tässä keskiöön nousee taiteen perusopetus. Vasemmistoliitto on pitkään ajanut taiteen perusopetuksen saavutettavuuden parantamista.

title: Slushin suojelumetsäverkosto kasvoi 40 hehtaarilla – metsiä suojeltiin Pohjois-Savossa, Kainuussa ja Pohjois-Pohjanmaalla
content:
Kansainvälisesti tunnetun teknologia- ja kasvuyritystapahtuma Slushin suojelumetsä kasvoi tänä vuonna kolmella uudella metsäalueella. Luonnonperintösäätiön avulla pysyvään suojeluun hankittiin yhteensä noin 40 hehtaaria metsää Kiuruvedeltä, Kajaanista ja Muhokselta. Yhdessä viime vuonna hankittujen alueiden kanssa Slush-metsän kokonaispinta-ala on nyt noin 90 hehtaaria.

”Slush haluaa tehdä tapahtumasta vuosi vuodelta hieman vihreämmän. Siksi on hienoa päästä kertomaan, että laajennamme Slush-metsää tänä vuonna kolmella uudella alueella yhdessä Luonnonperintösäätiön kanssa”, kertoo Slushin operatiivinen johtaja Kasper Mäkelä.

”Tapahtuman järjestäminen vaatii valtavasti resursseja, ja haluamme kantaa siitä vastuun tavalla, joka sopii missioomme ja on merkityksellinen myös sidosryhmillemme. Metsien suojelu on meille konkreettinen tapa antaa jotain takaisin. Olemme olleet tyytyväisiä Luonnonperintösäätiön tapaan toimia metsien suojelussa ja siihen, miten säätiö on tukenut tavoitteitamme”, Mäkelä jatkaa.

title: Novaja Gazetan sulkeminen jättää aukon, jota on vaikea paikata
content:
Kyläläisiä pyydettiin kertomaan mielipiteensä. Mielipiteellä ei tosin olisi mitään merkitystä, selitti piirin johtaja suorasukaisesti.

Nikolsk on 700 asukkaan kylä Arkangelin alueella Pohjois-Venäjällä. Viranomaiset aikoivat lakkauttaa kyläkoulun kaksi ylintä luokkaa sota-ajan budjettipaineisiin vedoten. Säästöä kertyisi viisi miljoonaa ruplaa eli noin 55 000 euroa.

Kyläläiset olivat eri mieltä. Ilman ylimpiä luokkia lapsiperheet lakkaisivat muuttamasta kylään ja yksi Venäjän harvoista yhä kasvavista kylistä alkaisi kutistua. He ottivat yhteyttä valtuutettuihin, keräsivät nimiä, vaativat kansanäänestystä ja veivät asian oikeuteen. Lopulta aluehallinto lupasi ylimmille luokille viisi vuotta lisäaikaa.

Tämä on kertomus venäläisistä, jotka eivät hyväksyneet heidän puolestaan tehtyä päätöstä. Se on myös kertomus sanomalehdestä. Novaja Gazeta kirjoitti kiistasta helmikuussa ja palasi toukokuussa kertomaan, mitä kyläläiset olivat saaneet aikaan.

Marraskuun 9. päivänä 2026 tuo lehti lopetti toimintansa Venäjällä. (Novaja Gazeta Europe on erillinen, maanpaossa toimiva julkaisu.)

title: 8th International Open Search Symposium – A review (day three)
content:
The third and final day of #ossym started on a controversial note. The keynote by Aline Blankertz from Structural Integrity brought in valuable new angles to the open search discussion. She argued that openness enables AI and further deepens dependencies.

Aline stated that people “like openness because it encourages sharing and transparency”.
But she also pointed out that openness feeds AI, because AI is best at exploiting openness effectively. It takes the open web and closes it by encouraging people to use a chatbot that delivers the answers easily!

One example she mentioned, which illustrates the situation, was Wikipedia.
Wikimedia and Google used to have a mutual dependence. Wikimedia needed visibility and Google needed good content! Google used to make donations. But Wikipedia page views have fallen by over a third between 2020 and 2025. Wikipedia cannot do anything because of their commitment to openness. And it seems that as Wikipedia becomes less visible, Wikipedia might decline.

Aline concluded: High quality content should not be free!

title: Eduskuntavaalit 2027: Tekoälyä ja sisältöähkyä?
content:
Tekoälyn käyttö vaikuttaa siihen, millaista tietoa ehdokkaista ja puolueista välittyy äänestäjille. Muutokset kampanjoinnissa ja äänestyskäyttäytymisessä voivat näkyä jo ensi kevään eduskuntavaaleissa.

Tekoäly muuttaa vaalikampanjointia ja äänestäjien tiedonhakua myös Suomessa. Kevään 2027 eduskuntavaaleissa tekoäly auttaa ehdokkaita tuottamaan sisältöä sekä äänestäjiä vertailemaan poliittisia vaihtoehtoja. Se ei kuitenkaan itsessään ratkaise, kenen viestit tulevat näkyviin tai millaisina ehdokkaat ja heidän tavoitteensa esitetään.

Tekoälyn merkitystä onkin tarkasteltava osana laajempaa viestinnän ympäristöä, jossa alustat, kampanjat ja tiedonhakupalvelut vaikuttavat siihen, mitä ihmiset näkevät ja voivat arvioida.

Poliittinen näkyvyys ei ole sidoksissa vain julkaisujen määrään. Siihen vaikuttaa myös, millaisena ehdokas esiintyy, mitä hän kertoo poliittisista tavoitteistaan ja miten sisältö toimii eri kanavissa. Samaan aikaan yleisöjen sitoutuminen viesteihin, reaktiot, kommentit ja jaot vaikuttavat merkittävästi sisältöjen leviämiseen.

title: How we discovered a 115 million-year-old ‘algae rebellion’ in Portugal’s sea cliffs
content:
Quite a few scientific discoveries are a product of chance. You set out looking for one thing, but often end up finding something totally unexpected. In micropalaeontology, the study of microscopic fossils, this is especially common. You never know what you’re going to find until you start examining the samples under the microscope.

This story began in the spring of 2024, when we were travelling through the Algarve, in southern Portugal, with the aim of determining the age of rocks there by studying fossils of charophytes, a group of green freshwater algae that includes the closest descendants of land plants. This field is known as biostratigraphy: a branch of geology that determines the age of rocks based on the fossils they contain.

We visited several locations that had been studied between the 1960s and the 1980s. Among them was Praia da Luz, which would hold the biggest surprises for us. We collected 120kg of rock, mostly clay, and sent it all to Barcelona – much to the disbelief of the post office clerk in the Algarve town of Loulé, when we told him the (rather heavy) parcel contained “stones”.

title: Beijing has three priorities at the Shenzhen summit – a China expert explains
content:
China is hosting the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit for the third time in the past 25 years. The gathering in Shenzhen will see the leaders of the US, China and Russia sit down together for a formal three-way meeting for the first time in history.

But what does China want from the summit? I see it as having three main priorities. First is to consolidate its position as one of the world’s most important diplomatic hubs. Second is to set out its vision for a new global order.

And third is to take advantage of favourable geopolitical conditions, primarily brought about by US setbacks in Iran and Russia’s quagmire in Ukraine, to adjust the terms of its engagement with Washington and Moscow.

Hosting national leaders and other high-level officials has become a key feature of Chinese diplomacy in recent years. President Xi Jinping has welcomed over 25 world leaders to China so far in 2026. These include Canada’s Mark Carney, Germany’s Friedrich Merz, Spain’s Pedro Sánchez and the UK’s former prime minister, Keir Starmer.

title: Missä kulkee raja? Maahanmuuton turvallistaminen heikentää kansainvälisen suojelun ehtoja
content:
Ihmisten liikkuminen on aina ollut osa kansainvälistä politiikkaa, mutta viime vuosina siitä on tullut yhä selvemmin valtioiden turvallisuuspolitiikan ja geopoliittisen kilpailun väline. Muuttoliikkeiden kytkeminen kansalliseen turvallisuuteen muuttaa tapaa, jolla valtiot suhtautuvat rajoihinsa, suvereniteettiinsa ja kansainvälisiin suojeluvelvoitteisiinsa. Samalla kasvaa riski, että turvapaikanhakijoiden oikeudet jäävät turvallisuuspoliittisten tavoitteiden varjoon.

Marraskuussa 2021 tuhannet ihmiset kokoontuivat Puolan ja Valko-Venäjän rajalle. He olivat lähteneet kotimaistaan eri syistä, mutta päätyneet tilanteeseen, jossa heidän liikkumisestaan oli tullut osa valtioiden välistä vastakkainasettelua. Valko-Venäjän hallintoa syytettiin ihmisten kuljettamisesta Euroopan unionin ulkorajalle tarkoituksenaan painostaa unionia ja horjuttaa sen jäsenvaltioita. Rajalle saapuneiden ihmisten tilanteesta tuli samalla osa turvallisuuspoliittista kertomusta, jossa kysymys heidän liikkumisestaan yhdistyi Euroopan vakauteen ja suvereniteettiin.

Huomiota kiinnitetään erityisesti kilpailukykyyn, liiketoiminnan kansainvälisyyteen ja kannattavuuteen. title: AKT: Kuljettajien työolosuhteita parannettava – ”Turvallisuuteen on pakko investoida”
content:
AKT haluaa parannusta kuljettajien työolosuhteisiin, erityisesti turvallisuuteen. Ongelmana ammattiliiton mukaan on, että kuljettajat työskentelevät yksin, töitä tehdään epätyypillisiin aikoihin, kuten aamuyöllä ja työhön liittyy jatkuva fyysisen ja henkisen väkivallan uhka.

Auto- ja kuljetusalan työntekijäliitto AKT:n valtuusto vaatii parannuksia kuljettajien turvallisuuteen. Kuljettajilta tulee yhä enemmän palautetta matkustajien häiriökäyttäytymisestä ja väkivallan uhasta, tiedotteessa kerrotaan.

LIITON MIELESTÄ vastuuta turvallisuudesta ja kuljettajien hyvinvoinnista ei voi jättää heidän itsensä tai yksittäisen liikennöitsijän harteille. Liiton mielestä turvallisuus pitää huomioida järjestelmällisesti osana kokonaisuutta ja koko koulutusketjua.

AKT esittää ratkaisuna esimerkiksi Traficomin, ammattiliiton, liikennöitsijöiden ja tilaajien yhteistyön tiivistämistä häiriökäyttäytymisen ja väkivallan uhkien ehkäisyssä.

– Turvallisuuteen on pakko investoida, jos alalle halutaan tulevaisuudessakin työntekijöitä. Kuljettajien turvallisuutta ei tunnuta ottavan riittävän vakavasti, AKT:n puheenjohtaja Ismo Kokko sanoo tiedotteessa.

title: Sudan: Devastating RSF drone strikes on civilians in El Obeid should be investigated as war crimes
content:
Drone strikes by Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which hit residential areas and civilian infrastructure in El Obeid city, in Sudan’s North Kordofan State, killing dozens and disrupting essential services, should be investigated as war crimes, Amnesty International said today.

The organization investigated nine RSF drone strikes in El Obeid and its surroundings, which killed 37 civilians and injured 10 between June and August 2026. Three of the strikes hit residential areas; four struck key civilian infrastructure, including El Obeid’s power plant, fuel stations, and the main market; and two targeted moving vehicles. In all incidents, interviewees said they either saw or heard the drones, moments before or after the strikes. Amnesty International’s investigation did not identify military objectives in the vicinity of the sites at the time they were struck.

title: Ecuador Pushes to Expand Amazon Oil Drilling While Land Defenders Face Threats
content: Ecuadorians voted overwhelmingly in 2023 to stop oil extraction at Yasuní National Park, one of the most biodiverse places on Earth, yet oil drilling has continued despite that historic referendum. “The government does not want to close the wells,” says Ivonne Yánez, the president of Acción Ecológica, an environmental nonprofit group based in Ecuador. The Ecuadorian government is also “continuing expanding the oil activities in the Amazon,” she points out. Yánez also speaks about how dangerous Latin America is for environmental activists. It is where “the most number of defenders that are just defending their lands, their rivers, their rights,” are killed. “And in Ecuador, this is also happening.”

title: The concept of scientific research in data protection law: current state and future prospects?
content: The EU’s General Data Protection Regulation 2016/679 (“GDPR”) applies also where personal data is processed for scientific research purposes. However, the GDPR does not formally define “scientific research”, and so far, there has not been a clear consensus on the definition of the term under the GDPR.1 The distinction matters, as processing personal data for scientific research purposes benefits from specific rules and flexibilities under the GDPR, including, for example, presumed compatibility of further processing and the possibility of longer retention under Article 5, subject to Article 89 safeguards. Article 17 also provides a conditional exception to erasure where erasure would make research impossible or seriously impair its objectives.

title: Outage Chaos: When Tech is too Big to Fail
content:
Outages happen, but we deserve a resilient internet where no one outage at one company can put people at risk and disrupt the global economy. We can only get there by addressing an over-reliance on a few cloud monopolists through effective antitrust laws and interoperability requirements.

Service outages, like we’ve seen recently at Microsoft, Apple*, banks, courts, airlines, and elsewhere, can be more than an annoying hurdle. Losing a vital service due to an error can cause the same impacts as a government-ordered internet shutdown—people losing access to vital information and lines of communication.  As usual, the greatest harms are faced by people on the margins globally.

There’s not much hope in companies out-nerding these issues either. Technical errors will always exist, whether it’s a bug, negligence from an administrator, or a malicious attack. The problem is an over-reliance on any one company or system when these inevitable outages occur. It’s a matter of public safety and economic stability that policymakers mitigate the impact of these disruptions before they occur.

title: Two Prisoners Executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison, Karaj
content:
According to HRANA, on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, two prisoners were executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

HRANA has confirmed the identity of one of the prisoners as Morteza Naghdi, 30.

Based on information received by HRANA, Mr. Naghdi had previously been arrested on a murder charge and sentenced to death by a criminal court. Prior to his execution, he was held in Ward 7 of Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

Earlier, Mizan, the judiciary’s official news agency, reported the execution of a prisoner without disclosing his identity. HRANA has identified the prisoner as Saeed Amel.

According to Mizan, he had been sentenced to death on charges of murder and rape.

At the time of this report, the execution of Morteza Naghdi had not been announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

According to HRANA, 1,062 people were executed by hanging in Iran between January 1 and October 31, 2026, amid a sharp increase in executions over the past two years.

title: Tiedekeskus Auroran aluetaloudellinen ennakkoarvio on julkaistu – tutustu Sodankylään suunniteltuun tiedekeskukseen!
content:
Sodankylään suunniteltu Tiedekeskus Aurora yhdistää tutkimuksen, oppimisen, matkailun ja alueen elinvoiman. Auroran lähtökohtana on Sodankylässä jo olemassa oleva kansainvälisesti merkittävä arktinen tutkimus ja osaaminen. Tavoitteena on tehdä tutkittu tieto suurelle yleisölle ymmärrettäväksi ja koettavaksi sekä rakentaa sen ympärille ympärivuotista oppimista, matkailua, yritystoimintaa ja uusia palveluja. Auroran sisältöaihioihin kuuluvat muun muassa avaruus, revontulet, arktinen ympäristö sekä geologia ja mineraalit.

Syksyn 2026 aikana Tiedekeskus Auroran valmistelu on edennyt uuteen vaiheeseen: vuonna 2027 ratkaistaan tiedekeskuksen toimintamalli sekä valmistellaan kiinteistöinvestoinnin omistus-, rahoitus- ja toteutusvaihtoehtojen markkinatestausta.

Auroran sisällöllinen perusta rakentuu tiiviissä yhteistyössä tutkimusorganisaatioiden kanssa. Keskeisiä sisältökumppaneita ovat Ilmatieteen laitos, Oulun yliopiston Sodankylän geofysiikan observatorio ja Geologian tutkimuskeskus GTK.

title: Kuntien nihkeys ekologiseen valokuiturakentamiseen ihmetyttää alan toimijoita – ”Vaatimus 70 sentin syvyydestä on historiallinen jäänne”
content:
Tekniikka & Talous nosti äskettäin esiin valokuidun rakentamisessa käytettävän mikrosahauksen, joka on yleisesti käytössä esimerkiksi Ruotsissa ja muissa Pohjoismaissa, mutta tyssännyt Suomessa kuntien lupakäytäntöihin.

Artikkelissa haastateltu Tietoliikenteen ja tietotekniikan keskusliitto Ficomin lakiasiainpäällikkö Marko Lahtinen kummastelee tilannetta. Mikrosahauksessa ja muissa matala-asennusmenetelmissä kaapeli sijoitetaan noin 30–50 senttimetrin syvyyteen perinteisen 70 senttimetrin sijaan. Menetelmä on jopa kymmenen kertaa perinteistä kaivamista nopeampi ja sen ympäristökuormitus on merkittävästi pienempi.

Valoo käyttää ekologista matala-asennustekniikkaa kaikkialla, missä se on mahdollista. Klaus Varis kuitenkin kertoo, että moni kunta ei edelleenkään salli nykyaikaisten menetelmien käyttöä.

”Pidän kuntien asennetta todella outona. Kun ottaa huomioon, miten paljon asukkaita harmittaa kotikadulla pyörivä kaivinkone, on suorastaan hullunkurista, että matala-asennuksia ei sallita”, Varis sanoo.

Jopa sähkökaapeleita syvemmälle – täysin turhaan

title: Music Now! Musica Nostra! Forum in Mafra put music and listening at the heart of Europe’s living cultural heritage
content:
Bringing together European heritage professionals, musicians, researchers, policymakers and young people, the ‘Music Now! Musica Nostra!’ Forum took place on 7-8 November 2026 at the Royal Building of Mafra, Portugal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Through two days of discussions, musical experiences and exchanges, participants explored how music and listening can strengthen democracy, foster intercultural dialogue, safeguard living heritage and contribute to a more sustainable and peaceful Europe.

Organised by the Centre Européen de Musique, a partner of the European Heritage Hub, in collaboration with Europa Nostra, the Municipality of Mafra and the Centro Nacional de Cultura, which operates the Europa Nostra Heritage Hub in Lisbon, the conference built on the first ‘Music Now! Musica Nostra!’ gathering held in April 2025 and the European Manifesto it inspired. The event brought together voices from across Europe and beyond, with a particular emphasis on the role of younger generations in shaping the future of Europe’s cultural heritage.

title: World ‘held hostage by oil mafia’, says Panama minister at Cop 31
content:
Key issues unresolved as summit enters final days, with 30 countries signed up to forge fossil fuel treaty separate to UN process

The world is “being held hostage by the petroleum mafia” and seems unable to break free, Panama’s environment minister has warned, as key issues remain unresolved in the final days of the UN Cop31 climate summit.

“We are in love with our kidnappers,” said Juan Carlos Navarro, at a press conference to announce 30 countries were now signed up to forge a new fossil fuel treaty, separate to the UN process. “We love the petroleum guys. We can’t live without them, and they are so smart they have convinced us that they are doing this for our own good.”

title: RJI grant funds Hacks/Hackers pilot with Wisconsin Watch to bring local journalism into AI assistants
content:
The Reynolds Journalism Institute has awarded Hacks/Hackers $35,000 to build News Connectors, a pilot with Wisconsin Watch that brings the newsroom's reporting into AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude. The connector is an open-source Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. People who add it to their assistant can ask about issues Wisconsin Watch has covered, and the assistant will search the newsroom's archive and cite its stories as the source. The pilot opens to the public in early 2027, and we'll release the code and a report on the results so any newsroom can learn from it.

"Bots and AI agents now make more requests to websites than people do, and many newsrooms don't have a plan for this yet. RJI is investing in finding answers now, while there's still time to act. This pilot with Wisconsin Watch will show us what AI-native distribution can look like for a local newsroom, and we'll share what we learn with the rest of the industry," said Burt Herman, co-founder and principal of Hacks/Hackers.

If your newsroom or organization is working on how journalism reaches people through AI, we'd like to hear from you. Email contact[at]hackshackers.com.

title: Sudan: Transfer War Crimes Suspects to ICC
content:
(The Hague) – Sudanese authorities should immediately transfer former Interior Minister Ahmed Haroun to the International Criminal Court (ICC) to face charges in The Hague, Human Rights Watch said today. Haroun was recently taken into Sudanese custody and faces ICC war crimes and crimes against humanity charges, committed in Sudan’s Darfur region, in 2003 and 2004.

On November 8, 2026, the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) reportedly re-arrested Haroun, interior minister of Sudan in 2007, when an ICC arrest warrant was issued against him. He was arrested one day after he took part in a video podcast interview, his first public appearance since 2019. The armed forces have not officially confirmed Haroun’s whereabouts, but media reported that he is detained in Khartoum state.

title: Oulaistelaisesta Tuula Aitto-ojasta Kotiseutuliiton hallituksen puheenjohtaja
content:
Suomen Kotiseutuliiton valtuusto teki syyskokouksessaan keskiviikkona Helsingin Tieteiden talolla lukuisia merkittäviä henkilövalintoja. 

Tuula Aitto-oja Oulaisista Pohjois-Pohjanmaalta on valittu Suomen Kotiseutuliiton uudeksi hallituksen puheenjohtajaksi.  Aitto-oja on ollut liiton hallituksen jäsen jo vuodesta 2022 lähtien. Aitto-oja on kulttuurituottaja ja -vaikuttaja, joka on omistautunut erityisesti koneisiin ja esineisiin, työmenetelmiin ja paikallisiin tarinoihin liittyvän tiedon säilyttämiseen tuleville sukupolville.  

Valtuuston ensimmäiseksi varapuheenjohtajaksi valittiin toisena varapuheenjohtajana toiminut Tuija Ahola Lappajärveltä. Valtuuston toiseksi varapuheenjohtajaksi valittiin Marjatta Huhta Äänekoskelta Keski-Suomesta.  

Ensimmäisenä varapuheenjohtajana toiminut Anna-Maija Korhonen Tervosta Pohjois-Savosta ja Katja Tikka Helsingistä valittiin hallitukseen kolmivuotisiksi kausiksi 2027–2029. Aitto-ojan loppukauden ajaksi vuodeksi 2027 hallitukseen valittiin Paavo Enroth Kajaanista. 

Aitto-oja ottaa hallituksen puheenjohtajuuden haltuunsa vuoden vaihteessa espoolaiselta Sampo Suihkolta, joka on hoitanut tehtävää kahdeksan vuoden ajan.

title: What China’s Gene-Editing Deaths Reveal About Its Biotech Industry
content:
BEIJING — In March 2023, four-year-old Mei in Shanghai was diagnosed with a rare genetic mutation linked to developmental delay and autism-like traits. Although her condition was mild and she improved with therapy and special education, her parents remained worried about her future. Hopeful for a cure, they paid Qiu Zilong, a renowned neuroscientist at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, and his team $860,000 to develop a customized gene therapy. The treatment, which used adeno-associated viruses to deliver gene editors to the brain, had been approved by Xinhua Hospital, a leading hospital for rare diseases.

On March 24, 2025, trillions of viral particles carrying gene editors were injected into Mei’s spinal cord. She soon developed a fever and kidney failure and died within days. A year later, Qiu’s team published its preclinical findings in Nature. Mei’s case was hailed by Chinese media as “a world-class breakthrough.” Mei’s death and her family’s financial support were not mentioned.

title: Accused South American Drug Lord Faces US Trial after Judge Rejects Motions
content:
Sebastián Marset, an accused South American drug lord, appears headed for a January jury trial after a federal judge in Virginia this week rejected multiple efforts by the defense to dismiss charges.

U.S. District Judge Rossie Alston Jr. on Tuesday rejected arguments from Marset’s lawyers that the Uruguayan national was being subjected to a vindictive prosecution and misconduct by prosecutors.

Marset’s defense team had argued their client’s Miranda rights, which protect against self-incrimination, were violated when agents from the Drug Enforcement Administration interviewed him without a lawyer present.

But the judge held that Marset had initiated some of the conversations after his arrest in southern Bolivia and was not coerced into talking with DEA agents during his expulsion to Peru and subsequent transfer to the United States and custody in Virginia.

The judge also rejected the defense’s “fruit of the poisonous tree” motion that asserted that evidence should be excluded because it was obtained improperly.

title: The Directing Genius of Akira Kurosawa Explained
content: Generations of Westerners have come to appreciate Japanese cinema through the films of Akira Kurosawa, but many have been shocked to find out that Kurosawa himself isn’t as beloved in Japan as they’d imagined. It’s less that his homeland rejects him than that his work has been regarded there as a somewhat foreign taste. That judgment must have something to it: despite their thoroughly Japanese settings, Throne of Blood, The Bad Sleep Well, and Ran were, after all, Shakespeare adaptations, and Kurosawa spoke openly of structuring his stories in the manner of not just traditional Japanese theater, but also symphonies. Consider, too, the way his films continue to inspire Western remakes, from The Magnificent Seven and A Fistful of Dollars in the nineteen-sixties to Living and Highest 2 Lowest in this decade.

title: Tasavallan presidentin kansainvälistymispalkinnot Iceyelle, Valiolle ja Meriteollisuus ry:lle
content:
Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubb jakoi vuoden 2026 kansainvälistymispalkinnot Presidentinlinnassa keskiviikkona 18. marraskuuta 2026.

Tulokasyrityksenä palkittiin avaruusteknologian yritys Iceye. Aalto-yliopistosta opiskelijaprojektina alkunsa saanut Iceye valmistaa tutkasatelliitteja ja tarjoaa asiakkailleen kokonaisvaltaisia satelliittipalveluita. Iceyessa yhdistyvät korkea teknologiaosaaminen, nopea kasvu ja globaali vaikuttavuus.

Kasvuyrityksenä palkittiin Valio, joka on liikevaihdoltaan Suomen johtavia ruoka-alan yrityksiä ja suurin elintarvikeviejä. Yrityksen tuotteita viedään noin 60 maahan, ja Valion osuus koko Suomen elintarvikeviennistä on noin neljännes.

Yhteisöpalkinto myönnettiin Meriteollisuus ry:lle. Meriteollisuus ry:n ja sen jäsenyritysten työn ansiosta Suomi on säilyttänyt asemansa yhtenä maailman johtavista vaativan meriteknologian ja kestävän merenkulun ratkaisujen osaajamaista. Meriteollisuus ry:n noin 100 jäsenyrityksen verkosto muodostaa suomalaisen meriteollisuuden ytimen.

title: Kysely: 95 prosenttia SAFAn kanssa kilpailun järjestäneistä sai tavoitteitaan vastaavan tuloksen
content:
Kysely toteutettiin syyskuussa yhteistyössä riippumattoman markkina- ja mielipidetutkimusyrityksen Suomen Kyselytutkimuksen kanssa. Kyselyyn saatiin 106 vastausta, joista 66 edusti Safan kanssa kilpailun järjestäneitä (edeltävän 10 vuoden aikana) ja 40 oli potentiaalisia kilpailujen järjestäjiä.

Safan kanssa kilpailun järjestäneistä 95 prosenttia kertoi, että arkkitehtuurikilpailun tulos vastasi hankkeen tavoitteita. Kilpailuehdotusten arviointi sujui hyvin 94 prosentin mielestä, vaikka mukana oli todella suuriakin yleisiä kilpailuja. 86 prosentilla idea- ja suunnittelukilpailu oli johtanut suunnittelutoimeksiantoon.

Safan palveluihin oli tyytyväisiä 88 prosenttia ja tyytymättömiä vain 1,5 prosenttia. Safan nimeämiin tuomareihin oli tyytyväisiä 95 prosenttia kokeneista järjestäjistä.

Kilpailun hyödyiksi koettiin muun muassa muita hankintamuotoja parempien tai monipuolisempien ratkaisujen saaminen (71 %) ja hankkeen parempi näkyvyys (67 %). Loppukäyttäjien osallistaminen oli toiminut kilpailuprosessissa melko tai erittäin hyvin 69 prosentin mielestä.

title: Vihreät suurin nousija tuoreessa HS-gallupissa
content:
Vihreiden kannatus kääntyi kasvuun tuoreessa Helsingin Sanomien teettämässä gallupissa ja ylsi 9,1 prosenttiin. Vihreät kasvatti kannatustaan puolella prosenttiyksiköllä, enemmän kuin mikään muu puolue. Myös vasemmistoliiton kannatus nousi lokakuuhun verrattuna 0,4 prosenttiyksikköä, kristillisdemokraattien 0,2 ja perussuomalaisten 0,1 prosenttiyksikköä.

Kirittävää vihreillä vielä kuitenkin on. Vasemmistoliitto ylsi jälleen HS-gallupien historiansa parhaaseen tulokseen, 12 prosenttiin.

Kokoomuksen kannatus on puolestaan jatkanut pitkään laskuaan. Oikeistopuolue sinnittelee toistaiseksi kakkospaikalla 15,6 prosentilla, joka on alhaisin HS-gallupin mittaustulos sitten vuoden 1991.

HS:n mukaan kokoomus on jo pidemmän aikaa menettänyt kannatustaan varsinkin naisten keskuudessa. Sen suosio on vähentynyt selvästi lehden mukaan myös miesten parissa, vaikka edelleen miehet, iäkkäät, korkeakoulutetut ja eniten ansaitsevat korostuvat kokoomuksen kannattajissa muihin puolueisiin verrattuna.

Selvässä kärjessä jatkaa SDP 23 prosentin kannatuksella, joskin sekin jatkaa hidasta laskuaan. Demaripuolue on tullut jo yli kaksi prosenttiyksikköä alaspäin vuoden 2025 huippuluvuistaan.

title: Europe launches €95m semi-autonomous ship in Estonia
content:
The Union’s newest naval vessel is to provide surveillance and to protect undersea infrastructure. The EUROGUARD is not yet in service; developers say testing is the point of the exercise.

Europe has launched a new kind of naval vessel. The EUROGUARD semi-autonomous ship went through its launch in Nasva, Estonia, on the Baltic Sea. The 45-metre craft is to strengthen maritime surveillance and help protect Europe’s coasts. The European Commission says it will support member states facing growing risks at sea.

Those risks are real, according to the Commission. Threats to undersea cables, energy infrastructure, and strategic maritime routes are rising. The purpose of the vessel is to help member states respond to them.

The EUROGUARD project began in 2022. It brings together 29 organisations from 10 European countries. The Estonian shipyard Baltic Workboats coordinates the work. The European Defence Fund has contributed €65m of a total budget of about €95m.

title: From a rejected applicant to the Mentor Summit: Wikimedia at Google Summer of Code 2026
content:
📷 Featured image: GSoC Mentor Summit 2026 group photo

In 2018, I applied to Google Summer of Code but wasn’t selected. The next year I reapplied and got selected as a GSoC contributor. I then continued my role as a contributor and mentor and now I have gone on to be Wikimedia’s organisation administrator and then I have represented Wikimedia at GSoC Mentor Summit.

My first summit experience was in 2023, and after some change of plans I had the privilege of returning to my second in Munich, Germany. From 30 October – 1 November 2026, I joined Sarthak Parashar as one of two representatives to meet mentors and org admins of more than 100 open source communities.

All below is a summary of what we discussed, what other communities are facing and what I think should be brought back to Wikimedia.

This is unlike any conference. As a full unconference, there isn’t a set programme in advance. Any mentor or org admin can submit a session by adding a sticky note to the schedule board and the rest of us choose what sessions to attend. We filled the entire schedule by the first morning, which shows what’s currently on people’s minds.

📷 The unconference schedule board, covered in sticky notes

title: Good neighbours, complicated history: What Poles and Germans really think
content:
Thirty-five years after signing their Treaty on Good Neighbourship, Poland and Germany remain closely connected. But how do people on both sides of the border actually view their relationship? And do they see each other as equal partners?

These are some of the questions explored in the latest edition of the Polish-German Barometer, titled Between Cooperation and Security: 35 Years After the Treaty on Good Neighbourship.

One of the biggest differences between Polish and German respondents concerns how Germany has addressed its crimes and acknowledged the suffering inflicted on Poland during World War II.

As many as 44% of Germans believe their country has already done enough in this regard. In Poland, only 18% share that view.

The issue is even more prominent among respondents who have a negative opinion of Polish-German relations: 61% of them point to the failure to fully address German wartime crimes as a key reason.

Germans, meanwhile, tend to blame poor relations on political differences (43%) and the policies of Polish governments towards Berlin (38%). Historical issues rank only third.

title: No olives left to pick
content: It's olive harvest time in Italy, but in many parts of Puglia, there's nothing left to pick. Since 2013, the bacterium Xylella fastidiosa has killed at least 20 million olive trees in Salento alone. The bacterium chokes the tree’s water supply until it dries out. In areas near the outbreak, every host plant within 50 metres of a new case must be felled to prevent the disease spreading. An estimated 33,000 jobs have been lost in Puglia, according to the farmers’ association Confagricoltura. “This is the most serious agronomic problem in the EU,” said Patrizio Ziggiotti, secretary general of the Puglia-based charity Save The Olives, which was set up to confront the crisis and help farmers. The bacterium is thought to have arrived on ornamental plants from Central America, and has since been detected in Spain, France, and Portugal. Olives are central to southern European history and culture. In Greek mythology, Athena won the patronage of Athens by giving the city an olive tree. title: Age-friendly workplaces: experts assess 19 policy proposals
content:
How can we help people stay well and keep working as they grow older?

On 4 November 2026, the Solutions for Age-Friendly Employers (SAFE) project brought together nearly 50 experts from Estonia, Finland and Sweden to assess policy proposals for age-friendly working conditions. The online workshop examined two questions for each proposal: how much difference could it make, and how feasible would it be to put into practice?

The online workshop, Age-Friendly Workplaces: Ideas for Action, focused on how policy can help people aged 55+ stay in employment. The SAFE project focuses on health and social care, but the discussion showed that many of the questions apply across sectors. Can employees access training throughout their careers? Can they adjust their work when their needs change? And what support do managers need to make those changes possible?

title: They Were Just Admitted to the Bar. Now They’re Federal Prosecutors. Meet Trump’s New DOJ.
content:
In early October, a recent law school graduate shared a post on LinkedIn that would have been unheard of before the second Trump administration.

After passing the bar exam, 29-year-old Preston Bigley wrote, “With this milestone complete, I will begin serving as an Assistant United States Attorney in the Criminal Division of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Texas.”

It was a remarkable achievement, considering Bigley had graduated from Texas A&M’s law school in May and had been hired by the Justice Department in August to be, as his resume notes, an “incoming” assistant U.S. attorney. That unusual title was followed by an unusual caveat: “pending bar admission.” Once officially licensed to practice the law, he updated his profile to show he had become a bona fide federal criminal prosecutor.
snippet: In early October, a recent law school graduate shared a post on LinkedIn that would have been unheard of before the second Trump administration.

title: ‘Who will respond?’: Jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong fears being forgotten amid 10-year sentence
content:
The activist admits his mental state has been negatively affected by the 10-year sentence increase

Originally published on Global Voices

Joshua Wong released from Lai Chi Kok Reception Centre on June 17, 2019. HKFP's File photo.

This article was originally published by Hong Kong Free Press on November 16, 2026. The following version is edited and republished on Global Voices under a content partnership agreement. It is also part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “Justice as infrastructure.” You can support this coverage by donating here.

In a letter from a Hong Kong prison earlier this year, jailed activist Joshua Wong expressed dread over the looming sentence in his foreign collusion case. “Fretting about whether it’s 2032 or 2037, my mental state is hardly all right,” he wrote in Chinese, weighing when he might regain his freedom.

The agony inevitably stems from this: What if it’s 2037? Well, it’s easy [for people] to sympathise in the moment, but it’s difficult to be consistent, and it will only get harder.

title: Where in Europe could electric-powered ferries create cleaner travel routes?
content:
Electric battery-powered ferries use electricity from the shore to charge batteries on board. These batteries supply electric motors that propel the ship. On suitable routes, low-carbon electricity could make sea travel substantially cleaner and strengthen its potential as an alternative to flying.

In June 2025, Finnish ferry operator Viking Line unveiled its Helios concept, outlining plans for a fully electric passenger-and-car ferry between Helsinki and Tallinn. The proposed vessel, designed to carry around 2,000 passengers and 650 cars, would be powered by batteries with a capacity of 85–100 megawatt-hours (MWh).

title: Xi-Trump-Putin summit: when great powers want to call all the shots, what does it mean for everyone else?
content:
Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump are meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday.

The meeting is no doubt unusual – a very rare opportunity for the leaders of the world’s three major powers to exchange views directly on major global issues.

It’s drawn comparisons to the Yalta conference of 1945, when US President Franklin D Roosevelt, British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Russian leader Joseph Stalin met to divide the world into spheres of influence after the second world war.

But this is no Yalta 2.0. Nor is the Shenzhen summit an isolated episode. In May this year, Xi hosted back-to-back visits by Trump and Putin to Beijing. Trump reciprocated by hosting Xi in Washington in September, and met with Putin in Alaska last year.

Taken together, these developments signal a broader shift away from the post-Cold War emphasis on global institutions and multilateral consultations toward a more personalised form of great power management.

title: Massive New Study Shows How Young People Feel About AI Companions
content:
A new study from Gallup looked at how young people across the world are making friends, both digitally and in person. The good news is that around 93% of the young people surveyed reported having at least one strong in-person friendship. The weird news is that 33% said they had an AI companion.

Gallup’s study is lengthy and nuanced. It partnered with the Boston Children’s Digital Wellness Lab to conduct the study and used online surveys of more than 16,000 young people from the ages of 15 to 22 in 16 different countries.

A lot of the topline results won’t surprise anyone living in today’s constantly online digital-forward age. Gallup found that respondents felt their in-person friendships were their strongest, that digital friendships complemented rather than replaced in-person ones, and that stronger friendships made people happier no matter how the connection was made. Three things that stood out were how the young respondents talked about AI, loneliness, and doomscrolling.

title: "Shameful": Fossil Fuel Industry Blocks U.N. Climate Action as Global Warming Reaches 1.5°C
content: As Democracy Now! continues broadcasting from the U.N. climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, we speak with Rachel Cleetus, climate program director at the Union of Concerned Scientists, about climate finance — the notion that efforts to mitigate the climate crisis must be funded. “Climate finance is not an abstract thing. It’s what countries need to be able to transition away from fossil fuels,” says Cleetus. “And right now we have pennies in these funds.” She notes that at a pledging event for the Adaptation Fund, which supports climate finance for developing countries, a mere $50 million was pledged. “It’s shameful, absolutely unjust, what’s happening here. And richer countries are continuing to block progress.” This comes as scientists say the world is set to overshoot the target, set by the 2015 Paris Agreement, of limiting global heating to 1.5 degrees Celsius.

title: Three More Detainees from the January 2026 Protests Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Amirhossein Gholamshahi, and Hossein Jafari have been sentenced to death.

Based on information received by HRANA, the three individuals were sentenced to death in a joint case by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. Among the charges brought against them is allegedly carrying out operations on behalf of Israel. The death sentences were communicated to the three individuals in October 2026.

The three men were arrested by security forces in January 2026 in connection with the nationwide protests. Following their arrests, they were transferred to the Greater Tehran Prison, where they remained for some time.

During the summer of 2026, Hossein Parvin, Amirhossein Gholamshahi, and Hossein Jafari were transferred from the Greater Tehran Prison to Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj, where they have remained incarcerated ever since.

HRANA’s investigation into the specific allegations underlying the charges against these three individuals is ongoing.

title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
content:
A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza

Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

title: Human Rights Watch Mourns Death of Activist Nabeel Rajab
content:
(New York) – Nabeel Rajab, a prominent human rights activist from Bahrain and a close partner of Human Rights Watch, passed away on November 17, 2026, at the age of 62. He reportedly died in Türkiye following a heart attack.

Rajab rose to prominence as a human rights defender in Bahrain in the 1990s, and in 2000 he co-founded the Bahrain Human Rights Society, one of Bahrain’s first human rights organizations. He then co-founded and later became the president of the Bahrain Centre for Human Rights.

Rajab had served as a member of the Human Rights Watch Middle East and North Africa division’s advisory committee since 2010, playing a key role not only in supporting Human Rights Watch work in Bahrain, but also providing guidance to the documentation and advocacy work that Human Rights Watch carries out across the region.

title: EU Commission accused of withholding emails on killing patent law
content:
LUXEMBOURG — The European Commission was accused Wednesday of withholding internal messages that explain why it dropped a contentious patent proposal, amid claims of pressure from U.S. Vice President JD Vance.

At a court hearing in Luxembourg, judges were told that German center-left MEP Tiemo Wölken asked the Commission for internal notes on why the proposal was abruptly killed in early 2025. He was told there was only one relevant internal document: minutes of a private meeting between heads of cabinet, which the Commission refused to hand over.

Wölken’s lawyers said the absence of information was hard to believe given how contentious the proposal had become.

It was “unbelievable” that there were “zero emails on this highly-politicized, economically-relevant procedure,” Carsten Zatschler, Wölken’s lawyer, said at the EU’s General Court.

“All of this apparently happened without any form of electronic communication,” Zatschler said. “That’s quite simply not credible.”

title: Susien kiintiömetsästystä vastustava vetoomus keräsi lähes 33 000 nimeä – ministeriö suunnittelee 109 suden kaatamista
content:
Eläinoikeusakatemia on luovuttanut maa- ja metsätalousministeriölle lähes 33 000 ihmisen allekirjoittaman vetoomuksen susien kiintiömetsästystä vastaan. Vetoomus luovutettiin Säätytalolla torstaina 12. marraskuuta.

Maa- ja metsätalousministeriö on esittänyt, että susien kiintiömetsästys alkaisi joulukuussa ja kohdistuisi yhteensä 109 suteen. Eläinoikeusakatemian pitää suunniteltua metsästystä ongelmallisena Suomen susikannan haavoittuvan tilanteen vuoksi.

"Vetoomuksen suosio osoittaa, että Suomesta löytyy runsaasti susien puolustajia", toteaa järjestön toiminnanjohtaja Elisa Aaltola tiedotteessa.

Eläinoikeusakatemia huomauttaa, että Suomessa elää vain muutamia satoja susia. Järjestön tiedotteessa esitettyjen lukujen mukaan maaliskuussa 2026 susia oli noin 430. Marraskuun kanta-arvio oli 476–669 yksilöä.

Kanta-arviot kuvaavat eri ajankohtia, eikä niiden perusteella voi suoraan päätellä, kuinka suuri vaikutus suunnitellulla metsästyksellä olisi susikantaan. Eläinoikeusakatemia katsoo kuitenkin, että populaatio on liian pieni laajamittaisen metsästyksen kohteeksi.

title: Outspend and outproduce Russia, Kubilius exhorts business summit
content:
Europeans are still too slow in paying the price of peace. The price of war would be higher, Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius said on Wednesday.

Russia will spend about as much on its military next year as all EU member states combined, according to EU Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius. He made the claim at the European Business Summit in Brussels on 18 November 2026. For Mr Kubilius, the conclusion is stark. Europe is not yet deterring Moscow, and that must change.

The numbers are large. Russia plans to allocate €180bn to its military next year, a 33 per cent increase on this year. In purchasing power parity terms, that matches or slightly exceeds the €500–550bn that all member states will spend together. Mr Kubilius said Russia’s war economy remains able to expand production and to innovate.

Mr Kubilius said Russia was not being deterred. It was escalating attacks on Ukraine and waging a hybrid war against Europe. “We need first of all to outspend Russia in defence and to outproduce Russia in defence.” The question, he said, is whether the EU is doing enough at every level.
snippet: Europeans are still too slow in paying the price of peace. The price of war would be higher, Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius said on Wednesday.

title: EU steps up Black Sea security as Russian threats mount
content:
European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen’s visit has placed Romania and Bulgaria at the centre of the EU’s response to the deepening security crisis in the Black Sea. Its most significant outcome is the acceleration of work on a joint maritime security hub – a project that will test whether Europe can turn its strategic commitments into genuine operational capabilities.

The Black Sea is no longer merely a regional theatre of conflict. It is becoming a test for NATO and the EU: can they protect commercial shipping, energy infrastructure and the territory of member states without triggering a wider confrontation? In October alone, at least 10 merchant vessels were attacked near the Romanian and Bulgarian coasts or within those countries’ territorial waters. Four vessels sank, while 34 seafarers were reported dead or missing.

title: The information war in your comments
content: “Spamouflage” is an operation you may never have heard of. It best embodies a phenomenon we likely all interact with on a daily basis on social media: coordinated state-backed attempts to manipulate online conversations. In 2023, Meta took down 7,704 Facebook accounts and 954 Pages belonging to Spamouflage, a Chinese bot network it linked to Chinese law enforcement. Hundreds of accounts posted comments on Facebook written to sound “personal” and aimed at Western governments, voters, and critics of Beijing. One bot wrote that the 6 January attack on the US Capitol “made the world see the hypocrisy and unbearable [sic] of ‘American democracy,'” according to influence operation tracker Graphika. Fake commenters often adopt invented identities. “Sometimes the bots are even given a bit of personality, like ‘I'm a Black American’ or ‘I'm a doctor in the Midwest,’” Darren Linvill, co-director of Clemson University's Media Forensics Hub, told TEC. Spamouflage accounts replying to news outlets and public figures typically criticise or harass them. Some pose as members of groups tied to those they are attacking, Graphika analyst Lili Turner told TEC. AI makes these tactics easier to deploy.

title: Mental Health in All Policies: what the Baltic Sea Region can offer
content:
PA Health Coordinator/NDPHS Secretariat Director Ülla-Karin Nurm joined policymakers and experts to discuss the economic and social case for sustained investment in mental health at Mental Health Europe’s (MHE) conference “Investing in Mental Health for Resilient Societies”. Held at the Estonian Parliament (Riigikogu) in Tallinn on 4 November 2026, the conference brought together more than 130 participants in person and online, including researchers, civil society representatives and people with lived experience.

OECD modelling presented at the conference estimates that mental ill health costs around 1.7% of GDP across the EU, a figure comparable to the estimated costs of tobacco use or obesity. The conference also highlighted an access gap across OECD countries. Around 60% of people who need mental health care are unable to access it.

Ülla-Karin Nurm took part in a panel on how to translate EU priorities into national action, alongside Ann-Katrin Orr of MHE, Lithuanian Vice-Minister of Health Ignas Rubikas, Stefan Schreck of the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Health and Food Safety, and Riina Sikkut, a member of the Estonian Parliament and former Minister of Health.

title: Diversifying funding was supposed to protect civil society: It did not
content:
‘…stability, where it exists, is only ever twelve months deep’

Originally published on Global Voices

Activists hold a candlelight vigil to commemorate those who lost their lives in post-election violence in Tanzania in Nairobi, Kenya, on November 20, 2025. Image by Anadolu Lucas-Mukasa courtesy of FORUS.

By Clarisse Sih, Bibbi Abruzzini, and Jake Wieczorek

“Every one of our grants is annual and project-tied. We have no reserves and no core funding, which means that stability, where it exists, is only ever twelve months deep.”

That is how one civil society organization in Algeria described its finances to us in a recent survey. It is a sentence many donors would recognize from their own grant files, and it captures a reality familiar to many organizations: years of navigating short-term grants, restricted budgets and uncertain renewals, with little room to plan beyond the next funding cycle.

title: How sustainable are bioplastics, really?
content:
Plastic’s durability and strength make it extremely useful, but plastic waste is a major source of environmental pollution. It does not biodegrade, and we are failing to recycle enough of it.

Bioplastics offer an alternative to traditional, petroleum-based plastic. The term refers to a range of different polymers with similar properties to plastics, but derived from biological raw materials rather than fossil fuels.

Over the last decade, bioplastic development has sped up for a number of reasons. New environmental policies have been introduced, which aim to reduce dependence on fossil fuels and promote the use of renewable raw materials. These include a Europe-wide strategy on plastics and an EU Directive on single-use plastics.

Leer más: 12 reasons why plastic recycling is failing so badly

A wave of research and innovation projects has also made these materials more sustainable than plastics. They take less energy to manufacture, and produce less greenhouse gas emissions. Since bioplastics are compostable, they also help to promote the circular economy and prevent the release of microplastics into the environment.

title: Les terres rares ne sont ni rares, ni même des terres, alors qu’est-ce que c’est ?
content:
L’ESSENTIEL

- Le terme « terres rares » désigne un ensemble de 17 éléments chimiques.

- Ils ont des propriétés très intéressantes pour de nombreuses applications industrielles, ils sont donc devenus des ressources stratégiques majeures.

- La Chine est l’un des acteurs majeurs du domaine mais la France a également des atouts.

Qualifiées de « vitamines de l’ère moderne » en raison de leurs propriétés catalytiques, optiques, magnétiques et électroniques exceptionnelles, les terres rares présentent un intérêt stratégique pour de nombreuses technologies actuelles, dans les secteurs de l’énergie bas carbone, de la défense, de l’électronique (écrans LCD, LED, composants de disques durs et de smartphones) et du médical (IRM, lasers). Le secteur le plus important est celui des aimants permanents, surtout néodyme-fer-bore (NdFeB), pour les moteurs des véhicules électriques ou les équipements des éoliennes. Les autres secteurs, comme les catalyseurs pour l’automobile, les poudres de polissage ou les alliages nécessitent des terres rares plus abondantes et moins coûteuses que le néodyme, surtout le lanthane et le cérium.

title: Asuntojen lyhytvuokraukseen tulee vuorokausirajoja
content:
Eduskunta hyväksyi keskiviikkona rakennuslain muutokset, jotka koskevat asuntojen lyhytaikaista vuokrausta. Hallituksen esitys hyväksyttiin äänin 108-80.

Vuokranantaja saa tulevan lain mukaan vuokrata omistamaansa, asumatonta asuntoa lyhytaikaisesti enintään 90 vuorokautta vuodessa.

Kunta voisi nostaa vuorokausirajan enintään 180 päivään haluamillaan asemakaava-alueilla.

VUOROKAUSIRAJAT koskisivat esimerkiksi taajamien sijoitusasuntoja, joissa ei ole kirjoilla ja asumassa yhtään ihmistä.

Vakinaisesti ja tilapäisesti asuttuja asuntoja, loma-asuntoja sekä haja-asutusalueella sijaitsevia asuntoja voisi vastedeskin vuokrata ilman vuorokausirajoja.

Tätä ennen laissa ei ole ollut säännöksiä lyhytvuokrauksesta. Nyt hyväksytyt muutokset ovat tulossa voimaan ensi vuoden alussa.

title: "Ecocide": Colombia's New Right-Wing Gov't Ends Amazon Protections, Rejects Fossil Fuel Phaseout
content:
The U.N. climate summit comes seven months after a major climate meeting was held in Santa Marta, Colombia, where more than 50 countries gathered for a groundbreaking effort to push for phasing out fossil fuels to combat the climate crisis. The initiative was championed by Colombian President Gustavo Petro, whose term ended in August, but Colombia’s new right-wing President Abelardo de la Espriella has withdrawn Colombia from the Santa Marta coalition.

“Colombia has just reversed the protection of the Amazon,” says Irene Vélez-Torres, former Colombian environment minister under Petro. “What we are seeing is really an ecocide taking place in Colombia.”

Meanwhile, at COP31, “there are petro lobbyists, people here defending the interest of the corporations, and therefore the discussions cannot make any progress,” Vélez-Torres adds. “The agreements cannot even mention the word 'fossil fuels.'”

title: Voters Reject ALPRs and Surveillance Tech at the Ballot Box
content:
Do automated license plate readers (ALPRs) have any place in our communities? That question has been a hot topic in city council meetings, community conversations, and news coverage around the country for months. This past election day, a couple of U.S communities took it further: to the ballot. 

And overwhelmingly, voters decided that, no, these devices should not be deployed on our streets. We agree! 

In Maine, the coastal community of York voted to remove the town’s existing ALPR cameras and require that any future proposed installations receive voter approval before proceeding. The local initiative ended up on the ballot after constituents gathered enough signatures on a citizens’ petition for a local ordinance. On Election Day, nearly three-quarters of York voters supported the ban. 

Thousands of miles away, voters in League City, Texas also voted against allowing the local police department to continue use of ALPR cameras. That vote was formally approved on November 17, which began a 72-hour window to remove the cameras. Since the election, the cameras have been “bagged” or covered to prevent the collection of data.

content:

The Climate University has evolved from an initiative of a few higher education institutions into a community of dedicated teachers, originating from different disciplinary backgrounds, but united by dedication to teach sustainability related Climate University courses to their students. These teachers are interested in growing professionally, exploring new ways of teaching and making sustainability education accessible to their students.  Climate University has also enabled other initiatives, like Specialisation programme in climate expertise (2024-), Climate University for Virtual exchanges Erasmus+ project for students from Ukraine (2023-2026), Una Europa Micro-credential in Sustainability (2022-), Climate change Teachers Academy (2022-), and many others.

title: Burkina Faso Targets Critics in Exile
content:
Journalists, activists and political opponents who fled Burkina Faso to escape the junta’s repression now risk arrest and prosecution abroad, as the country’s judicial authorities pursue dozens of individuals over alleged terrorism-related offenses.

Burkina Faso Prosecutor General Désiré Sawadogo announced on November 13 that a special court handling terrorism-related offenses had opened six cases against at least 45 people and entities. All those targeted exposed serious military abuses during counterinsurgency operations and include exiled journalists critical of the junta, among them Ahmed Newton Barry, Issaka Lingani, Inoussa Ouédraogo, Adama Ouedraogo, and Abdoulaye Barry; exiled social media activist Naïm Touré; former foreign affairs minister Alpha Barry, and international journalist Wassim Nasr. They face various charges, including complicity in terrorist associations and financing terrorism.

Burkina Faso sent international arrest warrants and extradition requests to Côte d’Ivoire, France, and the United States, said Sawadogo. He added that Burkina Faso asked the United States to use Meta to identify and prosecute Facebook page administrators accused of promoting terrorism.

title: Germany, Austria demand TikTok’s European platform be sold to owners in EU
content:
Germany and Austria say Chinese-owned TikTok should come under European ownership to safeguard personal data, boost sovereignty and curb the platform’s “openly visible threat to our democratic society.”

The joint proposal Wednesday by top government ministers of the two countries comes after President Donald Trump forced the separation last year of TikTok’s operations into a U.S.-based entity, with its original owner, Beijing-based Bytedance holding about one-fifth of the new entity.

Trump’s campaign to initially ban and later split up TikTok cited national security concerns. Now, Berlin and Vienna are going down a similar route.

With 200 million EU users, TikTok is “a central player with significant relevance for opinion formation and social participation,” Germany’s media minister Wolfram Weimer and Austria’s State Secretary for Digitalization, Alexander Pröll said in a joint statement.

A TikTok spokesperson said there was “zero merit” to the proposal.

The platform’s role in elections is being investigated under the EU’s Digital Services Act, while regulators have fined the firm for sending Europeans’ data to China, in breach of privacy rules.
