title: Mediterranean net is cast wide as Kallas’s absence raises eyebrows
content:
Security arrangements between the EU and its regional southern partners must address everybody’s concerns, the EU-MED Security Forum 2026 heard.

Hadja Lahbib opened the first EU–Mediterranean Peace and Security Forum in Brussels on Wednesday. It fell to the commissioner for equality as the planned keynote speaker, Kaja Kallas, head of the European External Action Service (EEAS) and EU security and foreign policy chief, was conspicuously missing.

The High Representative did not attend Wednesday’s scheduled appearance at the Schuman Security and Defence Forum, either. Her press office told EU Perspectives that Ms Kallas was down with flu. Whether it is a case of ‘political influenza’, an explanation that sprang to mind following major setbacks for Ms Kallas in recent weeks, was not clear at the time of writing.

Ms Lahbib opened the forum with a story from the 12th century. She described Al Idrisi, a cartographer commissioned by King Roger II of Sicily to survey the known world. The result, the Book of Roger, held detailed accounts of countries, cities, rivers, mountains, trade routes, and peoples.
snippet: Security arrangements between the EU and its regional southern partners must address everybody’s concerns, the EU-MED Security Forum 2026 heard.

title: Preserving Irra’s Heritage, Empowering Its Youth: AIHI and Yoruba Wikipedia Fan Club Offa Train Community Youths Ahead of Oya Festival 2026
content:
The preservation of our cultural heritage begins with the people who own the stories, traditions, and histories. As communities continue to embrace digital technologies, it is increasingly important to equip young people with the knowledge and skills to document, preserve, and share their cultural heritage with the world.

In a significant step towards achieving this, the African Institute for Heritage Intelligence (AIHI), in collaboration with Yoruba Wikipedia Fan Club Offa, organised a one-day digital heritage documentation and Wikimedia training for youths and students in Irra community, ahead of the highly anticipated Oya Festival 2026.

The training was held at the Onira Palace, Irra, providing an important cultural setting for the engagement. Bringing the training to the palace was particularly meaningful, as it connected the younger generation directly with the traditional institution and the cultural heritage they are being empowered to document and preserve.

title: Voices from Turkey: "The More Oppressive the Regime Gets, the More Resilient People Become"
content: As climate negotiations enter their crucial final stretch in the last few days of COP31, held in Antalya, Turkey, dozens of human rights groups urged Turkish authorities to release four LGBTQ+ activists ahead of a hearing that has just begun at a court in Istanbul. Back in September, Turkish authorities began a large-scale crackdown on LGBTQ+ organizations and activists, raiding offices, blocking social media accounts and websites, arresting at least 116 people and launching criminal investigations into at least 160 people. Meanwhile, since last month, Turkey’s last two remaining opposition television channels have been brought under government control. This follows the Turkish government’s widespread crackdown on the main opposition party with dozens of mayors arrested since 2024.

title: Cambodia’s Repression Hangs Over Francophonie Summit
content:
As world leaders recently gathered in Phnom Penh to celebrate the 20th Francophonie Summit with the theme of peace and shared prosperity, French President Emmanuel Macron took to the podium to call publicly for an investigation into the killing of former Cambodian lawmaker and French citizen Lim Kimya. It was a rare public rebuke of the Cambodian government by a foreign leader.

A gunman killed Kimya in Bangkok, Thailand in January 2025. Kimya had served as a parliament member with the opposition Cambodia National Rescue Party before its 2017 dissolution.

A Thai court convicted the gunman, Ekkalak Paenoi, in October 2025 and issued arrest warrants for two Cambodian suspects, Ly Ratanakraksmey and Pich Kimsrin, both of whom have connections to high-ranking Cambodian officials. The Cambodian government—like many of its neighbors in Southeast Asia—is increasingly persecuting activists abroad.

The Cambodian government has yet to acknowledge the arrest warrants or start an impartial investigation. Both men remain at large. France has issued Interpol Red Notices for them on charges of complicity in premeditated murder.

title: EU strikes overnight deal for faster solar, grid, and charging permits
content:
Homes and businesses installing solar panels, batteries, or charging points could get permits within months. The smallest might need none at all. An EU deal also eases grid applications and makes larger renewable projects share benefits with locals.

Under the deal EU governments and Parliament reached early on Wednesday, permits for solar equipment and batteries installed alongside it would take no more than three months. Stand-alone storage and charging stations would have a six-month deadline. The agreed rules also set a three-month limit for grid connections, extendable to six months where justified.

“We need grid infrastructure for clean, affordable, and homegrown energy and to break our dependence on imported fossil fuels,” said Darragh O’Brien, Ireland’s Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment, whose country holds the rotating Council presidency. He spoke after the provisional agreement. Electricity transmission projects currently take around ten years to complete, with permitting accounting for more than half that time.

title: Along the Red Sea Coast: Documenting the Heritage of Hurghada and El Qoseir
content:
From 10 to 12 October 2026, six members of the Egypt Wikimedians User Group embarked on a three-day photo documentation trip to Hurghada and El Qoseir, two coastal cities whose heritage extends far beyond their familiar image as tourist destinations. The expedition explored historic neighbourhoods, museums, scientific institutions, religious landmarks, and industrial remains, documenting the region’s diverse cultural and natural heritage. Through photography and subsequent editorial work, the participants sought to address gaps in the representation of these places across Wikimedia projects and make the history of these places more accessible through freely available knowledge.


The first two days focused on Hurghada, a city shaped by its relationship with the Red Sea, its maritime environment, and the growth of tourism. Rather than focusing solely on its resorts and beaches, the six participants explored several aspects of the city’s urban, cultural, and scientific heritage. The participants were Amr Fathy, Donia El Domiaty, Sohila El Shaer, Summer Kamal, Mohamed Ouda, and Ibrahim El Aidy.

title: La peur nous rend-elle plus faciles à gouverner ?
content:

    • Plus un danger est médiatisé, plus il nous paraît proche et peut renforcer notre aspiration à la stabilité.

    • L’incertitude peut conduire à privilégier des explications simples et à s’aligner sur la majorité.

  • Lorsqu’elle est instrumentalisée, la peur peut aussi produire des effets inverses de méfiance, voire de révolte.

    • Lorsqu’elle est instrumentalisée, la peur peut aussi produire des effets inverses de méfiance, voire de révolte.

    En 2026, près de 68 % des Européens estimaient leur pays menacé dans le contexte international actuel. La France est l’un des États membres où cette perception est la plus élevée, avec 79 % des citoyens préoccupés par ces enjeux de sécurité, ce qui se reflète dans les discours politiques, à l’approche de l’élection présidentielle 2027. Déplorant le « déclin du pays » et les crises économiques, les candidats opposent à ces diagnostics alarmants leurs promesses de protection, de changement ou de redressement.

title: Avhandling om oavsiktliga graviditeter undersöker normer om moderskap och reproduktivt ansvar
content:
Ansvaret för att skydda sig mot att bli gravid anses fortfarande främst vila på kvinnans axlar. Lina Metsämäki disputerar i nordisk folkloristik vid Åbo Akademi med en avhandling om oavsiktliga graviditeter.

Det har gjorts mycket forskning om erfarenheter av abort men det saknas kulturvetenskaplig forskning kring situationen som föregår en eventuell abort, alltså den oavsiktliga graviditeten. Lina Metsämäki har genom intervjuer och analyser av textmaterial, som nyhetsartiklar, kommentarsfält och myndighetsrekommendationer, undersökt hur kvinnor som blivit oavsiktligt gravida förhåller sig till normer om kvinnlighet, moderskap och reproduktivt ansvar.

Några av de intervjuade upplevde den oavsiktliga graviditeten som skamfylld – fast de själva ifrågasatte den ståndpunkten som gammaldags. Ett vanligare sätt att resonera kring sin graviditet var dock att rama in den som något som kan hända vem som helst.

– Men denna förståelse förutsatte att de hade vidtagit åtgärder för att skydda sig mot en graviditet. Då kunde graviditeten förstås som en olycklig slump. Om kvinnan däremot inte hade skyddat sig var det svårare att framställa sig som moralisk.

title: Rights Defender in Central African Republic Dies
content:
Nicolas Tiangaye, a prominent Central African lawyer, human rights defender, and former prime minister died in Bangui on November 16, at the age of 70. One of the country's most respected rule of law advocates, his career spanned more than four decades.

Tiangaye first came into the spotlight as a young lawyer when he defended the former emperor, Jean-Bédel Bokassa, in 1986. Later he defended the future president, François Bozizé, when he was accused of plotting a coup.

For Tiangaye, the cardinal rule that all defendants must benefit from their right to a fair trial is one he lived by. By the early 1990s, Tiangaye was one of the leading Central African human rights advocates and served as the Bar Association president.

In 1996 he was the lead defense council for Jean-Paul Akayesu before the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda. Human Rights Watch strongly advocated for the prosecution of Akayesu hailing his 1998 conviction as a historic international precedent. I once discussed the seminal conviction with Tiangaye and he reiterated that a good lawyer must be willing to defend clients and insist on due process, even in highly charged circumstances.

title: Extreme weather cost EU €270bn in five years. And 2026 is not over
content:
Floods, storms, and droughts have cost the EU more in the past five years than in any other five-year stretch since 1980. Most of that bill never reaches an insurer. Households, businesses, and governments pay it themselves, while Europe’s efforts to adapt fail to keep pace.

Extreme weather events caused approximately €920bn in direct economic losses across EU member states between 1980 and 2025, the European Environment Agency (EEA) reports in its updated data. More than €270bn came in the last five years alone, nearly a third of the total.

The figures make 2021–2025 the costliest five-year period on record, highlighting the growing economic burden of extreme weather across Europe. The estimates cover only direct economic damage, excluding indirect costs such as lost productivity, impacts on GDP, environmental impacts, and consequences for human health.

With extreme weather events expected to intensify further, the agency warns that Europe’s adaptation efforts are not keeping pace. The European Climate Risk Assessment estimates annual losses of at least €175bn across the EU and the UK at 3°C of global warming.

title: En bog på en time for 6 dollar: Mød ”meta-forfatteren” Teddy Brask
content:
Teddy Brask er IT-vejleder på en skole. I fritiden laver han bøger, men han skriver dem ikke selv. Siden 2022 har han bygget det, han kalder en AI-styret bogfabrik, på sit eget forlag, One More Book. Det er et system af AI-agenter, som tilsammen skriver bøgerne, læser dem op som lydbøger, laver forsider, markedsfører dem og lægger dem ud til salg. Teddy Brask bestemmer rammerne, og maskinen gør resten.

Når der skal laves en ny bog, sætter han sig derfor ikke ved skrivebordet. Han taler til computeren i stuen:

“Så siger jeg faktisk bare til min computer hjemme i stuen: ’vi skal lave den næste bog.’ Den finder bog nummer 15 frem i serien ud af 30. ’Nå, er det den her, du vil lave?’ Det vil jeg gerne. ’Du går bare i gang’”.

En til halvanden time senere er bogen færdig. Den er skrevet og indlæst, har fået en forside og ligger online, klar til læserne.

“Jeg kan egentlig sidde og drikke en kop kaffe eller se fjernsyn imens. Min rolle lige der er, meget firkantet, egentlig bare at overvåge processen.”

Det kræver hverken et stort budget eller et forlag i ryggen:

title: CFP: Transatlantic Slavery and the Archive Conference, 2027
content:
The National Archives is pleased to announce details of the conference, Transatlantic Slavery and the Archive. The conference is one of the outputs of PASSAGE (Partnership for Atlantic Slavery, Scholarship, Archiving and Global Exchange), which is funded by the Lloyd’s Register Foundation.Conference dates

21–22 June, 2027Venue
The National Archives, KewDeadline for submissions
17.00 (GMT/UTC+0) on Monday 14 December 2026

Histories of transatlantic slavery have long been shaped by the archive. This has led researchers to confront the fact that records of transatlantic slavery were overwhelmingly written by or for enslavers.

Influential critiques by Michel-Rolph Trouillot (Silencing the Past, 1995) and Saidiya Hartman (Scenes of Subjection, 1997; ‘Venus in Two Acts’, 2008) have highlighted the relationship between archival production, power, violence and historical silence. They have shown how the lives of enslaved people are often fragmented, obscured, or wholly absent from the documentary record.

title: How a Town’s Forgotten History Helped Protect Its Drinking Water
content:
When word started to circulate in Falmouth, Massachusetts, that the town had proposed housing development near Long Pond, the town’s main water source, Eric Hryniewicz said he was confused.

“It seemed to be conservation land in everybody’s mind,” said the 25-year-old resident of the Cape Cod town with about 30,000 residents. “It didn’t seem to be an appropriate arrangement for land that was conserved.”

Hryniewicz, a maritime project manager who’d moved back to Falmouth in 2023 after graduating from college, began to do some digging at the local library when a librarian recommended he and his friends continue the search on the Internet Archive. 

At the Internet Archive, he found records that showed the town had purchased the forested land around Long Pond to protect the source of 60% of the town’s drinking water. Hryniewicz was able to look at the property’s history dating back nearly 100 years to demonstrate the intent of earlier residents to safeguard the land,  with the help of records scanned at the New England Regional Digitization Center at the Boston Public Library.

title: CMI joins discussions on the changing role of peace mediation at Paris Peace Forum
content:
CMI – Martti Ahtisaari Peace Foundation participated in the Paris Peace Forum last week for discussions on the changing role of peace mediation and cooperation between states, regional organisations and private diplomacy actors.

The two-day forum, ‘From Sovereignty to Cooperation’, brought together government officials, ministers, heads of state, and representatives of international organisations, think tanks, NGOs and the private sector. CMI attended at the invitation of the European Commission’s Service for Foreign Policy Instruments (FPI).

CMI’s Acting CEO Hanna Klinge spoke on the panel, Peace Mediation Today: New Actors, New Coalitions, Lasting Results, which examined how different mediation actors can combine their strengths in efforts to achieve sustainable peace. Klinge said that it was important that roles were clarified and she championed complementarity, highlighting the contribution of private diplomacy actors in bridging different actors, processes and mediation tracks.

title: COAR launches Retractions Task Force
content:
(photo credit: Salon/Getty Images)

Retractions usually take place on the journal website and by the publisher, without the information being conveyed to other platforms or infrastructures, such as a repository that hosts a copy of that article. In the 2012 paper, The Persistence of Error, Philip Davis found that most freely available copies of retracted biomedical papers outside the publisher’s site carried no notice of the retraction. As a result, those orphaned copies keep being read and cited and also critics can use unmarked retracted copies to argue that repositories spread discredited science or weaken quality control. With the explosive growth of fake and AI-generated papers and a significant increase in the number of article retractions each year, this is becoming an important issue for the repository community to address.

To support the adoption of good practices, COAR is launching a Task Force to develop recommended practices for managing retractions in repositories, with three main objectives:

  • Define the various terminologies related to retractions, corrections, removals, and expressions of concern)

title: Commission preliminarily finds Temu in breach of the Digital Services Act for failure to tackle the sale of illegal products
content:
The European Commission preliminarily found Temu in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) obligation to put in place reasonable, proportionate and effective measures to mitigate the risk of illegal products being offered on its platform.

The Commission preliminarily found that Temu's mitigation measures include ineffective controls to check the compliance of products; a weak content moderation system; and an ineffective sanction system.

Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, said:

Shopping online should not mean risking the purchase of illegal and unsafe products. Under the Digital Services Act, platforms are responsible for protecting users from the risk of illegal content and goods. The preliminary findings against Temu mark another step towards making the online world safer.

title: Tilannekuva tekoälyn käytöstä perusopetuksessa 2026: Tekoäly opetuksessa, oppimisessa ja opetuksen hallinnossa
content:
Teksti: Kaisa Honkonen

Nyt on se julkaistu! Erika Tanhua-Piiroisen ja Jarmo Vitelin kanssa on vuoden verran tehty selvitystä, millä tavoin tekoälyä käytetään perusopetuksessa opettajien, rehtoreiden ja opetuksen järjestäjien työssä. Selvityksessä syvennyttiin käyttötapohin, tulevaisuuden mahdollisuuksiin, tekoälyn tuomiin haasteisiin sekä vastuullisen käytön näkökulmiin. 

Selvitys on tilannekuva keväästä 2026. Kyselyihin vastattiin tammi-helmikuun aikana ja haastatteluja toteutettiin sen jälkeen pääasiassa kevään kuluessa. Tekoälyn kehitys etenee niin nopeasti, että osa toiveista on voinut jo täyttyäkin ja joku silloin käytössä ollut käyttötapa muovautunut uuteen malliin. Selvitys antaa mainioin lähtökohdan tarkastella edellytyksiä, joilla käyttöönotto on tapahtunut sekä tuo esiin kysymyksiä tekoälyn pedagogisesti mielekkäästä käytöstä, joita meidän on syytä yhdessä pohtia. 

Lopuksi olemme tehneet 12 toimintasuositusta selvityksen pohjalta.

title: The electric truck is ready. Europe is not
content: Your latest online delivery probably travelled to you by road, and so does a quarter of all other goods delivered in the EU. The final stretch is usually covered by small vans, many of them electric, but heavy trucks were also likely involved in connecting manufacturers and smaller couriers. And those are still mainly powered by diesel engines. By 2030, an EU law requires heavy-duty truck and bus manufacturers to cut the carbon emissions of the vehicles they produce by 45% compared to 2019. According to the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association (ACEA), that means at least a third of all new trucks currently bought in the EU need to be zero-emission, mainly electric. Now, fewer than 3% are. For manufacturers, shifting production to e-trucks only makes sense if there's demand. “Obviously, you don't produce these vehicles without having someone who wants to buy them,” Thomas Fabian from ACEA told The European Correspondent. And why aren't people buying? Lack of charging infrastructure, mainly. title: They Suffered Brain Injuries After Riding a Six Flags Roller Coaster. Regulators Pinned the Blame on Them.
content:
A 17-year-old boy died after riding the extreme X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain in California this summer, just weeks before two more people suffered severe brain injuries after riding the same attraction, ProPublica and L.A. Material have found.

A homicide detective investigating Christopher Gibson’s death in June sent an email to the California official responsible for ensuring roller coaster safety. But records show that the official did not reply until nearly two months later. The lack of action raises the question of whether the brain damage suffered by the two riders the following month could have been avoided.

Christopher’s death, which has not been previously reported, also raises questions about Six Flags, its flagship X2 ride and the way in which California regulates roller coasters.

Billed as a “fourth-dimension” roller coaster, the X2 drew more than 16 million riders attracted to extreme thrills. It featured seats that swiveled in all directions as the ride hurtled and twisted along the track, sometimes at a rate of up to 76 mph.

title: The Nordic-Baltic Eight policy brief: NB8 and Ukraine security cooperation
content:
New publication in the NB8 policy brief series by Olena Davlikanova (Sahaidachnyi Security Center), John Karlsrud (Norwegian Institute of International Affairs), Klara Lindström (Stockholm Centre for Eastern European Studies, Swedish Institute of International Affairs) and Lesia Ogryzko (Sahaidachnyi Security Center).

Europe’s security order is undergoing a structural transformation. The assumptions that underpinned the post-Cold War architecture – stable deterrence, US primacy and predictable threat environments – have been eroded under pressure from Russia’s protracted war against Ukraine and its broader campaign of sub-threshold operations across the continent. In this emerging landscape, Ukraine is no longer merely a recipient of security assistance. It is a central contributor to Europe’s defence capacity and a driver of its adaptation. Ukraine is also frequently mentioned when European leaders envision the future of the European security architecture – as a member of the proposed European Security Council and the European Defence Union. NB8 countries have entered into strategic partnership agreements with Ukraine and are embarking on operationalising these.

title: Op-ed | Drying Up? The Future of the UK’s Diplomatic Pipeline
content:
As the UK faces growing international challenges and proposed cuts to the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), questions are being raised about the future of British diplomacy and the next generation of diplomatic talent. Drawing on his experience working with the OSCE Mission in Kosovo and serving as one of the UK’s Youth Delegates to the G20 in 2026, Alastair Nicol explores the barriers facing young British people seeking careers in diplomacy and the opportunities for the UK to invest in its future diplomatic workforce.

In 2025, I spent six months with the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe’s (OSCE) Mission in Kosovo. For an internationally-minded young person looking to gain experience in a field operation, Kosovo is a rich environment. 27 years after the Kosovo War (1998-99), the country  continues to host NATO’s Kosovo Force (KFOR), the United Nations, the European Union, the OSCE, and an array of diplomatic missions.

title: Joint NGO Appeal to PM Albanese about Human Rights Activists’ Abduction
content:
The Hon Anthony Albanese MP
Prime Minister
Parliament House
CANBERRA ACT 2600

Dear Prime Minister Albanese,

We, the undersigned human rights organizations, urge you to directly and firmly raise the case of Australian citizen Hiep Tran’s abduction from Cambodia.

You have an important opportunity to raise Hiep Tran’s case directly with Vietnam’s top leaders this week—with Prime Minister Le Minh Hung at the ASEAN Summit in Manila (16–17 November), and with President and Party General Secretary To Lam at the APEC Summit in Shenzhen (18–19 November). We strongly urge you to make his case a priority. 

Tran Hiep was among three human rights activists abducted in Cambodia on 18 September 2026, and forcibly taken to Vietnam. The two other abducted human rights activists are Thuan Nguyen, a Norwegian citizen, and Thai Cong Truong Son, a Vietnamese citizen. The circumstances of their disappearance and cross-border transfer raises fundamental questions concerning Cambodia’s sovereignty, Vietnam’s obligations under international law, and Australia’s responsibility to protect its citizens abroad.

title: Street medicine vendors are dangerously filling Haiti’s healthcare gaps
content:
The ongoing security situation has made the country’s healthcare crisis worse

Originally published on Global Voices

Image by Global Voices, created using Canva elements.

Haiti is a country with very few health facilities and a dearth of healthcare workers to meet people’s needs. Public hospitals lack basic medical equipment, demand far exceeds staff capacity, and administrative problems are rife.

Other health centres, usually run by non-profit organisations, help some of the most vulnerable people, while private hospitals are few and far between, given that most Haitians cannot afford to pay for treatment there. Even the wealthy are often forced to go abroad for treatment when faced with critical health issues.

This already dire situation became worse when gangs from the Viv Ansanm criminal coalition began targeting both public and private health facilities, looting many of them, stealing equipment, and even setting fire to some of the properties. Health centres located in gang-controlled areas are often forced to close temporarily because of fights that break out between rival gangs.

title: OPINION: Time to Suffocate the New Nuclear Arms Race
content:
In Shenzhen, three presidents need a common nuclear language. No treaty is on offer when Xi, Putin and Trump meet on Thursday. A statement of basic principles, and a mandate for talks among the five nuclear-weapon States, would be achievement enough.

By Tariq Rauf*

VIENNA | 17 November 2026 (IDN) — On 19 November, on the margins of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, Presidents Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump are due to sit down together for the first time.1 Between them they command roughly nine of every ten nuclear warheads on earth.2 US officials already are playing the meeting down as an “entry point” from which no agreement is expected.3 They are right about the agreement, and wrong if they think that makes the meeting inconsequential. The most useful thing the three leaders can do in Shenzhen is not to haggle over numbers but to agree on “basic principles” governing strategic relations between them and nuclear weapons.

title: Apply AI? It’ll Cost You
content:
Europe wants researchers and businesses to apply AI. But what happens when using AI on material they already have lawful access to means another licence, another payment, or a contractual ban?

Today, leaders from across Europe meet for the Apply AI Summit, a milestone in the EU’s wider efforts to encourage stronger uptake of AI across industrial sectors in Europe. It offers an opportunity to take stock of progress and set out plans on a topic that Commission President von der Leyen identified as a key priority in her State of the Union speech in September.

When the Apply AI Strategy first came out last year, Knowledge Rights 21 (KR21) welcomed it, recognising the value of an approach focused on the specific needs of each sector, rather than blunter, cross-cutting tools such as copyright. An untargeted approach risks causing significant collateral damage, in particular for research, and is not guaranteed to achieve its goals given that most (copyright-relevant) training takes place outside Europe.

title: Sodan ympäristövaikutukset näkyvät Armenian ja Azerbaidžanin rajalla – Kaukasuksen arvokkain luonnonpuisto vetäytyy armeijan tieltä
content:
Etelä-Armeniassa sijaitsevalla Šikahoghin luonnonsuojelualueella huomio kiinnittyy ensimmäiseksi puihin. Tai oikeastaan niiden puuttumiseen.

Metsän pitäisi jatkua yhtenäisenä, mutta rinteillä avautuu laajoja paljaita alueita. Eri puolilla suojeltua aluetta erottuu raivattua maata, rajavartioasemia ja muuta armeijan infrastruktuuria. 

Vuonna 1958 perustettu Šikahoghin luonnonsuojelualue sijaitsee Armenian Sjunikinin maakunnassa. Sen pinta-ala on lähes 12 140 hehtaaria, josta noin 94 prosenttia on metsää.

Alueella elää muun muassa harvinaisia kaukasianleopardeja, besoaarivuohia, ruskeakarhuja ja armenialaisia kyykäärmeitä sekä lukuisia lintulajeja. Kasvilajeja on noin 1 100, joista 70 on uhanalaisia.

Šikahogh on yksi Kaukasuksen arvokkaimmista luontoalueista. Nyt sen tulevaisuutta uhkaa luonnon monimuotoisuuden vähenemisen lisäksi rajan militarisoituminen.

Armenian ja Azerbaidžanin välinen vuosikymmeniä jatkunut konflikti on keskittynyt Vuoristo-Karabahiin, joka kuuluu kansainvälisesti tunnustettujen rajojen mukaan Azerbaidžaniin mutta oli pitkään pääosin etnisten armenialaisten asuttama.

title: Ekothon on yhteistyön toimintamalli Norjasta, osa I
content:
Mikä ihmeen Ekothron? ”Ei kun Ekothon! No tää on tämmönen yhteistyömalli, jonka toin Norjasta Suomeen”, vastaan kysyjille.

Löysin mallin Brysselissä lokakuussa 2019 Norjan EU-toimiston tilaisuudessa. Oli meneillään Euroopan kaupunkien ja alueiden viikko -tapahtuma (The European Week of Regions and Cities). Kiertotalous- ja ilmastoaiheisissa tilaisuuksissa puhuttiin Greta Thunbergista ja nuorten ilmastolakoista (Fridays for Future), ranskalaisista keltaliivien mielenosoituksista ja Alppien sulamisesta.

Vihdoinkin, ajattelin. EU:ssa on ymmärretty, että ilmasto- ja ympäristötyötä on tehtävä demokraattisesti ihmisten kanssa. Ei ylhäältä määräten, vaan ruohonjuuritason toimintaa mahdollistaen.

Olen tehnyt ilmasto- ja ympäristötyötä 2000-luvun alusta saakka. 25 vuotta sitten askartelin pienoiskasvihuoneen paperimassasta tehdyn maapallon päälle opettaakseni ihmisille kasvihuoneilmiön ja ilmaston muutoksen vaikutuksista. Tein lumiukkojen mielenosoituksen ja soitin herätyskelloja, jotta päättäjät reagoisivat planeettamme hätätilaan. Jaoin kaduilla lentolehtisiä ja kävin loputtomasti keskusteluita.

title: 8th International Open Search Symposium – A review (day two)
content:
3 days in the name of European digital sovereignty! The 8th Open Search Symposium #ossym, which was kindly supported by the German Aerospace Center, united roundabout 100 participants in Berlin and online. – continued

The morning of the second conference day was dedicated to legal and societal sessions, while the afternoon called for active participation in the form of parallel workshops.

The day kicked off with a keynote by Dr. Michael Granitzer from University of Passau, who unlocked potential scenarios of agentic information access via the OWI: “From an Open Web Index to Agentic Information Access”.
In his talk Michael shared how the future of search with AI agents could potentially look like. He predicts that the search ecosystem is changing drastically in various ways:

1. The future of search will be human-agent collaborative set-ups. Agents will become the interface between humans and information and processes; the Web will become their medium.
2. Agents will develop new knowledge by communicating between each other.
3. Small models that operate on well curated data points might be able to compete with bigger models

title: Osta hyvän mielen joulumuistamiset Kirjastoseuran verkkokaupasta
content:
Osta hyvän mielen joulumuistamiset Kirjastoseuran verkkokaupasta! Jokainen kauppaan laitettu euro palautuu kirjastojen toiminnan kehittämiseen, tukemiseen ja puolustamiseen.

Ostamalla Kirjastoseuran verkkokaupasta vaikkapa lahjajäsenyyden, korvakorut, kahvikupin, kangasmerkkejä tai tarroja, tuet työtämme yleisten kirjastojen edunajajana ja kehittäjänä. Ensi kevään ohjelmassamme on ennen muuta eduskuntavaaleissa vaikuttamista ja kirjastojen lukutaitotyön tukemista.

title: Jensen Huang scandal illustrates why human nature is cybersecurity’s weakest link
content:
The end of Jensen Huang’s tenure at Nvidia is steeped in irony. The chief executive of a company whose growth has been propelled by the seemingly unstoppable rise of artificial intelligence was brought down by a vulnerability that no algorithm can eliminate: human nature.

Huang’s resignation from the chipmaker he co-founded followed reports of multiple affairs, most notably one with Alice Huang, a business executive whom U.S. authorities suspect of spying for China. The company says no secrets were leaked.

In a world increasingly focused on protecting private information against high-tech hacking schemes, Huang’s downfall is a reminder that, as the infamous hacker Kevin Mitnick observed, the “human factor is truly security’s weakest link.”

Huang is hardly the first person in a powerful position to lower their defenses. In 2023, Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni spoke candidly about foreign affairs in a call with Russian pranksters who recorded and released the conversation. In 2011, former CIA Director David Petraeus gave his biographer, with whom he was having an affair, access to notebooks containing classified information.

title: Ulkoasiainhallinnon uudistus on saatu päätökseen
content:
Ulkoministeriö on saanut ulkoasiainhallinnon uudistuksen päätökseen. Ministeriö on uudistanut johtamistaan, organisaatiotaan ja toimintatapojaan vahvistaakseen toimintakykyään muuttuneessa ulko- ja turvallisuuspoliittisessa ympäristössä.

Uudistus käynnistyi syksyllä 2023 pääministeri Petteri Orpon hallitusohjelman pohjalta. Valmistelussa kuultiin henkilöstöä ministeriössä ja edustustoissa. Toimeenpano käynnistyi alkuvuonna 2024, ja ensimmäiset muutokset koskivat johtoryhmää, alueosastoja, EU-koordinaatiota ja strategiayksikköä.

”Ulkoasiainhallinnon uudistus on toteutunut laajempana ja vaikuttavampana kuin osasin hanketta käynnistäessäni odottaa. Kokonaisuutena uudistus vahvistaa merkittävästi ulkoasiainhallinnon toimintakykyä ja työn tuloksellisuutta epävakaassa ja nopeasti muuttuvassa kansainvälisessä ympäristössä”, sanoo ulkoministeri Elina Valtonen.

  • Ulkoministeriö uudisti johtamisjärjestelmänsä ja organisaationsa vastaamaan Suomen ulko- ja turvallisuuspolitiikan muutosta ja tarvetta tehostaa operatiivista päätöksentekoa epävakaassa maailmantilanteessa.

title: Att bygga en strategi för fri kunskap i en tid av AI och kriser
content:
Vad kommer fri kunskap att behöva om fem år? Vilken roll kommer Wikipedia att spela i en värld där AI-tjänster förändrar hur människor söker information? Och hur påverkas Wikimediarörelsen av ett samhälle där öppenhet, demokrati och tillgång till tillförlitlig information allt oftare utmanas? Det var några av frågorna som Wikimedia Sverige ställde sig under 2025 inför arbetet med föreningens nya strategi för 2026–2030.

Att ta fram en strategi handlar inte bara om att formulera mål, det handlar om att förstå omvärlden, identifiera möjligheter och utmaningar och skapa en gemensam riktning för vår gemenskap framåt. För Wikimedia Sverige var det viktigt att processen skulle präglas av samma värden som föreningen arbetar för varje dag: öppenhet, delaktighet och samarbete.

title: BREAKING: Everything
content: A few hours ago, I went to rent a Lime bike to ride the ten minutes to my therapy appointment. I opened Lime, scanned the QR code, and double clicked my iPhone’s side button to authorize Apple Pay. The app hung for a few moments, then closed. I tried several more times and the same thing happened. In the back of my mind, I wondered what was going on — was the Lime bike broken? Was my cell phone service out? Was it something else? I opened the Uber app and, similarly, wasn’t able to pay. I opened DownDetector and realized that the entirety of Apple Pay, a thing I thought existed only on my phone and not the cloud, was down. I texted my therapist, put my phone in my pocket, and started jogging.

title: Italy: “A bleak day for freedom of expression” as parliament votes through repressive definition of antisemitism into law
content:
Reacting to a vote by Italy’s parliament to formally adopt the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) working definition of antisemitism, Erika Guevara Rosas, Amnesty International’s Senior Director for Research, Policy, Advocacy and Campaigns, said: 

“Today marks a bleak day for freedom of expression as Italy explicitly makes the IHRA working definition of antisemitism legally binding. The new law, based on a definition that has long raised serious concerns because it conflates antisemitism with legitimate criticism of Israel, heightens the risk of far-reaching forms of censorship and self-censorship. Its application across schools, universities, social media platforms and beyond threatens a chilling effect and infringe on the rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly.

title: Revealed: Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia are largest CO2 exporters of all time
content:
Russia, Saudi Arabia and COP31 co-president Australia are the largest exporters of carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions in history, reveals Carbon Brief analysis.

Since 1850, the three nations – and other major fossil-fuel exporters – have exported hundreds of billions of tonnes of CO2 in the form of gas, oil and coal that has been burned in other countries.

Carbon Brief’s analysis of extraction-based CO2 emissions is based on figures compiled by Robbie Andrew, a senior researcher at Norwegian climate institute CICERO.

It shows that Australia is responsible for more than twice as much global warming when including emissions from its fossil-fuel exports, while Saudi Arabia has caused more than four times as much.

Australia has been under pressure for continuing to expand its fossil-fuel production ahead of the UN climate summit in Antalya, where it is co-president with host nation Turkey.

Membership

In contrast, nations that are heavily reliant on energy imports – such as Japan or Germany – are responsible for far lower shares of planet-warming emissions, if responsibility passes to fossil-fuel producers.

title: The Justice Department Wants To Give Patent Trolls More Power
content:
Software patents are mostly vague, hard to define, and widely abused. Most tech patent lawsuits aren’t filed by companies that make real products. They’re filed by patent trolls, companies that acquire patents to extract payments through litigation and legal threats. 

A patent on one feature of a smartphone shouldn’t give the patent owner the power to threaten the existence of the entire product line. But that is exactly the leverage patent trolls want—and the current administration is helping them to get it. 

In two recent patent cases, Radian Memory Systems v. Samsung and Collision Communications v. Samsung, the Justice Department and the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office have asked courts to make it easier for patent owners to get injunctions. These are judicial orders that can force companies to stop selling products or remove features from them, rather than simply pay monetary damages.

title: Baha’i Citizen Mobin Hosseini Arrested After Appearing at Sari Prosecutor’s Office
content:
According to HRANA, Mobin Hosseini, a Baha’i citizen residing in Sari, was arrested today, Tuesday, November 17, 2026.

Based on information received by HRANA, Hosseini attended an interrogation session today at the Sari Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office, where he defended himself against charges including “propaganda against the regime.” He was arrested following the conclusion of the session.

Hosseini had previously been arrested at his home on October 11, 2026, by agents of the IRGC Intelligence Organization, who reportedly beat him and took him into custody without presenting a judicial warrant. He was released several hours later. During the incident, the agents also verbally and physically assaulted him and confiscated his mobile phone.

At the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding any additional charges that may have been brought against Mobin Hosseini or his current place of detention.

title: Advania Finland syventää yhteistyötään Microsoftin kanssa vauhdittaakseen pilvitransformaatiota ja tekoälyn hyödyntämistä
content:
Advania Finland on solminut Microsoftin kanssa Data Center Optimization (DCO) -yhteistyösopimuksen. Yhteistyö vahvistaa Advanian kykyä auttaa asiakkaitaan hyödyntämään Microsoft Azure -pilvipalveluita, modernisoimaan hybridiympäristöjä sekä ottamaan käyttöön data- ja tekoälyratkaisuja turvallisesti ja kustannustehokkaasti.

Yhteistyön myötä Advania tarjoaa asiakkailleen entistä kattavampaa asiantuntemusta pilvitransformaatioiden suunnitteluun ja toteutukseen, hybridiympäristöjen modernisointiin, Azure-arkkitehtuurien kehittämiseen sekä data- ja tekoälyratkaisujen käyttöönottoon.

Tavoitteena on auttaa organisaatioita rakentamaan liiketoiminnan tarpeita palvelevia IT-ympäristöjä ja samalla hyödyntämään hallitusti pilven tarjoamaa joustavuutta, suorituskykyä ja mahdollisuuksia innovaatioihin.

”DCO-yhteistyö Microsoftin kanssa vahvistaa kyvykkyyttämme ja tukee strategiaamme auttaa asiakkaitamme modernisoimaan IT-ympäristöjään. Pilvipalveluiden, datan ja tekoälyn merkitys kasvaa nopeasti, ja haluamme varmistaa, että asiakkaamme pystyvät hyödyntämään niiden tarjoamia mahdollisuuksia turvallisesti ja tehokkaasti”, sanoo Advania Finlandin toimitusjohtaja Janne Ahonen.

title: Komission työohjelma 2027: “Euroopan unioni – yhdessä toistemme tukena”
content:
Euroopan komissio on jälleen linjannut tulevan vuoden poliittiset tavoitteensa ja keskeiset aloitteensa tuoreessa työohjelmassaan, jonka otsikko kuuluu: Euroopan unioni – yhdessä toistemme tukena. Vuoden 2027 työohjelmassa korostuvat erityisesti Euroopan kilpailukyvyn ja strategisen itsenäisyyden vahvistaminen sekä sääntelyn yksinkertaistaminen, jonka edistymistä arvioidaan myös työohjelman yhteydessä julkaistussa vuoden 2026 yksinkertaistamisraportissa. Uusien lainsäädäntöaloitteiden määrän vähentyessä komissio suuntaa huomionsa entistä vahvemmin aiemmin esitettyjen aloitteiden edistämiseen ja toimeenpanoon.

Komission 4.11. julkaisema työohjelma jatkaa johdonmukaisesti von der Leyenin toimikauden alussa asetettujen prioriteettien edistämistä. Työohjelmassa korostuvat Euroopan kilpailukyvyn, taloudellisen turvallisuuden ja strategisen riippumattomuuden vahvistaminen etenkin sääntelyn yksinkertaistamisen ja toimeenpanemisen, teollisuuden kilpailukyvyn parantamisen ja sisämarkkinoiden syventämisen kautta. Turvallisuus ja puolustus säilyvät keskeisinä painopisteinä, vaikka niihin liittyviä uusia aloitteita on vähän.

title: Musiikin arvo -videosarja huipentuu Free Carmeniin: avoimen haun kautta mukaan valittu yhtye tähtää maailmalle
content:
Musiikin arvo -videosarjan tavoitteena on tehdä näkyväksi musiikin julkaisemisen taustalla työskenteleviä ihmisiä sekä sitä, kuinka monen ammattilaisen osaamisesta valmis äänite syntyy. Sarjan viimeisessä kokonaisuudessa seurataan kansainvälistä uraa rakentavan Free Carmenin (Veeti Mäkinen, Onni Leminen, Roope Kaunisharju ja Ukko Vuorela) matkaa uuden Beekeeping-EP:n julkaisuun.  

Vaihtoehtorockista, folkista ja amerikkalaisesta juurimusiikista ammentava yhtye valittiin mukaan avoimen Open call -haun kautta. Hakuun saapui yhteensä 62 hakemusta niin itsenäisiltä artisteilta kuin levy-yhtiöiden edustuksessa olevilta yhtyeiltä ja artisteilta. 

– Free Carmenin erotti muiden hakijoiden joukosta heidän kunnianhimoinen ja ammattimainen otteensa sekä aidosti kansainväliset tavoitteensa. Samalla yhtyeen tarina havainnollistaa erinomaisesti sitä, kuinka suuren joukon ihmisiä yhden musiikkijulkaisun taustalla työskentelee. Juuri tätä haluamme Musiikin arvo -sarjassa tehdä näkyväksi, sanoo Gramexin viestintäpäällikkö Noora Marttila. 

Sarjan ensimmäinen jakso julkaistaan Gramexin Instagram-, TikTok- ja YouTube-kanavilla tiistaina 17. marraskuuta, minkä jälkeen uusia jaksoja ilmestyy joka viikko.

title: The Guardian view on climate and debt: a vicious cycle the world must break at Cop31 | Editorial
content:
Poor countries are paying creditors instead of preparing for climate disasters. The international financial system must stop deepening their vulnerability

The catastrophe that struck Nepal’s Himalayas in August began with a collapsing glacier. An avalanche of ice and rock unleashed deadly floods, sweeping away villages, bridges and roads, and leaving thousands dead or missing. It illustrated the dangers posed by global heating to the Himalayas’ increasingly unstable glaciers. Nepal lost a tenth of its electricity generation. Reconstruction will cost about $5bn. Yet the Loss and Damage Fund, hailed as a historic breakthrough at the 2022 UN climate summit, has earmarked just $20m for Nepal – less than 5% of the $482m that Kathmandu must pay its external public creditors this year.

title: Call for Papers – Seminar: Urban Research in Biological and Environmental Sciences
content:
We invite all researchers to submit presentation proposals for the research seminar Urban Research in Biological and Environmental Sciences, which will take place on December 11, 2026, at the University of Helsinki. The aim of the seminar is to explore urban issues and cities from the perspectives of various branches of biological and environmental sciences and to offer a multidisciplinary forum for researchers engaged in urban studies.

Urban research is a central aspect of disciplines in the biological and environmental sciences, including urban ecology, environmental science, and conservation biology. Urban spaces shape ecosystems, biodiversity, and the living conditions of both humans and other organisms. The seminar will focus on the following three themes:

  • Biodiversity – Species, habitats, and ecological diversity in urban environments
  • Pollution and environmental quality – Contaminants, air and water quality, and their effects on organisms and ecosystems in cities
  • Environmental Change – Environmental pressures and adaptation in urban spaces, such as climate change, pollution, and land-use change

title: Azerbaijan Jails Parliamentary Watchdog Activists
content:
An Azerbaijani court sentenced two activists affiliated with Meclis.info, an independent platform monitoring the country’s parliament, to lengthy prison terms on dubious financial crime charges on November 12, 2026. These are the latest convictions as part of a wider crackdown that has seen scores of journalists, human rights defenders, and civic activists prosecuted on politically motivated charged since late 2023.

The Baku Grave Crimes Court sentenced Imran Aliyev, Meclis.info’s co-founder, to 10 years in prison, and Elgiz Gahraman, another co-founder and data analyst, to nine years. A third defendant, the platform’s accountant Tamella Musayeva, received a suspended prison sentence. All three were convicted of illegal entrepreneurship, money laundering, currency smuggling, tax evasion, and document forgery.

Launched in 2023, Meclis.info published analyses of Azerbaijan's parliament, scrutinizing lawmakers’ attendance, voting records, and public statements. Aliyev has been in detention since his arrest in April 2024. Gahraman and Musayeva were placed under police supervision in February 2025; Gahraman was taken into custody in the courtroom after the verdict.

title: Le vol des cygnes – A Concert with the Mirjam Helin Academy
content:
Le vol des cygnes – A Concert with the Mirjam Helin Academy
Wednesday, 2 December 2026 | 8pm

Through a dialogue between musical traditions and cultural heritage, Institut finlandais invites you to discover Le vol des cygnes, a concert exploring themes of longing, roots and identity.

The concert dives into the connections between Finnish Romanticism and Italian and Argentine folk song traditions. Works by Sibelius, Berio, Ginastera and Pylkkänen take the audience on a musical journey through ideas of home, belonging and the search for identity, brought to life by three artists whose backgrounds span across multiple cultures.

The concert pays homage to Finnish soprano Aino Ackté (1876–1944), marking the 150th anniversary of her birth. One of the first Finnish opera singers to achieve major international recognition, Ackté made her mark during her years in Paris, from 1894 to 1903, which were decisive in establishing her European reputation and launching her international career.

In honour of her legacy, the artists will perform Höstkväll by Jean Sibelius, a work dedicated to Ackté, thereby following in the footsteps of her international career, which began in Paris.

title: Tietoisku kirjastosta — Kirjasto ei vaadi eikä valikoi
content:
Tietoisku kirjastosta – Kirjasto ei vaadi eikä valikoi -video muistuttaa, että kirjasto on kaikille. Kirjastoon saa tulla kuka tahansa, eikä tulosyytä tai taustaa tarvitse selittää.

Arjessa meitä lähestytään jatkuvasti vaatimuksilla: joku myy, joku kysyy, joku haluaa jotain. Kirjasto on poikkeus, sillä sinne saa tulla ilman selittelyjä, eikä kukaan kysy, miksi tulit. Kirjasto edistää jokaisen yhdenvertaisia mahdollisuuksia sivistykseen ja kulttuuriin, ja kirjastoon ovat tervetulleita kaikki.

Tämä video on osa Tietoisku kirjastosta -sarjaa, jota tuottavat yhdessä Kirjastokaista ja Suomen kirjastoseura yhteistyössä yleisten kirjastojen kanssa.

Tietoisku kirjastosta -sarja nostaa esiin kirjastojen näkökulmia ajankohtaisiin ja yhteisiin asioihin sekä ihmisten arkeen. Yle on esittänyt kanavillaan klassikoiksi muodostuneita tietoiskuja, joissa on muistutettu ja opastettu kansalaisia yhteiskunnallisesti tärkeissä asioissa, kuten turvallisuudessa, terveydessä ja arjen valinnoissa. Kirjastot herättävät tämän mainion kerronnan tavan henkiin omassa kontekstissaan ja tuottavat tietoiskuja kaikelle kansalle.

Videot tehdään yhteiseen käyttöön: katso ja jaa tietoiskuja kirjastosta!

title: Lämnade du in en ansökan i september?
content:
I september hade många av våra specialfonder ansökningstid och också många bidragsformer med specifika ändamål. Vi fick över 2 000 ansökningar och behandlingen av de flesta ansökningar är ännu i full gång.

De allra flesta som lämnade in en ansökan i september måste vänta på besked till mitten av december.

Då beslutar Kulturfondens styrelse om de nästan 1 200 ansökningar som lämnades in inom våra bidragsformer med österbottnisk eller nyländsk anknytning.

Redan i november kunde vår styrelse ta beslut om utdelningen inom en del bidragsformer med ansökningstid i september. Det här gäller:

  • residensstipendier
  • lärlingsstipendier
  • journaliststipendier
  • systrarna Standertskjölds stipendier
  • rekreation för äldre i Åboland
  • renoveringsbidrag för föreningshus
  • Hallå! Språkprojekt
  • förbundspaket
  • bidrag för resor till Skolmusik och Stafettkarnevalen

    • Om du lämnade in en ansökan inom någon av de här bidragsformerna har du redan fått mejlbesked.

    Om du däremot ännu inte fått besked på ansökan du gjorde i september måste du vänta till mitten av december.

    Du minns väl att du kan ansöka också inom vår allmänna ansökningstid i november även om du inte fått besked på ansökan du lämnade in i september.

title: British Hacker Admits Breaching Uber, Revolut and Rockstar
content:
A member of the notorious Lapsus$ cybercrime group pleaded guilty on Monday to hacking several major international companies, including Uber, Revolut and Rockstar Games, the developer of the Grand Theft Auto video game franchise.

Arion Kurtaj, 21, formerly of Oxfordshire, admitted six offenses at Woolwich Crown Court in London, including computer misuse, fraud and possessing an unauthorized mobile phone in prison. He is due to be sentenced on November 23.

Prosecutors said Kurtaj was involved in a series of cyberattacks between 2021 and 2022 that compromised customer and employee information, disrupted corporate systems and resulted in the theft and publication of commercially sensitive material.

“Arion Kurtaj used sophisticated hacking techniques to carry out a sustained campaign of cyberattacks, causing serious disruption to major international business and putting sensitive information at risk,” said Robert Hutchinson, a specialist prosecutor with the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).

title: When Jorge Luis Borges Co-Wrote a Surreal Sci-Fi Noir Film: Invasión (1969)
content: “La ciudad es más que la gente.” So declares a character called Don Porfirio in Invasión, the debut feature by Argentine director Hugo Santiago. The line is the film’s most memorable, not least because of the reversal it pulls on our expectations. Saying that a city is really its people must have been a somewhat banal observation even in 1969, when Invasión came out, but saying that a city is more than its people still sounds contrarian enough to be intriguing. It’s even more compelling coming from Don Porfirio, a mastermind whose intensely abstracted manner and refined literary diction will remind some viewers of no figure so much as Jorge Luis Borges — and as well he might, since Borges co-wrote the script.

title: Dutch resist ‘unacceptable’ US bid to tighten semiconductor export controls
content:
BRUSSELS — The Netherlands has pushed back against a U.S. congressional bid to tighten restrictions on exports of advanced chipmaking equipment to China, warning that Washington’s attempt to dictate the rules for Dutch companies such as ASML is unacceptable.

The Dutch objections come as the proposed MATCH Act gains fresh momentum in Washington following revelations about Nvidia’s former chief executive Jensen Huang and his links to a suspected Chinese spy, intensifying concerns in Congress about Beijing’s access to advanced U.S. technology.

The bipartisan legislation would give U.S. allies, including the Netherlands and Japan, 150 days to align restrictions on sales and servicing of advanced chipmaking equipment to China with those imposed by Washington, or show progress toward doing so. If they fail to comply, the U.S. Commerce Department would be required to extend American export controls unilaterally to equipment supplied from those countries.

“The main concern is the bill’s extraterritorial character,” a spokesperson for the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs told POLITICO on Tuesday.

title: Tasavallan presidentti Alexander Stubbin puhe Walther-Rathenau-palkinnon jakotilaisuudessa Berliinissä 17. marraskuuta 2026
content:

Muutosvarauksin

Herra presidentti,

Aluksi haluan vilpittömästi kiittää presidentti Gauckia hänen ystävällisistä sanoistaan. Minulle on suuri kunnia vastaanottaa Walther-Rathenau-palkinto.

Otan palkinnon vastaan kiitollisena sekä Suomen puolesta että kaikkien niiden puolesta, jotka uskovat. etteivät rauha, vapaus ja kansainvälinen yhteistyö ole itsestäänselvyyksiä. Ne ovat valintoja, jotka jokaisen sukupolven on tehtävä uudelleen.

Walther Rathenau ymmärsi tämän. Hän oli monessa mielessä eurooppalainen jo ennen kuin Eurooppa oli olemassa sellaisena kuin me sen nykyään tunnemme. Hän ymmärsi, että vauraus edellyttää avoimuutta, turvallisuus yhteistyötä ja demokratia vastuullisuutta.

Nämä ajatukset muovasivat Eurooppaa 1900-luvulla. Ne ovat yhtä tärkeitä 2000-luvulla.

Elämme parhaillaan syvällisen murroksen aikaa. Saksassa on sille oma sana: Zeitenwende. Tämä osuva sana on vakiintunut kansainväliseen sanastoon samaan tapaan kuin Schadenfreude, Zeitgeist ja Kindergarten. Suomesta vain yksi sana on saavuttanut vastaavan maailmanlaajuisen menestyksen: sauna.

Mutta Zeitenwende on paljon enemmän kuin vain sana. Se on kuvaus ajastamme.

title: Nuoret arkkitehdit vievät suomalaista kiertotalousosaamista maailmalle apurahan turvin
content:
Bryggman-apuraha luovutettiin Turun Sampotalossa 17.11. järjestetyssä tilaisuudessa.

Heljä Nieminen ja Havu Järvelä perustivat yhdessä Keltaisen toimiston vuonna 2021. Kaksikko on menestynyt arkkitehtuurikilpailuissa: he sijoittuivat toiseksi muun muassa Trondheimin taidemuseon (2025) ja Keran hallien uudelleenkäytön (2023) kilpailuissa ja jakoivat kolmannen sijan Sara Hildénin taidemuseon kilpailussa (2021).

Apurahan turvin arkkitehdit osallistuvat kolmeen kilpailuun, joiden tehtävät sopivat kiertotalousratkaisujen kehittämiseen. Kilpailut valitaan myöhemmin. Kilpailutöissä tarkastellaan rakennuskannan ja rakennusosien uudelleenkäyttöä, rakennusten muuntojoustavuutta ja ehjänä purettavuutta sekä vähähiilisten materiaalien arkkitehtonisia mahdollisuuksia.

Suomessa avoimet arkkitehtuurikilpailut ovat perinteisesti olleet nuorille tekijöille väylä uudistaa alaa.

“Haluamme kehittää kiertotalousratkaisuja kilpailuissa, koska niissä voi soveltaa uusinta tutkimustietoa vapaasti. Toteutusratkaisut ovat vielä auki”, Nieminen sanoo.

Kaksikon mukaan Keski-Euroopassa ollaan Suomea selvästi edellä monissa kiertotalouden ratkaisuissa, esimerkiksi rakennusosien laajamittaisessa uudelleenkäytössä.

title: Herneen viljelyala nousi yli 50 000 hehtaariin
content:
Suomalaiset peltoviljelijät uudistavat tuotantoaan, ja herneen viljelyala nousi yli 50 000 hehtaariin, tiedottaa Maa- ja Metsätaloustuottajain Keskusliitto (MTK). 

Peltoviljelyn kannattavuus on edelleen Suomessa heikkoa. Vuonna 2026 peltoalaa siirtyi muun muassa valkuais- ja öljykasveille, ja viljakasvien ala pieneni noin seitsemän prosenttia.

MTK:n mukaan peltokasvien monipuolistaminen avaa mahdollisuuksia, mutta niiden hyödyntäminen edellyttää toimivia markkinoita ja yhteistyötä koko ruokaketjulta. Huoltovarmuus ja kotimainen ruoantuotanto säilyvät vain, jos niiden perustana on kannattavat maatilat, järjestö vetoaa.

"Kulunut kasvukausi osoitti, että viljelijät ovat valmiita vaihtamaan perinteisiä viljakasveja muihin tuotantokasveihin ja haluavat vahvistaa kotimaisen kasvivalkuaisen tuotantoa. Myös näiden kasvien tuottamisen on kuitenkin oltava taloudellisesti kannattavaa", MTK:n asiantuntija Max Schulman toteaa tiedotteessa.

title: Ukraine’s drone war never belonged to Fedorov, says defence entrepreneur
content:
Most wounded soldiers on Ukraine’s front lines are now hit by drones. Fedir Serdiuk, co-founder of defence company MOWA, tells EU Perspectives that Ukraine is ready to join Europe’s defence market. What it lacks are practical ways in.

EU Perspectives first spoke to Mr Serdiuk in April about what the EU can learn from Ukraine’s battlefields. Much has changed since. In July, President Volodymyr Zelensky dismissed Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, and in August Ukraine’s parliament appointed Yevhen Khmara in his place.

We spoke again shortly before the Abu Dhabi peace talks of 10–11 November. For Brussels, his message is clear. “Ukraine is absolutely ready to be integrated with EU defence market and defence space but now it’s a U-turn to find practical and measurable tracks to integrate both industrial-wise.”

It’s been four and a half years since the large-scale invasion by Russia started, and it’s for me every day is a gift. Because it’s the formidable power and very serious military power that Russia presents. Also very brutal and capable, unfortunately, with a lot of resources. So being able to defend as good as we are doing this is itself a very good, a very good scenario.
snippet: Most wounded soldiers on Ukraine’s front lines are now hit by drones. Fedir Serdiuk, co-founder of defence company MOWA, tells EU Perspectives that Ukraine is ready to join Europe’s defence market.

title: Kochi, from the inside: what it really takes to run WikiConference India 2026
content:
Most people meet a conference on its first morning: a badge, a lanyard, a full hall. I met WikiConference India 2026 six months earlier, in shared documents full of page drafts, translations and questions that still needed answers. By the time I landed in Kochi, the conference already felt like something I had helped build.

From 4 to 6 September 2026, with arrivals and a pre-conference day on 3 September, Wikimedians gathered in Kochi, Kerala, under the theme Reimagining the Knowledge Commons and the subtheme Community Leadership in an Evolving Wikimedia Ecosystem. I took part on a full scholarship, as a Core Team Member of the Communications Sub-team, as an on-site volunteer, and as a lightning-talk speaker. This is my account of those three days, and of the months of quiet work that came before them.

Euroopan unionin yhtenäisyyttä on viime vuosina haastettu monin tavoin. Kallistuva energia, nuorten korkeat työttömyysluvut ja ylipäätään kasautuvat sosiaaliset ongelmat ovat vahvistaneet poliittisen kentän äärilaitoja, joille eurooppalainen yhteistyö on perinteisesti ollut vastustuksen kohde. Nämä populistiset voimat suhtautuvat kriittisesti myös Ukrainan tukemiseen.

Kansainvälisillä kentillä EU sääntöpohjaiseen järjestelmään perustuvana yhteisönä joutuu kilpailemaan autokraattisten järjestelmien kanssa. Tuohon voimankäyttöä korostavaan joukkoon on presidentti Trumpin kaudella valitettavasti ajautunut myös unionin tärkein liittolainen Yhdysvallat. Eurooppalaisen päätöksenteon avoimuus tarjoaa tilaisuuden myös unionin ulkopuolelta tulevalle vihamieliselle vaikuttamiselle.

Euroopan unionin päätöksenteko ja lakien säätäminen on kolmen instituution varassa. Komission, neuvoston ja parlamentin lisäksi on myös neuvoa-antavat elimet, Euroopan alueiden komitea sekä talous- ja sosiaalikomitea. title: Rare sighting: European leaders at COP31
content: Last week, we introduced you to the creatures of COP31. Today, we zoom in on a species that seems to be slowly going extinct at the global climate conference: the European leader. Habitat: under threat. In 2025, the world saw an extreme weather event every day on average, according to the Climate Risk Index. Spain ranked third among those most affected, and France, Italy, and Romania also made the top 20. In European cities, 50,000 people are estimated to have died from heat this summer alone. title: A Federal Women’s Prison Became a “Rape Club.” After Officials Shut It Down, Rampant Abuse Continued Elsewhere.
content:
Officer Felix Wilder sauntered around the women’s prison like he owned the place. 

Prone to showing up to work in gold chains and stylish jeans instead of his concrete gray government uniform, the slender 35-year-old moved, one woman said, “like he had just gotten off of a horse from a long ride.” He spoke slowly and eyed the prisoners as they walked through the drab buildings and shadeless yards of the secluded federal lockup in Aliceville, Alabama.

By the fall of 2024, some of the women there had begun to notice him hovering over a soft-spoken immigrant from Mexico who’d been in prison for only a few years. Ela, as she asked to be called, had dark hair, dark eyes and children to get home to back in Utah. Wilder was just a little too close, a little too familiar.

Ela’s cellmate, who asked to be identified as Ana, watched it all with unease. At 40, she knew exactly what that kind of attention from an officer could mean in a women’s prison.
snippet: Officer Felix Wilder sauntered around the women’s prison like he owned the place.

title: In win against impunity, Indonesian court orders the reform of Military Justice Law
content:
The court ruled that soldiers who committed criminal offenses should be tried by civilian courts

Originally published on Global Voices

Constitutional Court of Indonesia in Jakarta. Photo by Christophe95. Wikipedia. CC BY-SA 4.0

This post is part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “Justice as infrastructure.” In this Spotlight, Global Voices is partnering with The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law (HiiL) to highlight the ways justice functions as critical infrastructure for any society. You can support this coverage by donating here.

Indonesia’s Constitutional Court ruled that the 1997 Military Justice Law would be invalid unless amended within two years. The decision was hailed by human rights groups because it means soldiers who commit crimes can be tried in civilian courts.

Article 9 of the Military Justice Law requires active-duty personnel of the Indonesian National Armed Forces to be held accountable exclusively under the military justice system, even when they commit ordinary criminal offenses and human rights violations.

title: An atlas of vanished places: how climate change is rewriting the books on our shelves
content:
On August 26, 2026, a huge mass of rock and ice broke away at an altitude of around 5,200 metres in the Himalayas. Within minutes, it became an avalanche of debris and water that hurtled down towards the Nepal-Tibet border, with such force that the seismic signals were initially mistaken for an earthquake.

The region’s glaciers are visibly retreating, and thawing permafrost may well have contributed to destabilising these Himalayan slopes. Above all, the Nepal landslide illustrates something that will only become increasingly familiar: places that appear stable can change almost without warning.

While events like the Nepal landslide have an immediate, devastating impact on the people who live in these environments, they also leave their mark in a less obvious sphere: literature.

Biologist Rachel Carson’s 1951 book The Sea Around Us reminded readers that the boundary between land and sea has never been stable. Throughout our planet’s very long history, the oceans have advanced and receded. What makes the current situation exceptional is the speed of this transformation, as well as human activity’s decisive contribution to it.

title: Fighting in Yemen has made crossing the Bab el-Mandeb even more dangerous – jeopardizing aid and refuge for millions
content:
In recent days, Iran-backed Houthi forces have gained greater control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a vital hub of trade, travel and migration between the Middle East and Africa.

The partial closing of the Strait of Hormuz as part of the war in Iran – and escalating conflicts in Yemen, Ethiopia and Eritrea – had already brought this narrow waterway into new global prominence. Control over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait remains critical to military operations and commodity markets throughout the region.

However, the Bab el-Mandeb’s strategic geopolitical and commercial shipping importance has largely overshadowed its role as a critical humanitarian corridor.

Bab el-Mandeb means “gate of lamentation” or, more poetically, “gate of tears” in Arabic. It remains one of the most dangerous migration passages in the world. Last year, more than 900 people died or went missing trying to cross. In October 2026, a boat capsized off the coast of Djibouti carrying nearly 300 people, many of whom were escaping violence and persecution.

title: Komissio kovistelee Ranskaa Belgiaa velasta ja alijäämistä
content:
EU-komissio patistaa Ranskaa ja Belgiaa laskemaan julkisia velkojaan ja julkisen talouden alijäämiään.

EU:n talouskomissaari Valdis Dombrovskis kommentoi Ranskan ja Belgian tilanteita julkistaessaan komission talousennusteen tiistaina.

EU:n taloussääntöjen mukaan julkisen velan määrä ei saisi ylittää 60:tä prosenttia maan bruttokansantuotteesta eikä julkisen talouden alijäämä kolmea prosenttia bruttokansantuotteesta.

Ranskalla ja Belgialla molemmat mittarit ylittyvät selvästi.

KOMISSIO arvioi, että Ranskan – EU:n toiseksi suurimman talouden – julkisen velan määrä suhteessa bruttokansantuotteeseen on tänä vuonna yli 119 prosenttia. Ranskan julkisen talouden alijäämäksi komissio arvioi tänä vuonna 5,5 prosenttia bruttokansantuotteesta.

Belgian julkisen velan määrä suhteessa bruttokansantuotteeseen on komission mukaan tänä vuonna reilut 111 prosenttia. Belgian julkisen talouden alijäämäksi komissio arvioi tänä vuonna 5,2 prosenttia bruttokansantuotteesta.

Dombrovskis sanoi tiedotustilaisuudessaan, että Ranskan ja Belgian valtion velkakirjoille näyttää edelleen olevan kysyntää, joten välitöntä uhkaa maiden rahoitusvakaudelle ei näyttäisi olevan.

title: As U.S. Boycotts U.N. Climate Talks, California Leads State/City Efforts to Combat Climate Crisis
content:
For the second year in a row, the Trump administration has not sent an official delegation to the United Nations’ annual climate change conference, held this year in Antalya, Turkey. But although no federal representatives are present, more than 120 U.S. state and local leaders are participating, including the governor of the fourth-largest economy in the world, California Governor Gavin Newsom. Newsom, a likely candidate for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, has endorsed the Santa Marta Process, a coalition of nations working to develop a global green energy transition.

“The petrostates have made it abundantly clear: Under the current rules of consensus, they are never, ever going to allow COPs to succeed. They’re just not going to sign that agreement. So, essentially, the Santa Marta coalition is making an end run around that, using economic power,” says longtime environmental and climate reporter Mark Hertsgaard.

title: The Paramount-Warner Brothers Deal Could Usher in Another Age of Lost Media
content:
There are all sorts of reasons to be against the merger of Paramount and Warner Brothers-Discovery. There's the obvious problem of increasing concentration in the already pretty-concentrated film and TV industry. People have problems with Paramount's owner Skydance interfering  with its news coverage and late night comedy. But one of the biggest is the way we are losing choice and access to information and culture.  

In the context of the digital world, there are two major problems with these mega mergers. One, as we've said in the past, is that it further degrades the already awful state of mainstream streaming services. In short, by increasing the amount of legacy content under their control, major studios don't have to invest in either new content or well-engineered services to get users. Plus, they can pool the data they have on users together in an increasing assault on consumer privacy. A monthly subscription and more information about your habits and interests? Win-win for them.

title: Kurdistan Province: Nine Suspects Arrested by Ministry of Intelligence Agents on Security-Related Charges
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mehr News Agency, the Ministry of Intelligence announced in a statement that it had arrested nine individuals on security-related charges in Kurdistan Province.

According to the statement, the detainees are accused of “membership in separatist groups and organizing armed activities aimed at creating insecurity in Kurdistan Province.”

The Ministry of Intelligence also announced the arrest of a key leader of these groups who, according to the ministry, had been residing abroad. The statement alleged that the individual, acting under the direction of a regional intelligence service, was responsible for establishing and leading an armed network in Kamyaran County.

The statement further claimed that firearms and 70 Starlink communication devices had been discovered and confiscated from the suspects.

The ministry’s statement did not disclose the identities of those arrested, the exact dates of their arrests, or their current places of detention.

title: ICC: Afghanistan Decision Risks Narrowing Access to Justice
content:
(The Hague) – An International Criminal Court (ICC) decision risks hindering a path to justice for victims of grave crimes committed in Afghanistan, Human Rights Watch said today. On November 12, 2026, an ICC pretrial chamber, citing a lack of activity, effectively closed the court’s situation dealing with crimes by US, Afghan government, and other forces prior to the Taliban’s August 2021 takeover.

The ICC prosecutor’s office on November 13 sought to appeal the decision and to seek a stay of the closure decision. Research by Human Rights Watch and others over many years has documented war crimes and crimes against humanity by the Taliban; the Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP), an ISIS-affiliated group; Afghan government forces; and US military and Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) forces.

“Victims of serious international crimes committed by warring parties during Afghanistan’s long conflict have faced many roadblocks to justice,” said Liz Evenson, international justice director at Human Rights Watch. “The ICC judges’ decision threatens to compound barriers to future accountability for US and Afghan government forces.”

title: AI-kahvit: Mitä tekoäly ei näe? Ihminen ja tekoäly yhdessä kirjaston työssä
content:
Tämä Teams-tallenne on osa AI-kahvit-sarjaa, jonka on tuottanut Yleisten kirjastojen tekoälyosaamisen kehittämishanke. AI-kahveilla pohditaan tällä kertaa, miten tekoälyä voi käyttää osana omaa työtä niin, että oma ajattelu, harkinta ja luovuus eivät jää taka-alalle, ja mitkä asiat halutaan pitää ihmisen käsissä.

Aiheesta puhuu kouluttaja Kira Sjöberg Goodinilta. Webinaari alkaa pienellä kokeilulla: osallistujat pyytävät tekoälyltä lukupiirisuosituksia ja tarkistavat vastaukset. Kokeilu näyttää, miksi tekoälyn vastaus voi kuulostaa varmalta, vaikka se ei pidä paikkaansa, ja miksi kaikki pitää tarkistaa. Sjöberg käsittelee, mitä tekoäly ei näe: hiljaista tietoa, puuttuvaa dataa (esimerkiksi pienet kielet ja paikallinen tieto) sekä sitä, miten samojen mallien käyttö voi yhdenmukaistaa sisältöjä. Hän pohtii, mitä työssä kannattaa pitää ihmisen käsissä (vastuu, harkinta ja kohtaaminen) ja miten tekoälyä voi käyttää hakukoneen sijaan ajattelukumppanina. Hän nostaa esiin myös kirjastoammattilaisten osaamisen tiedon järjestämisessä, jota tekoälyn aikakaudella tarvitaan yhä enemmän. Webinaari järjestettiin 17.11.2026.

title: Kyrgyz Man Sentenced to Three Years For Re-Posting Video on Facebook
content:
A Kyrgyzstan court has sentenced a construction worker and father of four children to three years in penal colony for a Facebook post that was critical of authorities. 

Baktybek Moldaliev, 48, was sentenced last week in the capital, Bishkek, on charges of “distribution of extremist materials.” The material in question is a video by the investigative media outlet Kloop, which he re-posted along with a comment.

While Moldaliev was convicted over the post he made in April, court files obtained by OCCRP show that Kyrgyz authorities had been collecting evidence against him for at least six months before that. 

Police searched Moldaliev’s apartment in November 2025, and brought him to the Ministry of Internal Affairs for questioning about his social media activity. The files do not show any charge against him at that time.

The Ministry of Internal Affairs did not respond to a request for comment.

Moldaliev was detained and questioned again on May 8, according to the files.

He told police: “I had been writing posts expressing my personal opinions on political and social issues occurring in the Kyrgyz Republic, specifically regarding the high cost of living, unemployment, and corruption.”

title: Watch Accurate Recreations of Medieval Italian Longsword Fighting Techniques, All Based on a Manuscript from 1404
content:
Given recent history, the prospect of hundreds of young men meeting on Facebook, then traveling from around the country to a central U.S. location might sound like reasonable cause for alarm. Yet a convention fitting that description had nothing to do with political violence but, rather, a celebration and appreciation of the name “Josh” (full disclosure: this writer did not attend). The gathering of the Joshes in April 2021 in Nebraska could not have been more peaceful, including its finishing battle royale, conducted with pool noodles.

The Joshes had no concern for proper pool-noodle-wielding technique, if there is such a thing. But groups of people who gather around the country to stage medieval-style battles in live-action role playing (LARP) games with weapons both real and fake might benefit from pointers.

So, too, might those who choreograph sword fights on stage and screen. Where can serious historical re-creators learn how to wield a real blade in historically accurate combat? One resource can be found at Wiktenauer, a wiki devoted to collecting “all of the primary and secondary source literature that makes up the text of historical European Martial arts (HEMA) research.”

title: Irish regulator stops X training AI with data gathered by agents
content:
Ireland’s privacy regulator has forced X to stop feeding AI models with data collected by its agents, the authority told POLITICO.

The social media giant owned by Elon Musk has suspended the use of so-called third-party data collected by its Grok Bot AI agent, which started mining this data in late October to train its AI systems.

The Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC) raised “significant concerns” about that data processing in recent weeks, Commissioner Dale Sunderland told POLITICO in an interview. “We asked them to suspend the processing, and they’ve confirmed to us today that they’ve done that,” he said Monday.

X did not respond to a request for comment.

The Irish privacy authority is the most powerful in Europe, as it enforces Europe’s data protection rulebook on companies that have their regional headquarters in Ireland, including Apple, Google, Meta, X and OpenAI.

The X action is a test case as privacy regulators shift their focus from AI training that uses data people have shared about themselves, to third-party data that personal AI agents are accessing and gathering on other people.
snippet: Ireland’s privacy regulator has forced X to stop feeding AI models with data collected by its agents, the authority told POLITICO.

title: ‘Promise without money protects noone.’ Climate-hit health systems get a third of what they need
content:
A new global alliance launched at COP31 will bring together climate and health research funders, as countries face pressure to turn promises into action.

Forty-eight developing countries say they need $3.3bn (approx. €3.0bn) a year to prepare their health systems for climate change. In 2024, international finance covered less than 34 per cent of those needs, according to the 2026 Lancet Countdown report. At the UN climate summit in Antalya (COP31), the EU’s new health pledge is aimed at research.

On 13 November, the European Commission launched the Multilateral Initiative on Climate & Health Research Funding with the Wellcome Trust and public research funders from five continents. The Commission calls it the first global alliance of funders dedicated to climate and health research.

The pressure in Antalya is to deliver, not to promise. “COP31 must be the COP of implementation,” says Brazil’s Health Minister Alexandre Padilha, whose country hosted last year’s summit. “More than making political commitments, we need to turn them into concrete actions.”
snippet: A new global alliance launched at COP31 will bring together climate and health research funders, as countries face pressure to turn promises into action.
