title: How an AI Content Mill Put a Real Musician Through Copyright Hell
content:
When writer and musician Samantha Shokin noticed her cover of a public domain Bulgarian folk song had been copyright struck on YouTube, she assumed it would be easy to fix. It wasn’t. And trying to figure out what happened led her to discover an AI content mill that is running 500 slop-filled channels and abusing YouTube’s automated copyright detectors.

“Any human would agree with me that there’s something clearly wrong here that needs to be fixed, but I can’t get in touch with a human being,” Shokin said.

Shokin’s journey is a modern nightmare that highlights the ways AI can be weaponized against human creators, and the ways people fall through the cracks of big tech’s automated systems.

During the pandemic, Shokin recorded a 50 second version of the Bulgarian folk song ‘Bre Petrunko’ and uploaded it to SoundCloud, where it didn’t get much traction. Two years later, she uploaded it to YouTube and watched as her cover grew in popularity, gaining 125,000 views in four years.

title: Can EU Action Against TikTok Rabbit Holes Lead to Real Social Media Design Change?
content:
The European Union’s executive preliminarily found TikTok in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) for failing to adequately assess and mitigate the risk of users falling into rabbit holes that could harm their well-being. The Commission particularly raised concern about young users’ and vulnerable adults’ repeated exposure to content that can negatively affect people’s mental health. 

The TikTok case is the latest investigation by the EU under the Digital Services Act, focusing on the platform’s alleged issues with harmful rabbit holes created by design in its highly personalized ‘For You’ feed. It signals that regulators are finally demanding fundamental changes to the inherently toxic design shared by many of the leading social media platforms. It is time to stop tinkering around the edges and set out clear rules for a safer, rights-respecting tech landscape.

title: Global Warming Approaches 1.5 Degrees in "Calamity for the World's Ecosystems"
content:
As delegates, industry lobbyists and civil society activists attend this year’s United Nations climate summit, known as COP31, we speak with international environmental lawyer Farhana Yamin about the state of global climate efforts. Yamin helped write the landmark 2015 Paris Agreement and has attended 28 of the last 31 U.N. climate summits. The Paris Agreement aimed to keep global temperatures below 1.5 degrees Celsius above preindustrial levels, a threshold that climate scientists say the world will now overshoot.

“It’s a moment of great sadness, actually, for the world community that we weren’t able to start the phaseout, start the acceleration of the transition away from fossil fuels 10 years earlier,” says Yamin. “So, we’re about 10 years behind, but I hope that over time that we can accelerate.”

title: Donate Equity to Support Digital Rights: Stocks, DAFs, and Giving
content:
Do the holidays have you thinking about how you can support your favorite nonprofit?  

For 35 years, the Electronic Frontier Foundation has been advancing our digital rights, including defending security researchers, encrypting the web, and fighting illegal surveillance. Donating equity to EFF can help support this important work. 

Perhaps your family has taken advantage of the new tax law around giving by creating a Donor-Advised Fund.  

Perhaps your employer has gone public and you now own stock.  

Perhaps you’ve seen some of EFF’s recent successes and thought, Man, imagine what they could do with more. 

A gift of equity can help your contribution go farther and offer tax savings. When you donate appreciated stock, you avoid paying capital gains tax on any increase in its value. You also receive a charitable income tax deduction for the fair market value of appreciated stock on the date it is transferred. Also, more and more companies are offering gift-matching programs that can double your impact at no additional cost.

title: Sähkön hinta voi moninkertaistua hetkessä – maksuton Virtanen-palvelu kertoo, mihin sähkö todella kuluu
content:
Talvi lähestyy, ja sähkön hinnan voimakas vaihtelu tekee kulutuksen ajoittamisesta taas ajankohtaista. Vuonna 2026 pörssisähkön kuukausikeskihinta on vaihdellut rajusti: heinäkuun 1,93 sentistä helmikuun 17,22 senttiin kilowattitunnilta. Vuorokauden sisäinen vaihtelu on vielä suurempaa. Marraskuun 2026 alussa päivän halvimman ja kalleimman vartin hinnan ero oli melkein satakertainen.

Nitorin data-analyytikkojen kehittämä kaikille avoin, maksuton Virtanen.ai-työkalu auttaa kotitalouksia ymmärtämään, mihin sähköä todella kuluu. Uutuutena palvelussa voi nyt verrata pörssisähkön ja kiinteähintaisen sopimuksen eroja. Virtasella voi myös selvittää, onko noin vuosi sitten käyttöön otettu varttihinnoittelu tullut omassa taloudessa halvemmaksi vai kalliimmaksi.

”Sähkön hinta saattaa moninkertaistua hetkessä. Virtasen avulla voi laskea helposti, minkälainen sähkösopimus olisi tällä hetkellä oman kulutuksen kohdalla kaikkein järkevin”, palvelun kehittämisestä vastannut Nitorin data-asiantuntija Esa Puttonen kertoo.

title: Liberia Lifts a Major Barrier to Education
content:
“Our children are able to go to school again.” That's how one Liberian parent described the impact of a new government policy banning school registration fees for kindergarten through sixth grade. The policy is already helping families who struggled to pay the fees, removing a longstanding barrier to their children's education.

Since the policy took effect in September, Liberian child advocates have interviewed parents in four counties to assess whether schools were complying with the ban. The findings offered encouraging early indications: nearly all 20 parents interviewed knew about the policy and had enrolled their children without paying registration fees.

Parents described the difference the policy was making. “The decision by the ministry is so good,” said a parent in Bong County. “It enables our children to go to school free without worry.” Another parent whose children had previously been out of school said, “For some of us that don’t have money, it helps us a lot.”

title: Switzerland is Prosecuting the First Journalist Under its Banking Secrecy Law. The EU Has No Comment.
content:
The unprecedented criminal prosecution of a journalist under Switzerland's stringent banking secrecy law is raising alarms among press freedom advocates across Europe. But the European Union has nothing to say about it.

Lukas Hässig, founder of the financial news website Inside Paradeplatz, was charged in October over articles published a decade ago. The articles cited leaked information, and focused on financial dealings involving former Raiffeisen Switzerland chief executive Pierin Vincenz, and his business partner Beat Stocker.

The revelations helped trigger investigations that eventually led to criminal proceedings. In April 2022, Vincenz and Stocker were convicted of fraud and other offenses. Vincenz was sentenced to three years and nine months in prison, while Stocker received a four-year term. Both have appealed, with a ruling expected in January 2027.

Separately, Stocker filed a criminal complaint asking prosecutors to pursue charges against Hässig.

"There is a public interest in the facts. An unsubstantiated, flawed narrative is another matter," Stocker told OCCRP, arguing that there was “no legal basis under Swiss criminal law” for his own conviction.

title: How Leo Tolstoy Became a Vegetarian and Jumpstarted the Vegetarian & Humanitarian Movements in the 19th Century
content:
Leo Tolstoy is remembered as both a towering pinnacle of Russian literature and a fascinating example of Christian anarchism, a mystical version of which the aristocratic author pioneered in the last quarter century of his life. After a dramatic conversion, Tolstoy rejected his social position, the favored vices of his youth, and the dietary habits of his culture, becoming a vocal proponent of vegetarianism in his ascetic quest for the good life. Thousands of his contemporaries found Tolstoy’s example deeply compelling, and several communes formed around his principles, to his dismay. “To speak of ‘Tolstoyism,’” he wrote, “to seek guidance, to inquire about my solution of questions, is a great and gross error.”

“Still,” writes Kelsey Osgood at The New Yorker, “people insisted on seeking guidance from him,” including a young Mahatma Gandhi, who struck up a lively correspondence with the writer and in 1910 founded a community called “Tolstoy Farm” near Johannesburg.

title: EU sanctions Russian trolls, hackers
content:
European Union member countries on Monday issued sanctions against a Russian company running disinformation campaigns and one of Russia’s most well-known hacking groups.

The Council of the EU said it had sanctioned the Social Design Agency, a Moscow-based firm that carries out “large scale information manipulation and interference projects,” as well as 24 of its staff members.

The Social Design Agency is “funded, directed and supervised” by the Russian government and has organized disinformation campaigns targeting EU countries, EU institutions and European support for Ukraine, Council said.

The group has been connected in the past to a vast online disinformation network known as Doppelganger. It targeted the 2024 European elections and carried out “dedicated operations against EU member states such as Germany and France,” countries said.

EU capitals also agreed to levy sanctions against notorious Russian hacking group NoName057(16), which has targeted government bodies and critical infrastructure as well as private firms in the EU, Ukraine and the United States.

title: Kenen ehdoilla Suomea rakennetaan?
content:
Tekoäly muuttaa maailmaa nopeammin kuin ehdimme sitä ymmärtää. Puhutaan murroksesta, jota verrataan teolliseen vallankumoukseen. Se vaikuttaa siihen, millaista työtä teemme, miten turvallisuudestamme huolehditaan ja kenellä on valtaa. Tämä murros ei tapahdu vain jossain pilvessä. Sen fyysinen muoto on datakeskus: valtava halli, joka tarvitsee maata, sähköä, kriittisiä raaka-aineita ja usein vettä.

Juuri nyt maailmalla on käynnissä datakeskusbuumi, ja Suomi kiinnostaa. Meillä on vakaa yhteiskunta, toimiva sähköverkko, viileä ilmasto ja puhdasta, edullista energiaa. Siksi kansainväliset jättiyhtiöt katsovat tänne.

Se ei ole ongelma sinänsä, mutta ongelma on siinä, kenen ehdoilla jättiyhtiöiden datakeskuksia nousee Suomeen – kenen ehdoilla Suomea rakennetaan. Datakeskukset voivat tuoda Suomeen työtä, osaamista ja verotuloja, mutta jos annamme niiden tulla millä ehdoilla tahansa, havahdumme liian myöhään seurauksiin. Silloin metsät, vedet ja yhteinen sähkömme muuttuvat raaka-aineeksi, josta hyöty valuu muualle ja haitat jäävät tänne. Siksi meillä vihreillä on selkeä kanta: Suomi ei voi olla datakeskusten villi länsi.

content: Nine robots dance clumsily on the stage of Lisbon's FIL Arena. “This is our time, this is our fight” go the lyrics of the song. “This was the biggest robot dance performance outside of China!” the event's moderator proclaims. The 30,000 people in the arena give the robots a round of applause. The cameras filming the robots, however, are still operated by human videographers. I'm at the opening of Web Summit, one of the world's largest tech conferences, held annually in Lisbon. It draws 70,000 attendees encompassing the entire tech sector, from mega-corporations such as Meta, Apple, and Tiktok, to small start-ups, as well as countries from around the world showing off their industry. Attendees pay a lot to be there. General admission tickets cost around €1,500, unless you're a journalist, then you get in for free. I went to find out what the tech sector envisions for the future. title: Cycling Connects: Bringing Tourism and Transport Together for a More Connected Baltic Sea Region
content:
Almost 80 participants joined the “Cycling Connects” webinar on 26 October 2026, marking the first jointly organised thematic event by the EU Strategy for the Baltic Sea Region (EUSBSR) Policy Areas Tourism and Transport. The strong interest and lively exchange confirmed that cycling tourism is much more than a tourism product – it is an important link between sustainable mobility, regional development and cross-border cooperation.

The webinar brought together representatives of the European Commission, European cycling organisations, regional authorities, tourism stakeholders and EU-funded projects to exchange perspectives, showcase practical initiatives and explore how closer cooperation between tourism and transport can support a more sustainable and accessible Baltic Sea Region.

Cycling tourism is growing in importance across Europe, offering opportunities to encourage low-carbon travel, connect urban and rural destinations, support local businesses and develop attractive cross-border tourism experiences. Yet unlocking its full potential requires cooperation across sectors, administrative borders and policy areas.

title: Three of the Financial Sins That Left Chicago $55 Billion in Debt — and Counting
content:
Chicago’s finances have long been strained by soaring pension expenses, spiraling personnel costs and a massive amount of debt. Budget deficits and financial crises now arrive with regularity, as city leaders face crucial decisions on how to dig out of this financial mess. 

The track record of decision-making within City Hall suggests that avoiding hard choices for expediency leads to trouble. 

The city must spend billions every year from its main account — known as its corporate fund — to keep current on the $55 billion it owes to banks and its pension funds. The debt consists of $19 billion in loan payments that must be repaid by revenue from property and sales taxes as well as $36 billion to ensure former employees get retirement benefits. The city also borrows money to make improvements to its water and sewer systems and to fund operations at its airports, but that debt is repaid with fees, not money from the corporate fund. 

Here are three of the big decisions Chicago officials have made over the years that dug the city into such a massive financial hole.

Helsingin Suvilahdessa 29.–30.5.2027 järjestettävä Maailma kylässä -festivaali on avannut näytteilleasettajien paikkahaun sekä avoimen taiteilijahaun, jolla etsitään osallistavaa taideteosta, -tekoa tai -tempausta festivaalille. Järjestöille suunnattu puheohjelmahaku on avoinna 1.12. asti.

Suomen suurimmalla kestävän kehityksen festarilla organisaatiot voivat kohdata uusia yleisöjä, tehdä toimintaansa tunnetuksi ja edistää itselleen tärkeitä tavoitteita. title: Saudi Arabia: Amazon warehouse workers still facing exploitation despite company initiatives
content:
Migrant workers hired to work in Amazon’s operations in Saudi Arabia continue to face abuses from the third-party labour supply companies that employ them. They are also subjected to harsh working conditions in Amazon’s warehouses and the risk of the company ending their assignment at will, despite Amazon’s attempts to improve other aspects of their recruitment and living conditions, Amnesty International said in a new briefing today.

Amazon in Saudi Arabia: Why migrant workers remain at risk of exploitation documented some important improvements, including reduced recruitment-fee abuses, better accommodation standards and improved access to grievance mechanisms. Following Amnesty International’s 2023 investigation, Amazon also reimbursed more than USD 2.45 million to 1,180 workers in Saudi Arabia. Nevertheless, migrant workers remain vulnerable to exploitation under Amazon’s hiring model.

title: People's Climate March: Thousands Demonstrate in Turkey as Country Hosts COP31 U.N. Summit
content:
Democracy Now! is in Antalya, Turkey, where this year’s United Nations climate summit, COP31, is being held. For the second year in a row, the United States has not sent an official delegation to the international talks, in keeping with the Trump administration’s longstanding hostility to such efforts to address the climate crisis.

There are nearly 100,000 participants here at this year’s climate summit, including many civil society activists from Turkey and around the globe. Over the weekend, Democracy Now! was in the streets of Antalya to speak with some of the thousands of protesters who marched to demand urgent climate action, including many labor leaders.

“Trade unions care about a lot more than just protecting jobs. We have systemic demands,” said Lala Peñaranda, the Latin America coordinator for Trade Unions for Energy Democracy.

title: Amazon Ring’s New Indoor Surveillance Drone Is Not Compatible with Privacy
content:
Amazon Ring has finally announced their long-dreaded indoor drone, a small flying surveillance device connected to their security suite of products that can fly around your house filming and recording things. The device is supposedly designed to fly preset paths across your home and will also activate if a sensor or alarm has been triggered.  

Customers should think twice about purchasing these devices for a number of reasons. These devices are problematic in many of the ways we’ve said Ring’s stationary home surveillance products are a problem, plus some new ways. At a very basic level, they are essentially a window into your house that can be accessed by anyone with access to your account—which has historically included bad actors looking to embarrass or harass Ring users and employees of the company.

title: Monique Wittigin feminismin klassikkoteos kyseenalaistaa itsestäänselvyyksinä pidettyjä käsityksiä sukupuolesta, kielestä ja kirjallisuudesta
content:
Kirjailija, sukupuolentutkija, kirjallisuudentutkija ja feministi Monique Wittigin (1935–2003) esseekokoelma Straight-ajattelu (The Straight Mind and Other Essays, 1992) käsittelee edelleen ajankohtaisia sekä vähälle huomiolle nykykeskustelussa jääneitä teemoja. Hänen mukaansa sukupuoli pohjaa oletukseen ”miehen” ja ”naisen” luonnollisuudesta, mutta tähän poliittiseen straight-ajatteluun voidaan puuttua kieltä muokkaamalla ja kirjallisuuden avulla. Teoksen on suomentanut Heta Rundgren.

”Sorto luo sukupuolen, ei toisinpäin.”

Ranskalaisen toisen aallon kuuluisimpiin feministeihin lukeutuva Monique Wittig toimi paitsi Ranskassa myös Yhdysvalloissa ja kirjoitti sekä ranskaksi että englanniksi. Hänen teoreettinen työnsä on vaikuttanut vahvasti esimerkiksi queer-ajatteluun.

”Hän kehitti sukupuolen ja seksuaalisuuden kriittistä tutkimusta mutta myös ajattelua kielen ja sukupuolen yhteyksistä. Hänen elämäntyönsä inspiroi laajasti nykypäivän feminististä ajattelua ja tutkimusta ympäri maailman”, suomentaja Heta Rundgren kertoo.

title: Philippines: US Tech Hub to Displace Hundreds
content:
(Manila) – The Philippine government’s impending construction of a technology manufacturing hub under the US government’s “Pax Silica” initiative will displace hundreds of Indigenous peoples and farmers in Tarlac province, Human Rights Watch said today.

The Philippine government will provide the land—including territory inhabited for generations by the Indigenous Aeta tribe—while investors, including US companies, will finance the infrastructure and facilities. The framework agreement between the Philippines and the United States is yet to be signed.

“Indigenous communities and small farmers fear they will be unlawfully displaced by the semiconductor hub,” said Lian Buan, Southeast Asia researcher at Human Rights Watch. “The Philippine government should follow domestic laws and international standards that protect land rights.”

Human Rights Watch visited two affected sites in Capas in October 2026—Sapang Kawayan in Barangay Aranguren and Sitio Binyayan in Barangay O’Donnell—and spoke to 11 residents.

title: Estonia has a plan for Russian occupation: Run its government from the cloud
content:
TALLINN — Imagine French General Charles de Gaulle, exiled in London during World War II, running his Free France government by logging into the cloud.

Officials in Estonia are preparing for exactly such a scenario with a new strategy to boost doomsday resilience — hukukindlus in Estonian — that would allow the government’s digital services to be run entirely from abroad if its territory is occupied by a foreign enemy.

The Baltic country of  1.3 million, which shares a 294-kilometer border with Russia, fears it is a prime target if Moscow were to invade a European Union country. Security services have already warned that Russia is waging a hybrid war on Europe, and Estonia has blamed Moscow for everything from cyberattacks to arson plots to cuts to undersea data cables.

Now, Tallinn is preparing to move its public services to the cloud “either when data centers are destroyed or there’s boots on the ground and we cannot operate,” said Tõnu Grünberg, an architect of the new strategy and former deputy secretary general for digital infrastructure and cybersecurity at Estonia’s Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs.

content:
Tilastokeskus on julkaissut tilastoja perusopetuksen ainevalinnoista vuonna 2025. title: Ecuadorian Courts Expose Flaws in US High-Seas Arrests
content:
Between August 28 and September 16, US military forces intercepted and destroyed eight Ecuadorian fishing vessels, alleging that they served as floating refueling stations for drug-trafficking boats. They detained 146 of the 160 crew members and transferred them to Ecuadorian authorities, who charged 90 with “unlawful association.”

Since Human Rights Watch reported on the operations, Ecuadorian courts have acquitted 40 people. In an October 29 judgment reviewed by Human Rights Watch, a Manta judge acquitted eight fishermen from a vessel named the Don Rufo. The prosecution’s own witnesses, including Ecuadorian police and Navy officials, testified that no illicit items were recovered, and that they knew of no prior investigation linking the fishermen to organized crime.

The judge said the prosecution rested on a “chain of successive presumptions.” He admonished the prosecutor for pursuing an unsupported case and closed it.

title: UAE: 5 Shia Residents Arrested Arbitrarily
content:
(Beirut) – Emirati authorities have arbitrarily detained at least five Shia Muslim foreign residents since the United States and Israel carried out military strikes on Iran in February 2026, Human Rights Watch said today. The detentions appear to be based on the detainees’ religious identity. 

Emirati authorities detained the residents, who had been in the UAE between 2 and 40 years, between March and May. They have not been brought before a judge or formally charged, three informed sources said. 

“Emirati authorities appear to be rounding up residents simply based on their religious beliefs as Shia Muslims in a largely Sunni country rather than providing any evidence of wrongdoing, while trampling over people’s due process rights,” said Joey Shea, senior UAE researcher at Human Rights Watch. “The authorities should immediately release anyone targeted because of their religion.”

Between September and October, Human Rights Watch interviewed the three sources and reviewed CCTV footage of a raid on the company that one of the detainees owned. The detainees’ and sources’ names are withheld for fear of reprisals against them and their relatives.

title: Hanoi 2015: The City Conceded on Trees, Not on Accountability
content:
The Tree Hugs movement won the argument over trees and lost the argument over accountability. Its petition to Hanoi’s People’s Committee made three demands: stop the felling, open up the decision, and hold officials to account. The first was met within four days. The other two never were. That gap is the lesson.

The movement began with a dismissal. On 17 March 2015, a Hanoi propaganda official was asked whether residents had been consulted about plans to fell 6,700 street trees. There was no need, he replied. Within days, tens of thousands of Hanoians had answered him on Facebook.

No single organisation led the response. It was a loose network of three Facebook groups, drawing mostly young people and women.

No single organisation led the response. It was a loose network of three Facebook groups, drawing mostly young people and women.

The plan was approved in late 2013 without public notice. It would replace 6,708 trees on 190 streets for about US$3.4 million. Officials called it landscaping. Residents saw healthy, century old trees, many planted under French rule, falling within days in a city that shelters under their shade.

title: A Cop Was Charged With Causing His Wife’s Miscarriage. Alabama’s Laws Came Down Harder on Pregnant Women Who Used Drugs.
content:
On the night of Feb. 15, 2022, Robert Maddox Jr., a rookie cop in a small Alabama town, called his colleague in a panic. His wife was about three months pregnant and bleeding heavily. They needed someone to watch their two sleeping children while they went to the hospital.

Headland police Officer James “Bo” Knight arrived with his wife. He had been serving as a mentor of sorts to Robert, who had just recently joined the department, and had urged him to reach out if he ever needed help.

The situation Knight encountered was a heavy one. Robert had something in a plastic bag that looked to Knight like fetal remains. His wife stood by silently. Robert said he’d be back as soon as possible, that he was taking both his wife and the bag to the hospital. 

When the couple returned three hours later, Robert was holding a white container.

“They put my fucking baby in a box,” he said.

title: Kazakhstan and Japan Renew Test-Ban Appeal as Treaty Deadlock Persists
content:
Thirty years after opening for signature, the CTBT has broad international support but still lacks nine ratifications required for entry into force

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 15 November 2026 (IDN) — Kazakhstan and Japan have renewed calls for an end to nuclear testing as the treaty intended to prohibit all nuclear explosions remains blocked, three decades after it opened for signature.

Their appeal, made at a September commemoration at the United Nations Office at Nairobi, comes as preparations for enforcing the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) continue despite the political impasse. An inspection exercise in Namibia is testing capabilities that cannot be used under the treaty until it enters into force.

The contrast exposes a central weakness in the international effort to prevent renewed testing: governments have built a global detection network, but have yet to activate the agreement that would authorise inspectors to investigate a suspected violation on the ground.

title: Petition for the Creation of the European Public Social Network
content:
Social media in their current form are great for Big Tech companies making money selling our attention and training their machine learning models on our data using unsustainable, energy-heavy computations. Their business model turns out to be fertile ground for disinformation, conspiracies, affective polarization, and further marginalization of certain voices. Deep down, we all want to leave but we stay because we fear losing the means of communication with others. But where individual resistance seems futile, collective action could be the solution.

The good news is, there is a plenty of talent in the EU already, making alternatives not just easy to imagine, but ready to be observed. We strive to gather public support for the creation of a decentralized social network for everyone, where users have full control over their private data and the algorithm and where bots and fake accounts spreading disinformation are prevented from accessing the platform. As students from across the EU joined by other citizens, we ask the European Commission to support the creation of a European public-service social network financed and controlled by citizens.

Originally published on Rising Voices

Photo provided by Roseline Mballa, Itón, Kɔlɔ and Kwasio Language Activist, and used with permission.

This interview is part of the African Languages Digital Activism series by Rising Voices, highlighting the personal journeys of activists working to preserve, promote, and revitalise African languages. Through their stories, the series explores the role of digital platforms, community initiatives, and local knowledge in strengthening the presence of African languages both online and offline.

In this edition, Umasoye speaks with Roseline Mballa, a language activist from Cameroon working to promote the Itón, Kɔlɔ and Kwasio languages. She shares her journey into language activism, the challenges and opportunities facing these languages, and the initiatives helping to ensure their continued use and transmission to future generations.

title: Mass protests that led to regime change had their heyday between 1980 and 2011: what happened?
content:
People are taking to the streets across the world. In 2025, mass mobilisation occurred in countries such as Morocco, Tanzania and Turkey. In Madagascar, protests resulted in president Andry Rajoelina fleeing the country in October. More recently, protesters have filled the streets from France and Italy to Senegal and Kenya.

By mass mobilisation, we mean sustained, organised campaigns of protests that involve more than 1,000 people, aimed at changing a country’s political regime or removing the government or leader.

Mass mobilisation has historically been seen as a viable path to democracy. Ferdinand Marcos left Manila in 1986 after weeks of popular protests. The Berlin Wall fell in 1989 after months of demonstrations in East Germany. South Africa’s apartheid regime yielded to domestic and international pressure in the 1990s.

The examples are many, and mass movements have been a driving force to democratic change in authoritarian regimes.

title: This Comic Kills Technofascists
content:
Dave Maass has been writing about comics for more than 20 years, and now he also writes comics. By day, he teaches tech investigative techniques at the University of Nevada, Reno Reynolds School of Journalism and researches surveillance at the Electronic Frontier Foundation. 

If I was the manager of a comic book store, I’d create a section for “journalism nerdcore.” It’s where I would stock Transmetropolitan, DMZ, and Abbott–comics that place fictional journalists in the center of genre stories, be it science fiction, action or horror. Despite their daylight jobs, Spider-Man and Superman wouldn’t be allowed there, but DC’s Lois Lane would find a home of her own. 

On the end-of-shelf display, with a big fat, Sharpie-written “Employee Pick of 2026” sign: Exploit, the new comic series from Laura Hudson and Tim Leong and illustrator Emiliana Pinna, which was just published last month by Mad Cave Studios in its collected trade paperback volume. It doesn’t get more journalism nerdcore than its tag line: “Don’t Bury The Lede. Bury Your Enemies!”

title: The Guardian view on Cop31: the green transition must not be derailed | Editorial
content:
Renewed commitments to electrification and climate science are vital outcomes from the latest round of UN talks

The Cop31 climate talks have acquired something their delegates scarcely expected: a little political breathing space. The comeback by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the second round of Brazil’s presidential race was important for many reasons. Victory for his opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, would have marked a dangerous retreat from democracy. But Mr Bolsonaro’s commitment to environmental deregulation would also have spelled disaster for the Amazon, making Lula’s re-election a big win for the climate. Similarly, success by Democrats in the US midterms means that Donald Trump’s destructive grip has been loosened. If they win back the White House in 2028, the US should rejoin the UN process in time for Cop34.

title: The EU has always found a way through. On AI, it’s struggling to see it.
content:
There might be an AI apocalypse. European leaders don’t really want to talk about it.

By SEBASTIAN STARCEVIC and PIETER HAECK
in DUBLIN

Illustration by Natália Delgado/POLITICO

The European Union wasn’t set up to deal with challenges as vast and existential as the possibility of AI wiping out humanity.

For two decades, the EU’s leaders have muddled through crisis after crisis — from Greece coming within days of being pushed out of the eurozone, to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, which forced millions to seek safety in the bloc. Each time, it has found a way through. It’s what the EU does.

With AI, though, it’s turning out to be different.

Tech experts, industry and even governments themselves describe paralysis, distraction and defeatism in Europe’s capitals. It’s telling that it took four years after the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022 for EU leaders to bring themselves to discuss artificial intelligence at a summit in Dublin on Friday.

And even then, there was little enthusiasm for the topic.

title: After School MeToo: Political Mamas’ Fight for Answers in South Korea
content:
During South Korea’s 2018 School MeToo movement, students publicly reported sexual harassment and assault by teachers. But another question remained: how had schools and education authorities responded?

In 2019, Political Mamas, a South Korean nonprofit founded by mothers, and open to other caregivers, began requesting records from regional education offices and mapping publicly reported allegations.

The campaign aimed to make institutional responses visible, identify gaps in investigations and disciplinary action, and strengthen accountability for student safety.

South Korea’s wider #MeToo movement gained momentum in early 2018 after prosecutor Seo Ji-hyun publicly described sexual harassment she had experienced. One Yonghwa graduate later told WomenNews that seeing Seo and Hollywood actresses speak out had encouraged her to do the same.

title: Le pastoralisme, risque ou solution face au changement climatique ? L’évolution du regard porté par les COP climat
content:
Plusieurs centaines de millions de personnes dans le monde vivent du pastoralisme. Il peut être source d’inspiration pour penser et pour accompagner les autres formes d’agriculture, le changement agraire ou encore notre perception de la nature. L’ouvrage Penser avec le pastoralisme. Itinéraires de recherche (librement téléchargeable en ebook), récemment publié aux éditions Quae (coordination Véronique Ancey, Serena Ferrari et Claire Aubron), explore ces enjeux.

À l’occasion de la COP31 sur le climat, qui se tient en Turquie du 9 au 20 novembre, nous reproduisons une partie du chapitre consacré à la place du pastoralisme pour les experts du Groupe d'experts intergouvernemental sur l'évolution du climat (Giec), les COP climat et la diplomatie mondiale.

Bien que la contribution de l’élevage au changement climatique soit désormais largement reconnue, ce secteur est longtemps resté en marge de l’agenda climatique international dans le cadre du Giec et n’y a été intégré que tardivement.

title: ‘Risk multiplier’: super El Niño looms over Cop31 as climate pattern fuels global disasters
content:
Strongest El Niño in centuries adds urgency to UN climate talks as vulnerable countries face ‘compounding’ crises

If the galloping pace of the climate crisis isn’t enough to spur countries to act at UN climate talks under way in Turkey, there is another major threat heightening its havoc: the strongest El Niño event in at least 1,000 years.

The “jaw-dropping” El Niño, a naturally recurring phenomenon where the eastern Pacific heats up every few years with temporary but global implications, has provided added urgency to wrangling at the Cop31 summit over climate funding for vulnerable countries that are having to scramble to respond.

title: Small Steps 4 Hannah: How One Family Helped Queensland See Coercive Control
content:
In February 2020, Hannah Clarke and her three children, Aaliyah, Laianah and Trey, were murdered in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia, by the husband she had recently left. Her father, Lloyd Clarke, kept asking how he had missed the signs.

Part of the answer was a term many people did not know yet: coercive control. It means using a pattern of behaviour to dominate a partner, such as cutting her off from family, tracking her, and controlling her money. This abuse often leaves no visible injuries.

Within weeks, Hannah’s parents, Sue and Lloyd Clarke, set up the Small Steps 4 Hannah Foundation. It supports people affected by domestic violence, teaches students, workers and families to spot coercive control, and has pushed the Queensland Government to make it a crime.

This article argues that Small Steps used one family’s story to make hidden abuse visible and help write it into law in 2024. Whether the law brings real safety is still unclear.

In its 2016–17 Annual Report, Queensland’s Domestic and Family Violence Death Review and Advisory Board found signs of coercive control in almost all the deaths it reviewed. Yet services rarely responded unless physical violence was also reported.

title: Britain’s veto could stop the UAE’s choice from running the United Nations. Miliband must use it | Steve Bloomfield

Since the devastating war in Sudan began in 2023, some of the best investigative work uncovering those responsible has been carried out by the UN panel of experts. It is these reports, produced by UN-funded investigators, that the UN secretary general, António Guterres, cites whenever he speaks about Sudan.

title: The Right to Sit: How Kerala’s Women Retail Workers Pushed for Change
content:
The Right to Sit campaign in Kerala organized women textile workers around a simple demand—seating at work—and turned their shared grievances into a 2018 legal amendment mandating seats in shops and commercial establishments.

The following article discusses their campaign and the need for workers to keep organizing and monitoring conditions to defend protections.

For many women working in Kerala’s textile shops in India, sitting down was something they had to fight for. They spent long hours on their feet, and some were not even allowed to lean against a wall. Workers reported knee pain and restrictions on toilet breaks. Some avoided drinking water because their shops lacked toilet facilities.

The Right to Sit movement brought these working conditions into public view.

Organising centred on Kozhikode, with protests also taking place in Thrissur and Alappuzha. Penkoottu, a women’s collective whose name means “women’s nest”, and the Asanghadita Meghala Thozhilali Union (AMTU), a union for workers in the unorganised sector, helped workers organise.

title: Restoring social media access comes at a cost in Gabon
content:
Citizens in Gabon went 248 days without access to Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube

Originally published on Global Voices Advox

Image of a smartphone showing the Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, YouTube, and Messenger apps. Screenshot from the DW Afrique YouTube channel. Fair use.

After more than eight months of government blockage, Gabon has restored its social media access. But it has come at a cost. This reinstatement comes with a tighter regulatory framework and an unprecedented cooperation between the government and various tech giants, raising serious concerns about freedom of expression and privacy.

On February 17, 2026, Gabon’s media regulator, the High Communication Authority (HAC), suspended major social media networks, including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube, “until further notice.” According to the regulator, quoted in the daily newspaper L’Essentiel, this measure targeted not only content “undermining national security” but also content involving defamation, cyberbullying, hate speech, and threats to social cohesion.

title: I Investigated the Online Sports Betting Industry. DraftKings Shut Down My Account.
content:
Late last month, I was getting dinner on the table when an email hit my inbox with some bad news.

“Upon review your account has been closed at DraftKings’ discretion,” the message read. “We understand that this is not the decision that you were hoping for but this decision is final.” 

I hadn’t bet on sports in months and had withdrawn all but a few cents of my balance. Why, I wondered, would my account even be under review? Was it something I’d said?

In September, I’d published an investigation into how online sports betting companies like DraftKings court customers — and whether the internal guardrails they’ve put in place to stop their users from spiraling out of control are firm enough. For that piece, I’d intentionally bet like a problem gambler, recklessly escalating my betting behavior over 10 weeks. My wagering had been informed by a panel of professional sports bettors, recovering addicts and addiction specialists.

As I flagrantly waved the red flags, DraftKings made me a VIP and assigned me my very own personal host. My recklessness was being rewarded. It just took three weeks and about $6,000 of losses.

title: Learning under trees in the era of AI: The paradox of education in Mozambique
content:
AI could help bridge educational inequality in a country where thousands of students still learn outdoors

Originally published on Global Voices

Photo taken by Rahul Ingle, May 2012. This file is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 2.0 Generic license.

In many communities across Mozambique, formal education still takes place in the open air, under trees, in improvised yards, or inside fragile structures that barely offer protection from the sun and rain. These so-called outdoor classrooms are not an innovative pedagogical choice, but more often than not, the expression of a structural deficiency: a lack of infrastructure, a shortage of materials, and an estimated deficit of around 12,000 teachers in 2025.

During the rainy season (roughly November to March in Mozambique), the situation becomes more challenging. In several regions, the school calendar must be adjusted to respond to inclement weather, such as heavy rains that disrupt classes and hinder the continuity of teaching between November and March each year.

title: A new Democratic Congress will view Trump’s harsh Cuba policy skeptically – but that doesn’t mean a change is coming soon
content:
The so-called “blue tsunami” that hit the United States in the midterm elections is causing ripples around the world.

Having won a historic victory, congressional Democrats now appear poised to challenge the Trump administration’s conduct of foreign affairs.

The Iran war, support for Ukraine and the management of Venezuelan oil certainly all appear to be on the agenda of some Democrats.

The flipping of the House and Senate from Republican to Democratic control has also led to speculation that members of Congress may also wish to challenge Trump’s Cuba policy.

After all, the United States’ position on Cuba has swung in recent decades, depending on the balance of power in Washington. An easing of tensions and normalization of relations between the U.S. and Cuba took place under the presidency of Barack Obama, only to be reversed following the election of Donald Trump in 2016. President Joe Biden largely followed Trump’s lead, while making more allowance for activities supporting the Cuban people.

title: Scientists Made Monkeys Watch Minions to Study Their Brains
content:
Welcome back to the Abstract! These are the studies this week that watched movies, made sacrifices, got crafty, and aged backwards.

First, scientists learn how primates make meaning out of visuals by peeking into the brains of monkeys as they watch Despicable Me. Then: human sacrifice as climate “crisis rituals,” the fingerprints of prehistoric children, and the longevity secrets of ants.

As always, for more of my work, check out my book First Contact: The Story of Our Obsession with Aliens, or subscribe to my personal newsletter The BeX Files. 

Raghavan, Vinay S et al. “During natural vision, semantic novelty modulates fixation-related processing in primate cortex.” JNeurosci.

Settling down to watch a film is often viewed as a way to relax and shut our brains off for a while. Our brains, however, beg to differ—they are as busy as ever when interpreting videos, according to a new study based on brainwaves of humans and primates as they watch movies and short clips.

content:

title: Italy hits Meta with €805M fine over privacy law violation
content:
Italian authorities fined Facebook’s parent company Meta €805 million for using photos and videos from Android phones without users’ specific consent, the Italian Data Protection Authority said in a statement Saturday. 

The fine concerned the “camera roll suggestions when browsing Facebook” feature, which suggests photos and videos from a phone’s gallery for users to add to posts.

The feature violates the Italian law implementing the EU’s ePrivacy directive, the authority said. It is by far the largest fine ever imposed by the Italian regulator.

The investigation, launched in 2025, established that access to a user’s camera roll is requested with a single permission for the entire app, which the authority said covers multiple features with different needs. The authorization request was preceded by a generic warning that didn’t allow users to understand that they were authorizing picture and video suggestions, the authority said. 

“If granted in full, this type of permission allows the app to read the device’s entire photo archive, usually permanently, without the user or the authorities being able to verify which information is actually being used,” the statement reads.

title: Årets språklärare undanröjer hinder för lärande
content:
Språklärarförbundet i Finland SUKOL rf har utsett Anna-Leena Haapala till Årets språklärare. Haapala undervisar i engelska och svenska vid Sasky Tammerfors yrkesinstitut för servicebranschen. Det är viktigt för henne att alla hennes studerande får grundläggande språkkunskaper och mod att tala. Att motivera den studerande är en central del av hennes undervisning. “När den studerande får mod och vågar samtala på engelska eller svenska i lärarens närvaro, har man åtminstone övervunnit ett hinder för lärandet”, säger hon.

Tammerfors yrkesinstitut för servicebranschen är en del av utbildningssamkommunen Sasky, som verkar inom flera kommuners område i Birkaland och Satakunta. Anna-Leena Haapala har erfarenhet även från andra stadier, men största delen av sin yrkeskarriär har hon arbetat inom yrkesutbildningen på andra stadiet. Det som enligt henne är särskilt fint i yrkeslärarens arbete är mötet med de studerande och att uppmuntra dem att studera ett ämne som känns svårt: ”Känslan av framgång är ömsesidig och fantastisk när någon lär sig uttala ett svårt ord rätt eller kommer ihåg att skriva en struktur korrekt.”

title: Suzanne Innes-Stubb uppmuntrar till att tala olika språk utan rädsla för misstag
content:
Språklärarförbundet i Finland SUKOL rf tilldelar Suzanne Innes-Stubb priset Årets språkgärning 2026. Priset Årets språkgärning delas ut årligen för verksamhet som har främjat flerspråkigheten eller höjt språkundervisningens samhälleliga status.

I rollen som republikens presidents maka har Innes-Stubbs exempel en bred inverkan. Hon har inte nöjt sig med att använda enbart sitt modersmål engelska, även om hon skulle klara sig med det. Vid sidan av sina övriga språkkunskaper har hon lärt sig finska och svenska och talar båda nationalspråken flytande. Kunskaperna i de nationella språken har för hennes del också varit en väg till finländarnas hjärtan.

Innes-Stubb har studerat juridik samt franska och tyska och har under sin karriär arbetat i internationella uppgifter bland annat med konkurrenslagstiftning. Familjens flerspråkighet beskriver hon så här: ”Jag talar engelska med våra barn, min man talar svenska med dem, övriga familjemedlemmar talar finska, och vi har goda vänner som talar franska.” Innes-Stubb är ett utmärkt exempel på språkkunskapens viktiga roll både i vardagen och i krävande internationella relationer.

title: Attacks on the Freedom of Assembly: Lessons from Digital Rights Defenders
content:
In 2026, two cases revealed how civic space is eroding, and those defending digital freedom and combating disinformation are on the frontline.

RightsCon, the world’s leading summit on human rights and technology, was due to be held in Lusaka, Zambia on May 5-8. Civil society, technologists, academics and policymakers were set to tackle some of the digital age’s most pressing issues: AI, surveillance, the militarisation of tech, disinformation, and online hate, among them.

But just days before the summit was going to open, and with more than 3,000 delegates about to arrive in Lusaka, the Zambian government unilaterally postponed the event because it did not align with “national values”. The decision, according to local reports, was made after Chinese diplomats pressured the Zambian government, objecting to the presence of Taiwanese civil society delegates at the conference.

In October, another attempt by a foreign power to intervene in a civil society gathering occurred.

title: Young people’s wellbeing is essential for meaningful participation in peacebuilding
content:
At the Stockholm Forum, a session organised by CMI and Search for Common Ground explored how mental health and psychosocial support can help young people engage in civic life and peacebuilding processes. Drawing on experiences from Mali, Palestine, and Ukraine, participants shared insights on how psychosocial support can be better integrated into peacebuilding efforts.

Young people in conflict-affected settings are often portrayed as victims, risks, or symbols of resilience. Such narratives overlook the profound psychosocial impacts of violence, displacement, and prolonged insecurity, and the ways these experiences shape young people’s participation in peacebuilding and civic life.

Today, an estimated one in four young people live in contexts affected by conflict, and many experience mental health and psychosocial distress. In countries such as Mali, Palestine, and Ukraine, young people navigate not only immediate crisis, but also the lasting effects of intergenerational trauma, social fragmentation, and mistrust. Yet peacebuilding efforts rarely address these realities in a systematic way.

I travelled to Beijing, China, for the Beijing Science Dialogue and International Science Council (ISC) Midterm Meeting, expecting to engage in conversations about the future of science, international scientific cooperation and the opportunities and challenges presented by emerging technologies. title: AI and bots on the campaign trail: What Poland can learn from Hungary
content:
On screen, a young Hungarian soldier stands on the Ukrainian front line. Moments later, he is killed, leaving a child crying at home. The scene looks like something from a war movie. But it was generated using artificial intelligence.

The video was published in February 2026 by the Budapest branch of Fidesz, Viktor Orbán’s party. Its message was clear: a victory for Péter Magyar’s opposition Tisza party could drag Hungary into war.

It was hardly an isolated incident. Ahead of the April 12, 2026, parliamentary election, artificial intelligence became one of the principal weapons in the political battle. Videos, images and other material were generated to attack opponents. They spread not only through official party accounts but also through affiliated organizations, influencers and networks of social media accounts.

“Using AI in political campaigns was not new. What was new during this election campaign was that they used it massively,” says Zsófia Fülöp, a journalist at the Hungarian fact-checking outlet Lakmusz who investigated disinformation during this year’s parliamentary election.

title: Tekoäly työyhteisössä – kenelle tämä tapa toimii?
content:
Tekoälyratkaisujen käyttöönottoa perustellaan yleensä sillä, mitä hyötyä se tuo. Sen odotetaan nopeuttavan tekemistä, helpottavan tiettyjä työvaiheita tai parantavan lopputulosta. Samalla kannattaa pysähtyä tarkastelemaan, miten uusi toimintatapa vaikuttaa erilaisiin työntekijöihin. Moninaisuuden näkökulmasta olennainen kysymys kuuluu: kenelle tämä tapa toimii?

Moninaisuus on helppo nähdä vain demografisina eroina. Laajemmin käsitettynä moninaisuus ilmenee ihmisten erilaisina tapoina käsitellä tietoa, oppia, keskittyä ja ilmaista itseään sekä ajatuksiaan. Myös kielitaito, toimintakyky, digitaidot, työtehtävät, käytettävissä olevat laitteet ja mahdollisuus osallistua työajalla vaihtelevat. 

Digitaalinen osallistuminen alkaa käytännön toimintaedellytyksistä. Ihminen tarvitsee sopivan laitteen, toimivan yhteyden, käyttöoikeuden ja aikaa perehtyä. Toimistotyötä tekevä käyttää tekoälyratkaisua eri tilanteessa kuin vuorotyöntekijä, liikkuvaa työtä tekevä tai henkilö, jonka työpäivään kuuluu vain vähän tietokoneella työskentelyä. Myös lisenssit voivat jakaa henkilöstön eri asemaan: yhdellä tiimillä on käytössään maksullinen tekoälypalvelu, toisella suppeampi versio ja kolmannella ei mitään.

title: The grand art-taking - Tracking Europe's missing paintings
content: Over the past century, art thieves have stolen 27 Van Gogh masterpieces across Europe, more than any other famous artist by a healthy margin. But if you add up mainstream cinema hits, TV series, and even docu-dramas, the favourite victim is Rembrandt, followed by Degas and Rubens. Van Gogh’s lead owes a lot to one very ambitious night. On 14 April 1991, 20 paintings vanished from Amsterdam’s Van Gogh Museum. Two armed men had hidden inside the building and, as it turned out, had help from within. Yet the world-famous Dutch painter remains underrepresented on screen, appearing in just two action films: The Train and the less-known Righteous Thieves, both involving Nazi art plundered during World War II. As for locations, both real-life and fictional art theft love glamorous capitals like Paris and London. Where the film industry exaggerates is the method: forged copies, disguises, and acrobatic roof-suspension instead of nighttime break-ins and improvised ladders. In films, masterpieces usually end up back on the wall. In reality, some never make it home. Caravaggio's Nativity was cut from its frame in Palermo in 1969 and has presumably been destroyed by the Mafia. Monet's Waterloo

title: Peace on Moscow’s terms: disinformation ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks
content:
On 10-11 November, Russia and Ukraine held US-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi. Before the meeting, the Kremlin had stated that it is genuinely ready for talks, yet its FIMI machine had been working overtime ahead of the negotiations, seeking to shape the talks before they even begun. By portraying Europe as an obstacle to peace, pushing to exclude it from the negotiating table, and presenting Moscow’s demands as non-negotiable, Russia tried to undermine Ukraine’s and Europe’s positions and maximise the concessions it can extract. For the Kremlin, disinformation is not just commentary on the peace process. It is part of its negotiating strategy.

Ahead of the peace talks in Abu Dhabi, Russia set out to argue that Europe should be kept out of the negotiations. Russian officials and pro-Kremlin commentators have been pushing the same message:

  • Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov insisted that the negotiations should involve only Russia, Ukraine, and the US as a mediator, arguing that European governments’ stance is ‘provocative’ and aimed at prolonging the war.
  • Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova declared that European countries have ‘no business’ being at the negotiating table.

title: US university students tell surveillance cameras to Flock off
content:
The privacy issues over the company’s surveillance cameras have caused protests in schools all over the country

Angela Nguyen, a senior at Stanford University, has been on a mission to make sure her school doesn’t use automated license plate readers, like those made by Flock Safety, for mass surveillance. The 21-year-old computer science major helped collect hundreds of signatures earlier this year from students, faculty, alumni and residents to demand that Stanford drop its current Flock contract and codify safeguards for similar tech tools the school may use in the future. The fear, Nguyen says, is that these cameras, which show where a vehicle was at a certain point in time, can be exploited to victimize vulnerable people.

title: Ethics Watchdog Urges Investigation Into Top Health Official, Alleging Conflict of Interest Over Hormone Therapy Policy
content:
A nonpartisan ethics watchdog group has asked for an investigation into whether a top Department of Health and Human Services official violated ethics laws after a recent ProPublica investigation revealed actions experts called “alarming” and an “obvious conflict of interest.” 

Alicia Jackson, who heads the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, publicly endorsed a change to federal health policy on hormone replacement therapies while owning stock in a company that provides access to menopause treatments. 

In a letter to the department’s inspector general, the Campaign Legal Center also questioned whether Jackson properly identified up to $400 million in underlying assets held by her husband’s investment firm. The center’s review identified an additional potential conflict — investments in a second firm that provides hormone treatments for menopause. 

Jackson, who heads the HHS agency that invests taxpayer money in medical technology and research, was recently placed on administrative leave, though health officials have not publicly explained why.

content:
Kun virkahenkilöt arvioivat julkisesti ministerin toimineen lainvastaisesti, hallituskumppanit eivät voi mennä sen taakse, että tapaus kuuluu ministerin toimivaltaan.

Jaa

Fingo on pyytänyt oikeuskansleria tarkastelemaan ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavion (ps.) Somalia-päätöksen lainmukaisuutta. Fingo sai toimenpidepyyntöä varten sisältöä jäsenistöltään.

Tavio linjasi maanantaina sosiaalisen median kanavissaan, että hän ei tule myöntämään hanketukea järjestöjen Somaliaan suunnitelluille hankkeille – asiaa ei oltu ilmoitettu hakukriteereissä.

Virallisia päätöksiä hanketuesta ei ole vielä tehty. Fingon tietojen mukaan ne on tarkoitus tehdä ensi viikolla.

Fingo on avannut aikaisemmassa tiedotteessaan kantaansa siitä, miksi Tavion toimintatapa on huonoa hallintoa.

title: Rechte Kaderschmiede: AfD-nahe Stiftung dürfte kein Geld bekommen
content:
Das Innenministerium prüft derzeit, ob die Desiderius-Erasmus-Stiftung mit Millionen Euro gefördert wird. Ihr müssen staatliche Mittel verwehrt bleiben.

Seit Jahren arbeitet sie darauf hin, bald könnte es soweit sein: Die AfD-nahe Desiderius-Erasmus-Stiftung (DES) möchte sich am Bundeshaushalt bedienen. Wenn es nach ihr geht, könnte sie bald Dutzende Millionen Euro staatliche Förderung erhalten. Doch ob die DES tatsächlich gefördert wird, prüft derzeit das Bundesinnenministerium von Alexander Dobrindt (CSU).

Um Geld aus der Staatskasse zu erhalten, müssen parteinahe Stiftungen gewährleisten, dass sie aktiv „für die freiheitliche demokratische Grundordnung sowie für den Gedanken der Völkerverständigung“ eintreten. Das verlangt seit 2024 das Stiftungsfinanzierungsgesetz. Bei der DES gibt es zahlreiche Aspekte, die gegen diese Voraussetzung sprechen. Deshalb müsste ihr die staatliche Förderung verwehrt bleiben. 

Dass die parteinahe Stiftung der extrem rechten AfD nicht für die freiheitliche demokratische Grundordnung eintritt, mag offensichtlich sein – jedoch muss das Innenministerium dies auch nachweisen, um der DES staatliche Unterstützung zu verweigern.

title: Georgia Fort stands up for journalists
content:
Independent journalist Georgia Fort is stepping up to call attention to retaliation against reporters, including her own ongoing prosecution for covering a protest at a Minnesota church against violence by immigration enforcement officers. Plus, some advice for the next Congress to fix the broken federal transparency system.

Georgia Fort is being prosecuted in a legally dubious case for her coverage of a protest against immigration authorities at a Minnesota church in January. She’s also been the subject of secret subpoenas. Unfortunately, while the scale of the government’s campaign against her is absurd, it’s not unprecedented — across the country, journalists are facing threats, arrests, and violence for keeping the public informed.

Now, Fort is partnering with the U.S. Press Freedom Tracker, a project of Freedom of the Press Foundation (FPF), as well as the Committee to Protect Journalists and Protect Democracy, on a video series highlighting the experiences of other journalists under attack and how the public’s right to know has been impacted.

title: Forskning i nord, regnskog i sør og propaganda i vår tid – Tildelinger til journalistikk høsten 2026
content:
Kaldt ytringsklima i nord, regnskogsbistand i Colombia og 10 forsøk om propaganda som er vanskelig å få øye på. Se de nye journalistikkprosjektene som fikk støtte høsten 2026.

På få år har nordområdene for alvor blitt en del av stormaktsspillet. NATO har styrket sitt nærvær i Arktis, Donald Trump har sagt at både Canada og Grønland bør innlemmes i USA, og Russland og Kina har markert sine strategiske interesser i regionen.

Hvordan preger dette kunnskapen vår om nordområdene? Det spør akademia-avisen Khrono seg i en serie som går gjennom 2027. Avisen har fått støtte til å undersøke hva den sikkerhetspolitiske situasjonen har å si for forskerne: hva de forsker på, hvem de samarbeider med, og hva de kan og tør å si offentlig.

– Dette er ikke et prosjekt om akademia for akademia, men noe bredere. Prosjektet handler om hvilken kunnskap som når den norske offentligheten i en situasjon der sikkerhetspolitiske hensyn får stadig større betydning.

title: Diamond Open Access for Scholarly Books: Lessons from Croatia
content:
Blog post by Iva Melinščak Zlodi (*)

The possibilities for making research openly accessible, and for enabling authors to retain control over their rights, are closely connected to the scholarly publishing models that dominate in different countries. This connection matters most in countries where resources to cover article and book processing charges (APCs and BPCs) are limited, and where publishing agreements that cover Open Access (OA) fees offer only partial solutions. Croatia offers a useful example of how established non-commercial publishing traditions can support more equitable access to scholarly knowledge.

title: Afgaaninaisen katse: “Olet muslimimies, mutta käytät tuollaisia lapsellisia vaatteita” – Taliban valvoo myös miesten pukeutumista
content:
Taliban valvoo jatkuvasti afganistanilaisten nuorten elämän pienimpiäkin yksityiskohtia. Mikä tahansa vaatekappale tai persoonallisen tyylin merkki voi johtaa kuulusteluihin ja rangaistuksiin Talibanin sääntöjen vastaisena. Matkapuhelinten tarkastuksista on tullut jokapäiväistä.

Rajoitukset koskevat etenkin naisia, mutta myös miesten elämänpiiristä on tullut näkymätön häkki. Jatkuva pelko on korvannut tulevaisuushaaveet. Painostus ja tarkkailu ovat lisänneet nuorten ahdistusta ja masennusta.

Neljä nuorta miestä kertoo nyt kokemuksistaan Kabulissa.

Farid (nimi muutettu), 27, asuu Khushhal Khanin alueella Kabulissa. Hän opiskeli yliopistossa taloustieteitä ja meni valmistuttuaan töihin yksityiseen firmaan.

Farid huokaisee muistellessaan esimerkkejä siitä, miten Talibanin moraalipoliisi on kohdellut häntä viiden viime vuoden aikana.

”Menin ruokakauppaan päälläni t-paita ja housut eli yksinkertaiset, tavalliset vaatteet. Käytän niitä usein, samoin kuin perahan tunbania (afganistanilainen perinteinen löysä asu). Vartaloni oli muuten peitossa, mutta t-paidassa oli lyhyet hihat.”

Kadulla Talibanin moraalipoliisit pysäyttivät Faridin ja alkoivat haukkua häntä.

title: Security Council LIVE: Fragile Gulf calm tested as threats to Hormuz shipping mount
content: Nearly nine months after Israeli and US strikes on Iran set off a regional war, the Gulf remains on a knife edge. Iran has all but closed the Strait of Hormuz, which carried a fifth of the world’s oil before the conflict. title: Demokratiaa ilman poliitikkoja? Poliittisen osallistumisen ja toimijuuden solmukohtia
content:
Monet kokevat mahdollisuutensa vaikuttaa pieniksi tai jopa olemattomiksi. Pystyvätkö demokraattiset innovaatiot antamaan valtaa ja toimijuutta tavan kansalaisille?

Suomea on tavattu pitää monin tavoin esimerkkinä onnistuneesta demokraattisesta yhteiskunnasta. Vaalien jälkeen tehtävät eduskuntatutkimukset ovat kuitenkin jo pitkään kertoneet eri yhteiskunnallisten ryhmien osallistumisen eriarvoistumisesta.

Karkeasti ottaen osallistumiseen vaikuttavat varallisuus, koulutustaso, perhetausta ja yleinen hyvinvointi. Osallistuminen siis seuraa osallisuutta. Suomeen on syntynyt osattomuuden ja osallistumattomuuden taskuja, joissa yhteiskuntaan osallistuminen on jotain, minkä koetaan kuuluvan muille ihmisille.

Esimerkiksi sosiologi Lotta Junnilainen on teoksessaan Lähiökylä — Tutkimus yhteisöllisyydestä ja eriarvoisuudesta kuvaillut ilmapiiriä lähiöissä, jossa kaikki yhteiskunnallinen vaikuttaminen koetaan itselle vieraaksi. Tällaisiin kokemuksiin liittyy monesti tunne syrjään jätetyksi tulemisesta ja oman äänen puutteesta.

title: Could you survive without Microsoft? Inside the costs of digital dependence
content:
When I arrived at work to discover that Outlook had vanished from my computer, I wondered how I was supposed to get through my working day. No emails. No calendar. No meeting invitations.

Then another thought crossed my mind: when did we become so dependent on a single technology company that losing access to one application could disrupt our entire working routine? And what is the financial and environmental cost of that dependence?

We regularly discuss sustainability in terms of reducing plastic, cutting carbon emissions and consuming less energy. But the digital systems we rely on every day also have huge environmental consequences.

As world leaders gather at the UN climate summit, Cop31, in Turkey, perhaps it is time to ask an uncomfortable question: can our digital economy really become sustainable when so much of it depends on a handful of technology companies?

The cloud may sound weightless, but it runs on data centres, electricity, cooling systems and hardware.

title: Maria da Penha -laki täytti 20 vuotta, mutta Brasilian naiset eivät vieläkään ole turvassa
content:
Brasilia on vahvistanut naisiin kohdistuvaa väkivaltaa torjuvaa lainsäädäntöään jo kahden vuosikymmenen ajan. Silti tuhannet naiset joutuvat vuosittain lähisuhdeväkivallan uhreiksi. Ongelma ei kuitenkaan välttämättä ole lain puutteissa, vaan yhteiskunnallisissa asenteissa ja viranomaisten kyvyssä taata naisille todellista turvallisuutta.

Toukokuussa vuonna 1983 brasilialainen farmaseutti Maria da Penha Maia Fernandes oli nukkumassa kotonaan, kun hän heräsi yhtäkkiä kovaan pamaukseen ja voimakkaaseen kipuun selässään. Marian mies, joka oli ollut väkivaltainen häntä ja heidän yhteisiä lapsiaan kohtaan jo aiemmin, oli yrittänyt tappaa Marian ampumalla häntä selkään. Maria halvaantui hyökkäyksessä, joka ei jäänyt viimeiseksi laatuaan, vaan mies yritti tappaa hänet myöhemmin vielä uudestaan samana vuonna sähköiskulla Marian ollessa kylvyssä. Maria selvisi hengissä molemmista hyökkäyksistä ja on tämän jälkeen omistanut elämänsä taistelulle naisten oikeuksien puolesta.

title: EU:n ulkoasiainneuvosto keskustelee Venäjän hyökkäyssodasta ja Lähi-idän tilanteesta
content:
EU:n ulkoministerit tapaavat Brysselissä maanantaina 16. marraskuuta. Suomea kokouksessa edustaa poliittinen valtiosihteeri Pasi Rajala.

Kokouksen aiheita ovat Venäjän hyökkäyssota Ukrainassa sekä Lähi-idän tilanne, jonka osalta keskitytään erityisesti Syyriaan.

Ministerit keskustelevat Ukrainan vahvistamisesta talven lähestyessä. Venäjän iskut Ukrainaan ovat syksyn aikana kiihtyneet ja aiheuttaneet yhä enemmän siviiliuhreja. Suomi painottaa tarvetta jatkaa EU:n vahvaa poliittista, taloudellista ja sotilaallista tukea Ukrainalle. Lisäksi humanitaarista apua Ukrainaan tulee jatkaa ja lisätä. Painetta Venäjää kohtaan on lisättävä erityisesti pakotteiden sekä EU:n yhteisten tiukempien viisumitoimien muodossa.

Ulkoasiainneuvoston yhteydessä järjestetään myös ministerikokous alueiden välisestä turvallisuudesta ja yhteyspolitiikasta sekä kansainvälinen Ukrainan miinanraivauskonferenssi.

As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January, party leaders say they intend to hold Trump officials accountable with stepped-up hearings and investigations. The administration, however, has responded with threats to launch its own investigations into lawmakers for carrying out their oversight responsibilities.

“The oversight function of Congress is well established by the founders. It’s a normal part of government. The separation of powers requires oversight,” says Brad Adams, co-founder of The Rule of Law Project, which seeks to provide outside accountability due to what he describes as the administration’s refusal to investigate “obvious cases of corruption.”

title: Discover the ECHOLOT foundation and its main pillars
content:
The ECHOLOT foundation consists of four pillars that will enable cultural heritage provide cultural organisations with a user-friendly system that enables them to create and/or modify content once and publish it on multiple platforms while receiving enriched data in return.

ECHOLOT aims to deliver innovative, user-friendly, accessible technical solutions and collaboration models that interconnect and enrich cultural heritage datasets developed by a consortium with strong ties to major EU infrastructure projects, including the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC), ECHOES, and the Data Space for Cultural Heritage (DS4CH).

The activities and objectives of ECHOLOT are based on four key pillars:

  • Integration and Interoperability – a software suite that will be seamlessly integrated into the ECCCH infrastructure as a service for the collaborative curation, enrichment, management, publication and dissemination of cultural heritage data.

title: Emilia Palonen on Vuoden tieteentekijä 2026
content:
Emilia Palonen työskentelee valtio-opin apulaisprofessorina ja datafikaation ohjelmajohtajana Helsingin yliopiston valtiotieteellisessä tiedekunnassa.

- Emilia Palosen ansiot eivät rajoitu omiin tieteellisiin meriitteihin, vaan hän on kantanut tutkimustyönsä rinnalla laajasti vastuuta tieteellisissä seuroissa, järjestöissä ja luottamustehtävissä. Tällainen korvaamattoman tärkeä työ jää usein piiloon, vaikka ilman sitä tiedeyhteisö ei toimisi, Tieteentekijöiden puheenjohtaja Antti Pajala sanoo.

Palosen panos on ollut erityisen merkittävä avoimen tieteen ja avoimen julkaisemisen kehittämisessä. Tieteellisten seurain valtuuskunnassa sekä avoimen tieteen kansallisessa koordinaatiossa hän on ollut rakentamassa käytäntöjä, jotka parantavat tutkimuksen läpinäkyvyyttä, saavutettavuutta ja yhteiskunnallista vaikuttavuutta. Hän on ollut mukana myös kehittämässä tutkimustiedon infrastruktuureja ja tiedon saatavuutta tukevaa yhteistyötä, joka hyödyttää koko tiedeyhteisöä.

title: Tilastokeskus korjasi tammi–syyskuun asuntomarkkinalukuja – lokakuussa tehtiin yli 3 000 digitaalista asuntokauppaa
content:
Digitaalisten DIAS-kauppojen osuus kaikista kiinteistönvälittäjien tekemistä vanhojen asunto-osakkeiden kaupoista on kasvanut tänä vuonna aiemmin raportoitua hitaammin, kun asuntokauppoja on solmittu tammi–syyskuussa yhdeksän prosenttia luultua enemmän. Tilastokeskuksen 10.11. korjaamien kauppalukujen perusteella 60 prosenttia tänä aikana välitetyistä vanhojen asunto-osakkeiden kaupoista tehtiin DIAS-kauppoina.

Oikaistut luvut muuttavat myös DIASin aiemmin ilmoittamia yksittäisten kuukausien markkinaosuuksia. Heinäkuu säilyy edelleen DIAS-kaupan ennätyskuukautena, mutta aiemmin ilmoitetun 73 prosentin sijaan 66 prosenttia välittäjien kuun aikana tekemistä asunto-osakekaupoista solmittiin DIAS-alustalla.

Välittäjien tekemien asunto-osakekauppojen määrä oikaistuissa tilastoissa kasvoi eniten – lähes 15 prosenttia – syyskuussa. DIAS-kauppojen osuus kaikista välittäjien tekemistä vanhojen asunto-osakkeiden kaupoista syyskuussa oli siten mediatiedotteessa kerrotun 71 prosentin sijaan 62 prosenttia. Syyskuussa 2025 vastaava luku oli 57 prosenttia.

title: Uusikuu-yhtye on Vuoden ulkosuomalainen 2026
content:
Suomi-Seura ry on valinnut Vuoden ulkosuomalaiseksi 2026 suomalaissaksalaisen Uusikuu-yhtyeen, joka viettää tänä vuonna 20-vuotisjuhlavuottaan. Tunnustus myönnetään yhtyeen pitkäjänteisestä työstä suomalaisen musiikkiperinteen ja suomen kielen tunnetuksi tekemiseksi sekä myönteisen Suomi-kuvan rakentamisesta.

Yhtyeen musiikki herättää kiinnostusta Suomeen ja suomalaiseen kulttuuriin myös sellaisten kuulijoiden keskuudessa, jotka eivät osaa suomea.

title: Kasvuyritysten rahoituksen saatavuutta tulee parantaa
content:
Erityisesti nuoret, aineettomiin investointeihin nojaavat yritykset tarvitsevat sijoittajia, joilla on riittävästi pääomaa ja kykyä rahoittaa yrityksiä useiden tappiollisten vuosien ajan. Tämä käy ilmi eduskunnan tarkastusvaliokunnan tilaamasta Etla-tutkimuksesta, jossa tarkastellaan yritysrahoituksen saatavuutta ja toteutunutta käyttöä. Tutkimuksessa ehdotetaan myös, että kasvuun tähtäävien julkisten avustusten nykyistä vahvempaa kohdentamista mikro- ja pienyrityksiin tulee kokeilla ja arvioida sen vaikutuksia.

Suomalaiset yritykset rahoittavat toimintaansa ennen kaikkea omilla voitoillaan ja pankkilainalla. Muita keskeisiä rahoitusmuotoja ovat omistajien tekemät pääomasijoitukset ja erilainen julkinen rahoitus kuten avustukset, lainat, takaukset ja verotuet.

Vuonna 2023 kertyneet voittovarat kasvoivat runsaalla puolella yrityksistä. Pankkilainaa oli noin 32 prosentilla yrityksistä. Pankkilainan käyttö oli yleisintä 6–10 vuotta toimineissa yrityksissä. Rahoituksen käyttö vaihteli kuitenkin enemmän yrityksen koon kuin iän mukaan.

Eri rahoitusmuotojen yhteiskäyttö oli yrityksissä melko vähäistä, sanoo Etlan tutkimusjohtaja Heli Koski.

title: Essee: Mikä oli se raja, johon illiberaalin populismin nousu tänä vuonna törmäsi?
content:
Orbán menetti vallan Unkarissa, Serbian opiskelijat voittivat ja demokraatit ottivat vallan Yhdysvaltojen kongressissa – ja demokratian luisu pysähtyi näissä maissa ainakin toistaiseksi. Yritykset rakentaa illiberaalia tiedon infrastruktuuria kaatuivat lopulta hallintojen omiin virheisiin, jotka osoittautuivat kestämättömän suuriksi, väittää Eurooppalaisen Suomen erityisasiantuntija Samuel Tammekann. Mutta riittääkö se pelastamaan demokratian?

Illiberaalin populismin voittokulku on ollut itsestäänselväksi muodostunut synkkä suuri kertomus 2020-luvun ihmiselle. Kysymys ei ole enää ollut, mikä on demokratiakehityksen suunta, vaan milloin ja missä seuraava taantuminen tapahtuu. 

Raporttimme alkuperäinen, Trumpin toisen kauden alun varjostama tutkimuskysymys kuului seuraavasti: miten EU voi puolustaa arvopohjaista järjestelmää ja demokratiaa maailman murroksessa? Kysymys lähti oletuksesta Yhdysvaltojen strategisesta vetäytymisestä ja uusien puolustuslinjojen rakentamisesta ”viimeiselle liberaalidemokraattiselle suurvallalle” hyvin uudenlaisessa ajassa.

title: Join the Europa Nostra Hub in Athens’ Pan-European conference on cultural tourism and heritage
content:
The Europa Nostra Heritage Hub in Athens, operated by Elliniki Etairia – Society for the Environment and Cultural Heritage, and Europa Nostra will host the Pan-European Conference, “Cultural Tourism and Heritage: Threats and Opportunities”, on 10-11 December 2026 in Athens. 

Organised in the frame of the EU-funded European Heritage Hub, the conference aims to answer the key question: How can Europe reconcile the growing pressures of tourism with the protection of its cultural heritage?

Representatives of European institutions, international organisations such as UNESCO, representatives from the Greek ministries of Culture and Tourism, academia, civil society, and the cultural heritage and tourism sectors will gather for a high-level exchange on the challenges shaping Europe’s cultural and territorial future. 

From the resilience of historic cities and cultural landscapes to sustainable tourism, housing pressures and the role of civil society, the conference will provide a forum for dialogue, reflection and the exchange of perspectives.

title: ‘You cannot build peace on a burning planet,’ UN chief tells Cop31 in farewell speech
content:
António Guterres says climate action central to every aspect of UN’s work, as leaders depart Cop31 and talks go on

Tackling the climate crisis is central to all of human life and must be at the forefront of global governance, the outgoing UN secretary general has said in an emotional farewell address at the Cop31 climate summit.

“You cannot build peace on a burning planet,” António Guterres said at his final climate press conference as secretary general on Friday. “You cannot eradicate poverty when climate disasters keep throwing people back into it. You cannot promise young people a better future while destroying the natural systems on which that future depends.”

title: Israel Bans Travel for Prominent Palestinian Rights Defender
content:
(Beirut) – Israeli authorities on November 13, 2026, imposed an international travel ban on Shawan Jabarin, the head of Al-Haq, a leading Palestinian human rights organization in the occupied West Bank. The travel ban comes in the context of increasing attacks against Palestinians and civil society groups in the Occupied Palestinian Territory. 

Al-Haq, along with the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights and Al-Mezan Center for Human Rights, are continuing their critical human rights work despite US sanctions for engaging with the International Criminal Court. Human Rights Watch, with three other human rights organizations, filed a lawsuit in US federal court on August 11 seeking to have the sanctions struck down.

title: Serbia’s Experiment: Combining Democracy & Meritocracy
content:
It is no less true for being a cliché that innovation comes mostly from the edges. Whether in politics, markets or technology, fresh approaches emerge from the periphery and the margins rather than the well-established core. When it comes to the governing practices and institutions of democracies, innovation tends also to arrive not from the mature states, but the fledgling ones, less bound by legacy structures and entrenched constituencies.

That is the case today in Serbia, which only became a sovereign state in its own right in 2006 after its split from Montenegro following the breakup of Cold War-era Yugoslavia that began unraveling in 1992.

For the last 14 years, it has been ruled by a corrupt autocrat, Aleksandr Vučić, in the mold of Hungary’s Viktor Orbán. When his regime became too much to bear, a revolt by the nation’s youth erupted. The straw that broke the camel’s back came in November 2024 when the concrete canopy of a train station in Novi Sad collapsed and killed 16 people. Its shoddy construction was blamed on corruption in building permits and lax oversight inspections.
