title: Freedom House Launches New US Democracy Tracker, Identifies Serious Concerns
content:
WASHINGTON—Freedom House, in partnership with the Charles F. Kettering Foundation, today launched the US Democracy Tracker, a new, quarterly assessment of democratic institutions and fundamental freedoms in the United States. The inaugural edition identifies government accountability and freedom of the media as areas of “serious concern.”

“Near record-high numbers of Americans just exercised their civic duty to vote in the midterm elections. Yet a robust democracy is defined not simply by elections, but by how our constitutional freedoms are protected in practice. Our new US Democracy Tracker offers a vital measure of the state of our freedoms at an important time in our democracy,” said Jamie Fly, CEO of Freedom House. 

Since 1973, Freedom House has assessed political rights and civil liberties in over 200 countries and territories. The US Democracy Tracker is derived from the same rigorous research methods to assess conditions crucial to democracy in the United States. It examines eight categories including free elections, political competition, accountability, access to justice, media freedom, and other fundamental rights.

title: Sudan’s Empty Warehouses Leave Millions Without Shelter
content:
As relief stocks run out, expanding drone warfare, foreign arms supplies and divided diplomacy are worsening one of the world’s largest humanitarian emergencies

By Ramesh Jaura

BERLIN | 12 November 2026 (IDN) – Winter nights in Darfur and northern Sudan can be bitterly cold. Many families displaced by war are nevertheless sleeping beneath plastic sheets, in crowded public buildings or beside damaged houses.

Some have returned to their towns only to find that their homes have been destroyed or looted, water and electricity are unavailable and the nearest clinic is closed.

The UN Refugee Agency, UNHCR, and the International Organization for Migration, IOM, warned on 6 November that their stocks of tents, blankets and other essentials were almost exhausted. An estimated 15.4 million people need emergency shelter or basic household items, but available funds allow relief agencies to give priority to only about one in ten.

Even that reduced target has not been met. Only 936,000 people have received assistance.

Mohamed Refaat, head of IOM’s mission in Sudan, said the agency’s warehouses were empty. A convoy of 16 trucks that reached Darfur carried the last of its available stocks.
snippet:
As relief stocks run out, expanding drone warfare, foreign arms supplies and divided diplomacy are worsening one of the world’s largest humanitarian emergencies

title: The SS United States has been deliberately sunk – this is how marine life will colonise the world’s largest artificial reef
content:
As a marine ecologist and keen scuba diver, I’ve long been fascinated by what happens when a large structure is introduced to the sea. Within hours, microscopic organisms begin colonising its surfaces, forming a thin biological layer. Over the following months and years, barnacles, mussels, sponges and other marine life become established, creating a new habitat that attracts fish and a diverse range of species.

This week, one of the world’s most famous ocean liners, the SS United States, was sunk off the coast of Florida. At 302 metres long, it has become the world’s largest artificial reef. It is a very exciting prospect to one day dive on such a giant, and to see how it changes as marine life makes it home.

The SS United States was built as a luxury ocean liner, and its maiden voyage in 1952 captured the coveted Blue Riband by crossing the Atlantic in only three days and ten hours – a passenger liner record that remains unbroken.

title: "Don't F#*k It Up, Democrats": David Sirota on Direction of Party & Fight Over Jeffries & Schumer
content:
With Democrats set to take control of both chambers of Congress in January, Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders says he will not support Chuck Schumer for another term as the Democratic Senate leader, calling for the party to move in “a new and bold direction.” Michigan Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin has said she will not support Schumer unless he presents a plan to govern differently, and several senators-elect have called for new leadership or declined to endorse Schumer. Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is considering challenging Schumer. Meanwhile, Hakeem Jeffries is facing questions about his leadership of House Democrats after 11 of the party’s members missed a key vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

After “a big win for the populist wing of the Democratic Party, … it would be a betrayal for that election to result immediately in the Democratic Party simply responding by reelecting the same leadership,” says David Sirota, editor-in-chief of The Lever.

La famille Moomin vit dans une vallée reculée de Finlande. Petits personnages tout en rondeur, inspirés des trolls traditionnels, ils ressemblent à des hippopotames. title: More Than 1,300 Diplomatic Passports Missing in Vanuatu, Report Finds
content:
A damning parliamentary report in Vanuatu has found more than 1,300 diplomatic passports went missing in recent years and remain unaccounted for.

The report by Vanuatu’s Public Accounts Committee, released on Tuesday and obtained by OCCRP, revealed that 1,390 diplomatic passports went missing between 2019 and 2024, with 1,301 disappearing in 2024 alone.

The committee also found significant irregularities in the processing and issuance of the documents, including alleged misuse by the country’s prime minister and foreign minister.

It is the latest passport controversy for the small Pacific island country of roughly 340,000 people, whose so-called “golden passport” program has attracted a colorful cast of wealthy investors ranging from spies and fugitives to sanctioned oligarchs and influencer Andrew Tate.

The report followed several years of mounting concerns over the country’s issuance of diplomatic passports.

title: When Salvador Dali Met Sigmund Freud, and Changed Freud’s Mind About Surrealism (1938)
content:
The close associations between Surrealism and Freudian psychoanalysis were liberally encouraged by the most famous proponent of the movement, Salvador Dalí, who considered himself a devoted follower of Freud. We don’t have to wonder what the founder of psychoanalysis would have thought of his self-appointed protégé.

We have them recording, in their own words, their impressions of their one and only meeting—which took place in July of 1938, at Freud’s home in London. Freud was 82, Dalí 34. We also have sketches Dalí made of Freud while the two sat together. Their memories of events, shall we say, differ considerably, or at least they seemed totally bewildered by each other. (Freud pronounced Dalí a “fanatic.”)

In any case, there’s absolutely no way the encounter could have lived up to Dalí’s expectations, as the Freud Museum London notes:

[Dalí] had already travelled to Vienna several times but failed to make an introduction. Instead, he wrote in his autobiography, he spent his time having “long and exhaustive imaginary conversations” with his hero, at one point fantasizing that he “came home with me and stayed all night clinging to the curtains of my room in the Hotel Sacher.”

title: Ukraine Starlink speed restrictions in effect again, Zelenskyy says
content:
KYIV – Limitations affecting Starshield, the military version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite system, appear to be back in Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Thursday.

“Unfortunately, our units have been recording significant disruptions to Starshield’s operations over the territory of Ukraine for several days now – along the entire front line and in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine,” Zelenskyy said in a statement.

About a month ago, Ukraine reported a drop in connectivity for objects traveling faster than 161 km/h, which prevented its defensive systems, especially its interceptors, from working properly. The restriction was lifted on Oct. 24. In his statement, Zelenskyy said the disruptions were not due to a malfunction, but once again to a systematic speed restriction.

“For us, this primarily means a significant complication in intercepting Russian jet-powered drones,” Zelenskyy said.

The latest restrictions have already allowed several Russian drones to get through Ukrainian air defense and kill more Ukrainians, he added.

title: SAFA ja ATL: Ammatin harjoittaminen rakennusalalla ei saa riippua tutkinnon suoritusmaasta
content:
Orpon hallitus on päättänyt, ettei se esitä eduskunnalle muutosta lakiin rakentamisen suunnittelu- ja työnjohtotehtävissä toimivien pätevyyden toteamisesta. Muutos olisi mahdollistanut pätevyystodistuksen hakemisen myös niille, jotka ovat suorittaneet tutkintonsa EU- tai ETA-maiden ulkopuolella.

”Hallituksen päätös siirtää valitettavasti jälleen eteenpäin ratkaisua, jota koko rakennusalalla on odotettu pitkään”, SAFAn puheenjohtaja Asko Takala sanoo.

Iso osa EU- tai ETA-maiden ulkopuolella tutkintonsa suorittaneista arkkitehdeista ja muista rakennusalan ammattilaisista ei tällä hetkellä voi hakea rakentamislain mukaista pätevyyttä osoittavaa todistusta. Todistus on edellytys sille, että henkilö voi toimia vastuullisena suunnittelijana tai työnjohtajana rakentamisluvan edellyttävissä hankkeissa.

Tämä asettaa monet ulkomailla kouluttautuneet, pitkään Suomessa työskennelleet ammattilaiset eriarvoiseen asemaan.

“Väliinputoajista iso osa on suomalaisia arkkitehteja. Tilanne on kestämätön. Kaikille rakennusalan ammattilaisille pitää taata yhdenvertainen mahdollisuus harjoittaa ammattiaan ja osoittaa ammattipätevyytensä, tutkinnon suoritusmaasta riippumatta”, Takala sanoo.

title: Hannele Lampela: Näin tuhoamme suomen kielen ja säästämme selvää rahaa!
content:
Olen aina ajatellut, että suomen kielen, kirjallisuuden ja kulttuurin puolustaminen on tärkeä osa maanpuolustusta. Että sille on syynsä, miksi vihollinen aina ensimmäisenä pyrkii tuhoamaan painetun sanan, kirjastot ja painotalot, kuten nyt vaikka Venäjä on toiminut Ukrainalta riistämillään alueilla. Mutta vastikään opin, että höpö höpö! Kulttuuri onkin luksuspalvelu! Ja koska tietysti vastustan kaikenlaista humputtelua (etenkin taloudellista sellaista), ajattelin nyt säästää kaikkien vaivaa ja rahaa ja tuhota koko suomen kielen. Koska mitäpä sitä sellaisella turhakkeella mitään.  

Ainahan me voimme puhua vaikka englantia tai venäjää.  

Ajan trendien mukaisesti pyysin tekoälyä listaamaan keinot sen täydelliseen tuhoamiseen.

content:
Eduskunnasta vetäytyvä Ben Zyskowicz muisteli Uuden Jutun haastattelussa taas kerran taistolaisuutta. Ymmärsin. Nuoruuden kokemukset pinttyvät mieleen.

Taistolaisuudesta on kuitenkin yli puoli vuosisataa. Sen ajan nuoret ovat eläkeläisiä, ja nykyiset syntyivät maailmaan, jossa Neuvostoliittoa ei enää ollut.

Olen kauan ihmetellyt populistioikeiston kykyä nähdä mielikuvituskommunisteja sänkynsä alla. Heitä löytyy ilmastotutkijoista, kaupunkisuunnittelijoista ja ihmisistä, jotka haluaisivat saada palkallaan asunnon.

Totuuden jälkeisen ajan somevirroissa uhkakuvat ovat sitä klikattavampia, mitä hatarammin ne ovat olemassa. Mutta voisiko jo laittaa nämä pulinat pois?

Progressiiviset voittavat New Yorkissa, mutta koko maassa tarvitaan paljon harmaampia keskustalaisia. Harmaus ei kuitenkaan korvaa ehdokkaan tilannetajua tai ratkaisukykyä. Vaalivoitot lähtevät ihmisistä, joilla on omat tarpeensa ja odotuksensa. Entä jos niiden ymmärtäminen on tärkeämpää kuin ehdokkaan sijoittaminen janalle?

title: Relax, the embassy of Finland in Canberra is open again
content: Here's something I never thought I'd write: the embassy of Finland in Australia has gone viral. It all started when the Finnish embassy in Canberra announced it would be closed on Tuesday, 10 November, for “an internal planning day” (which turned out to be an end-of-the-year sauna day for the team). Nobody knows why, but the internet lost its mind. Thousands of people all across the world started posting memes on social media about how devastated they were, or how the closure had ruined their day. Like this video with more than 11 million views, or this one joking that riots in Paris were sparked by news of the closure. If you're not familiar with meme culture, the joke is that there is no joke. Nobody actually cares that a small embassy in Canberra is closed for a day (no offence to the staff). The fun is in everyone pretending it's a global catastrophe. But why this particular embassy, and why now? One theory is that the embassy's account was already gaining more attention after a post promoting an all-expenses-paid trip to Finland for 16 singles from across the world, “complete with dinner dates with local Finns” and organised by Finland's national tourism organisation.

title: US public workers are fighting to protect their jobs from AI – and some are winning
content:
As governments adopt AI, workers are gaining ground in how it’s used and securing safeguards against its harms

In the shadow of Silicon Valley, workers for the city of Oakland, California, worry the region will deploy AI systems that could increase surveillance and inaccurately evaluate their performance. Pushing for protections to ensure workers won’t be laid off or disciplined by AI, their union overwhelmingly voted on 22 October to authorize a strike, with 94.1% in favor.

“We just want the city administration to really be intentional about how it’s engaging with AI products,” said Julian Ware, an Oakland spatial data administrator and member of International Federation of Professional and Technical Engineers Local 21. “Sometimes with a fancy new toy, it actually costs more, it’s more difficult to implement and the results are not as good.”

title: How groomers operate – and why victims become trapped
content:
Entertainer and children’s author David Walliams is alleged to have used his fame to approach teenage girls, in some cases reportedly initiating sexual contact with them. Walliams has denied the allegations, but the claims raise some familiar tropes about grooming: why did she go, why didn’t she say no, why didn’t she tell anyone?

After a legal battle, ITV News and The Guardian have now published the findings of a three-year investigation into Walliams, reporting allegations that date back to 2003.

In this and other cases, there will always be people who focus not on the claims, but on the young person and what they should have done differently. Linguistic research on how grooming actually works suggests that this instinct is exactly the result that grooming is designed to produce.

Many people imagine sexual grooming as a recognisable and clearly staged process. Build friendship, then trust, then secrecy – all leading towards the offender’s ultimate goal of sexual gratification. But if this were the case, victims could notice the steps and walk away.

title: Relatives of Slain Freedom Summer Activists Celebrate Scott Colom's Historic Senate Win in Mississippi
content:
Democrat Scott Colom has defeated incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first African American senator since the post-Civil War Reconstruction era. The electoral breakthrough is particularly meaningful given Mississippi’s history in the civil rights movement. In 1964, three civil rights activists — James Chaney, Michael Schwerner and Andrew Goodman — were murdered by the Ku Klux Klan after traveling to the state to register Black voters. We speak with two of their relatives about Colom’s stunning upset.

“I believe that people were voting for help. And they evidently saw something in Mr. Colom that made them feel like that they could hope again and that he was the help that was needed,” says Angela Lewis, the daughter of James Chaney.

“The people of Mississippi have spoken,” adds David Goodman, the brother of Andrew Goodman. “And we have to cease and desist this divide-and-conquer business, because it’s not in our collective interest as the United States of America.”

title: World heading for ‘irrevocable overshoot’ of global temperature thresholds, analysis warns
content:
Failure to cut emissions will ‘consign humanity to disasters they are unable to adapt to’, report says

The world is heading for an “irrecoverable overshoot” of global temperature thresholds that will plunge billions of people into disastrous climate impacts because governments have stalled for so long to cut planet-heating emissions, analysis has found.

Under current policies, the planet will heat up by 2.7C on average by the end of the century compared with preindustrial times, the report by Climate Action Tracker (CAT) found. This is up slightly from a prediction of 2.6C in the group’s analysis conducted last year.

title: UK Arrests 349 in Nationwide Money Laundering Crackdown
content:
The UK's National Crime Agency (NCA) announced that 349 people had been arrested in a nationwide crackdown on businesses suspected of laundering criminal proceeds. During October, police inspected or raided 3,029 premises, including barbershops, vape stores and other cash-intensive businesses, seizing approximately $2.9 million in cash and obtaining court orders to freeze another $4.9 million in bank accounts. Authorities also identified or prevented an estimated $5.5 million in tax evasion and seized illicit goods worth nearly $9 million.

The operation was the latest phase of Operation Machinize, a nationwide campaign targeting businesses used to conceal criminal profits. An earlier phase of the crackdown resulted in more than 900 arrests and inspections of over 2,700 businesses. The NCA estimates that at least $1.3 billion in criminal proceeds is laundered through such businesses in the UK annually. The agency said the campaign is increasingly focused on identifying the criminal networks behind the businesses rather than just individual premises.

title: Australia signs up to EU’s Horizon Europe research program
content:
BRUSSELS — Australia’s Industry Minister Tim Ayres formally signed the country up to Horizon Europe on Thursday, giving the country’s researchers access to the EU’s €95 billion research and innovation program.

Australia will join Pillar II of the program, which funds research into areas including advanced computing tech, critical minerals, health, climate and clean energy. From January, Australian organizations will be eligible for funding on the same terms as EU countries and will be able to lead project consortia.

The move will be a “boon for Australian science, research and innovation,” Ayres said in a statement, adding that “the big challenges facing Australia and the world cannot be solved by any one country working alone.”

The signing formalizes negotiations concluded in June. Australian organizations have already taken part in 239 Horizon Europe projects, with nearly one in four applications selected, according to the European Commission.

title: Scott Colom Wins Stunning Victory, Becomes Mississippi's First Black Senator Since Reconstruction
content:
Democrat Scott Colom has made history as Mississippi’s first Democratic senator since 1982 — and its first African American senator since the post-Civil War Reconstruction era. Colom narrowly defeated Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in a state that President Trump won by nearly 23 points in 2024. Colom’s victory brings the incoming Senate Democratic caucus to 55. Colom gave his victory speech on Wednesday at the historically Black Tougaloo College, just miles from where civil rights activist Medgar Evers was murdered in 1963 by a member of the Ku Klux Klan.

“There were times that I couldn’t get donors to answer the phone; they did not believe a moment like this was possible. But I kept the faith,” said Colom. “There are so many people that had faith in Mississippi at times where it seemed impossible, people like Medgar Evers.”

title: CFP: SAA Visual Materials Section 2027 Win-Ventory
content:
“Winventory” is fast approaching!

VMS invites archivists to share their work wins with our community as part of “Winventory’s” series of 5-7 minute lightning talks this coming January.

This year has been a difficult one, marked by uncertainty, change, and ongoing challenges across our communities and institutions. We hope to create a space to share some of our wins, encouraging reflection, creativity, connection, and resilience. We would love to see what made you pause, smile, or say “this is why I do this.”

Don’t know where to start? Here are some ideas:

• A visual materials project that brought people together

• A win (big or small) that came out of working with visual content

• A collaboration engaging between archive and artist

• A surprising visual discovery that brought a moment of joy

• A behind-the-scenes story from the stacks

• A successful digitization or outreach initiative

Submit your idea by November 20th! Please send proposals – a brief paragraph sharing your lighting talk idea – or any questions to Maggie McCready at mgmc@loc.gov!

title: CODATA RDMT – Call for suggested additional terms now open; deadline 10 December 2026
content:
The CODATA Research Data Management Terminology (RDMT) https://vocabs.ardc.edu.au/viewById/685 gathers the key terms needed for a common understanding of the research data management domain. The RDMT is revised by the CODATA RDM Terminology Working Group, shared for public review, and then confirmed and finalised biennially.

The RDMT will be once again revised in 2027. In preparation for this process, we are inviting your ideas for any terms that you feel are missing from the current version (v002) of the Terminology.

Before suggesting terms, please read the RDMT scope statement, available here:

https://codata.org/initiatives/data-science-and-stewardship/rdm-terminology-wg/

Once you have verified that the term you’re interested in is a) in scope; and b) not already present within the Terminology, please add it to our suggested additions form here:

https://forms.gle/YyHGETo3FPwixPGB7

The form will close on 10 December 2026. Terms will be discussed by the 2027 RDMT Working Group.

If you are a RDM expert and interested in committing to the 2027 RDMT Working Group, please look out for the call for applications which will be advertised soon.

title: Uusi jäsen esittäytyy: Xoompoint Oy
content:
COSSin verkosto on laajentunut Xoompoint Oy:n liittyessä mukaan yhteisöjäseneksi!

Xoompoint tuo oppimisen osaksi työn arkea. Meiltä saat tietoturva- ja muut valmiskurssit, organisaatiollesi räätälöidyt verkkokoulutukset sekä oppimisalustan – ja tutut asiantuntijat tueksesi.

Valmiskursseilla pääset suoraan kouluttamaan. Tietoturvakurssimme auttavat henkilöstöä tunnistamaan arjen uhkia ja toimimaan turvallisesti. Muut valmiskurssit täydentävät osaamista työelämän eri tarpeisiin. Kun valmis ei riitä, suunnittelemme ja toteutamme teidän näköisenne verkkokurssit esimerkiksi perehdytykseen tai henkilöstön ja kumppanien kouluttamiseen. Omatoimisille tekijöille tarjoamme sisällöntuotannon työkalut ja koulutuksen.

Voit aloittaa yhdestä kurssista tai rakentaa kanssamme koko verkko-oppimisen kokonaisuuden.

Asiakkaitamme ovat eri kokoiset yritykset, julkishallinnon organisaatiot ja järjestöt. Palvelemme muun muassa teollisuutta, kaupan alaa, ravintola- ja palvelualoja, sosiaali- ja terveysalaa sekä koulutusorganisaatioita. Meihin ovat luottaneet esimerkiksi Meyer Turku, Metsä Group, Restel, Etra, Euronics, Beamex, Varha ja Väylävirasto.

title: Starlink Mobile is another Musk power grab
content:
In October, Elon Musk’s Starlink was back in the news. Ukraine’s access to the satellite communications network had once again been curtailed, following a previous restriction in 2022. Questions swirled about who was behind it: Musk himself, or the US government under Donald Trump.

There are in fact two Starlink services on offer to countries like Ukraine. There’s the commercial version we know by that name, but there’s also Starshield, the defense-oriented one that the US government has a lot more control over. Musk admitted he did limit Ukraine’s access to Starlink, but Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also suggested the US government was behind the restrictions placed on its access to Starshield. Once the service was restored, the truth of that claim was left unresolved.

The incident revived an unresolved issue from the original shutdown four years earlier: how was it that one man could wield so much power over the communications infrastructure of sovereign countries, not to mention that so many people depend on? At the time, it seemed clear that something was going to have to be done about it, but then the urgency behind that effort seemed to wane.

title: Etäopetuksen päivä tarjosi uusia näkökulmia ja nosti esiin vanhoja aarteita
content:
Perjantaina 6.11.2026 vietettiin Etäopetuksen päivää teemalla Pedagogista muutosta luomassa etä- ja hybridiopetuksessa. Järjestimme vuosittaisen verkkotapahtuman yhteistyössä Kvs-säätiön Etäkoulu Kulkurin kanssa.

Päivän aikana tarkasteltiin etä- ja hybridiopetuksen mahdollisuuksia eri koulutusasteilla sekä Suomessa että kansainvälisesti. Puheenvuoroissa ja keskusteluissa nousivat esiin muun muassa tekoälyn vaikutukset opetukseen ja osaamisen arviointiin, oppijoiden erilaiset tarpeet, uudet teknologiat sekä etäopetus oppimisen ja osallisuuden mahdollistajana.

Yksi erityisen ilahduttava keskustelu syntyi virtuaalisten oppimisympäristöjen äärellä, kun osallistujat nostivat esiin vuosien takaisten AVO-hankkeiden tuotoksia. Aikoinaan kehitetyt virtuaalimaailmojen opetuskäytön materiaalit herättivät jälleen kiinnostusta. Monet pedagogiset kysymykset ovat edelleen ajankohtaisia, vaikka teknologia ympärillä on muuttunut.

Ensi vuonna vietetään Suomen eOppimiskeskus ry:n 25-vuotisjuhlavuotta. Ehkäpä nyt onkin oiva hetki palata myös vanhojen hankkeiden ja arkistojen äärelle katsomaan, millaisia aarteita sieltä edelleen löytyy!

title: Europe's invaders have red claws
content: Lake Milada, one of Czechia's largest lakes, is home to a diverse range of animals: European catfish, greylag geese, and smooth snakes. But in September, recreational cyclists came across an unusual sight: a red crayfish marching on the path. While crayfish are not new to the country – signal and spiny-cheek crayfish have displaced native species over the years – this one was different. It was a red swamp crayfish, which is found in freshwater in about 20 European countries, but had never been spotted in Czechia before. Originally from North America, these crayfish are among the most invasive in Europe. For nature conservationist Lenka Čolobentičová and her colleagues at the country's Nature Conservation Agency, it was not good news. “They’re very aggressive; they fight a lot with other crayfish species, they carry the crayfish plague, and they reproduce quickly,” she told The European Correspondent. Though not confirmed, the agency believes it was likely released into Lake Milada by a hobbyist. Across Europe, invasive species are one of the five major causes of biodiversity loss. title: A Tool Built by Election Deniers Said These Voters Were Dead. We Found Them Alive.
content:
Ahead of the midterms, conservative election activists discussed plans to wield a powerful new weapon in the war against fraud: a data tool built by one of their own that could identify suspicious voters and help with contesting their ballots.

The system was put to the test this week in Forsyth County, Georgia, where a member of the county’s election board provided other officials with what he suggested was evidence of wrongdoing: four allegedly dead voters.

But it turns out all four are alive and well, ProPublica determined. The board rejected the attempt to challenge their ballots.

The effort, though, shows that even after last week’s blue wave, those who believe the 2020 election was stolen have continued to relentlessly search for ways to contest Republican losses. In Georgia, Democrats swept statewide offices.

title: Tavion toimintatapa hanketukipäätöksessä ei ole hyvää hallintoa – perustelemme näkemyksemme
content:
Hyvän hallinnon periaatteiden mukaista olisi ollut ilmoittaa jo hakuvaiheessa linjauksesta, jonka mukaan hanketukea ei myönnetä Somaliaan. Järjestöt olisivat olleet päätöksestä erimielisiä, mutta hakuprosessi olisi ollut yhdenvertainen.

Jaa

Pääministeri Petteri Orpo (kok.) linjasi tiistaina, että ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavion (ps.) päätös hanketuen epäämisestä Somaliassa toimivilta järjestöjen hankkeilta kuuluu ministerin toimivaltaan.

Fingo ei kiistä tätä. Tämä ei kuitenkaan poista sitä, että ministerin päätöksentekotapa ei ole ollut hyvän hallinnon mukaista. Perustelemme kantamme seuraavasti:

Orpon hallitus on ohjelmassaan linjannut, että kehitysyhteistyö ehdollistetaan omien kansalaisten vastaanottamiselle. Kirjauksen perusteella Suomi keskeytti Somalian maaohjelman kaksi vuotta sitten, mutta linjasi samalla, ettei keskeytys koske kansalaisjärjestöjä, humanitaarista apua tai yksityisen sektorin tukea.

Päätös oli perusteltu: kansalaisjärjestöt eivät tee päätöksiä kotimaidensa päättäjien puolesta. Tämän linjauksen myötä ulkoministeriö myönsi esimerkiksi vuosi sitten ohjelmatukea Somaliassa toteutettaville järjestöjen ja niiden kumppaneiden ohjelmille.

title: Geheimes Treffen zur EU-Methanverordnung: Mehr als ein Dutzend fossile Unternehmen auf Gästeliste
content:
Ende Juni trafen sich Öl- und Gaskonzerne mit deutschen Beamt*innen in der US-Botschaft in Berlin. Einen Tag später forderte Wirtschaftsministerin Reiche bei einem EU-Treffen genau das, was die fossile Industrie verlangte. Wir veröffentlichen weitere Details zur Lobbykampagne.

Dieses Treffen wäre geheim geblieben, wenn uns nicht ein Insider davon erzählt hätte. Ende Juni 2026 lud die US-Regierung Vertreter*innen der Öl- und Gasindustrie in ihre Botschaft in Berlin ein. Mit am Tisch saßen leitende Beamt*innen deutscher Ministerien, unter anderem aus dem Wirtschaftsministerium (BMWE). Das Thema: Die EU-Methanverordnung und warum diese laut den Energiekonzernen verschoben werden soll.

Das Treffen ist wichtig, denn nur einen Tag später sprach sich Wirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche (CDU) beim Rat der EU-Energieminister*innen für die Forderung der fossilen Lobby aus – entgegen der abgestimmten Position der Bundesregierung.
